The kind of a file is decided by what it does, not by who calls it ([.claude/rules/naming.md:9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L9)). A util read by only one folder still lives in `lib/utils/` ([.claude/rules/utils.md:11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/utils.md#L11)).

## What each kind owns and never does

The ownership table is the center of the design. Each row gives a part one job and names the one thing it must never do. The "never" column is what keeps parts from growing into each other.

| Part | Owns | Never does | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Collector | Gathers raw jobs and every field its source gives for free. Writes each into a `raw_` field exactly as it arrived. | Interpret anything. | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L33) |
| Normalizer | Reshapes raw data that is already there into the fields that matter. | Go looking. An empty `raw_` field stays empty. | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L34) |
| Resolver | Follows a job's link to the employer's own posting. | Read anything off the page it lands on. | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L35) |
| Parser | Makes the final attempt at filling `raw_` fields, including reading a salary out of the description. | Format what it extracts. | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L36) |
| Company association | Decides which employer a job belongs to, and creates one if none exists. | Invent a name from a board slug, or a slug from a name. | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L37) |
| Dedupe | Reduces the job list using identity tests that have all their fields on both sides. | Merge two jobs when no test has the fields it needs. | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:38](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L38) |
| Save | Creates, updates and deletes rows, and owns the merge rule every caller shares. | Decide which employer a job belongs to. | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L39) |
| Classification | Judgements about the job: is the location a match, has it expired. | Reshape a value or go looking for a missing one. | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:40](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L40) |
| Scoring | Alignment, employer scores, and promoting an employer to be watched directly. | Reach the database except through the services that own each table. | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L41) |
| Backlog cleanup | Expires a backlog job once it passes the age limit, and empties an employer's scores once they pass their own age limit, guessed scores sooner. | Delete a job or an employer. | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L42) |

### Reshaping versus going looking

The line between a normalizer and a parser is the most useful test in the design. Reshaping changes a value that is already there. Going looking produces a value that is not. If a field is empty and something has to find it, that is a parser's job, wherever it happens ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:48-50](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L48-L50)). This is why a parser hands its findings back to the normalizer instead of formatting them. See [Parsing](../pipeline/parsing.md) and [Normalization and Association](../pipeline/normalization-and-association.md).

### Seven jobs that exist exactly once

Seven jobs have one implementation each: removing duplicates, saving and updating, following a job's link to its source, tidying names, matching a location against the user's own, clearing out the backlog, and recording what happened ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:13-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L13-L17)). A second implementation is a defect, not a variation. The reason is practical. If dedupe existed twice, the two copies would drift, and one job could be a duplicate in one place and unique in another.

### Who sets a status

A step sets only the status that names its own outcome ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:44-46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L44-L46)).

| Step | Status it sets |
|---|---|
| Resolution | `unresolvable` |
| Parser | `unparseable`, or `expired` for a dead page |
| Classification | `too far`, or `expired` for an old posting |
| Backlog cleanup | `expired` |
| Promotion, and letting an added job through | `backlog` |
| A status change by hand | whatever the user chose |

The twelve valid statuses live in one list in code ([lib/utils/job-status.ts:24-37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L24-L37)). See [Data Model](../data/data-model.md) for what the statuses mean.

## The handler contract

A handler is the unit of work in the pipeline. The contract keeps every handler the same shape, so the orchestrator can call them all the same way.

| Rule | Plain meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Takes a list, acts on every entry, returns that list | Handlers work on whole lists, not single jobs | [.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L9) |
| The list comes back as `jobs` or `companies`, never both | One result carries one list, so a count is never ambiguous | [.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L11) |
| Runs once per position, never inside another handler's loop | Loops belong to the orchestrator | [.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L13) |
| Per-entry work lives in a helper | `normalizeJob` does one job. `normalizeJobs` is the handler. | [.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L15) |
| Reads no database beyond the trace service | Everything else arrives as an argument | [.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L17) |
| One handler serves every position it runs at | `dedupeJobs` runs three times with the same code | [.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L19) |

The orchestrator enforces the "jobs or companies" rule in the type system. A handler result is either `{ jobs }` or `{ companies }`, and the other name is typed as `never` so a result carrying both will not compile ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:58-67](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L58-L67)).

The naming is fixed too. A handler function is a verb and a plural noun, such as `normalizeJobs` or `saveJobs`. Its options and result types are `{Function}Options` and `{Function}Result`. Its parameters are the list, then an options object ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:23-27](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L23-L27)).

### Trace rows versus warnings

A handler can report two different things, and the contract keeps them apart ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:31-39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L31-L39)).

| Kind | Purpose | Where it goes | Who sees it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trace row | Analytics. Records that something happened. | Written straight to the database by the handler through the trace service | Nobody is told. It is read back later. |
| Warning | Validation. Something is wrong that the user must know. | Returned by the handler, passed up by the caller | The agent presents it to the user |

One event can be both. A salary that could not be read writes a trace row and returns a warning. A handler never returns trace events for its caller to write. See [Tracing and the Run Summary](./tracing-and-run-summary.md).

## Services and tools are handed in

Neither a handler nor an orchestrator builds its own database client or browser. The command script builds them and passes them down. This is called dependency injection: the caller hands in what the code needs.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Script as scripts/job-search.ts
    participant DB as createPipelineDb
    participant Svc as createXService(db)
    participant Orch as runJobSearch
    participant H as Handler
    participant Trace as TraceService

    Script->>DB: build one client
    DB-->>Script: PrismaClient
    Script->>Svc: build settings, trace, companies, atsSlugs, jobService, places
    Svc-->>Script: small objects of functions
    Script->>Orch: pass services, tools, runId, collectedAt
    Orch->>H: pass the list and an options object
    H->>Trace: write(event)
    H-->>Orch: list back, with warnings
```

<!-- Sources: scripts/job-search.ts:42-97, lib/db/pipeline-db.ts:14-18, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:95-149, lib/handlers/let-through.ts:68-103 -->

The script builds every service from the one client at the top of `main` ([scripts/job-search.ts:54-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L54-L70)). The orchestrator lists each of them as a required option and explains why. For example, `companies` is required so a caller cannot forget association and have the orchestrator silently skip it ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:98-101](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L98-L101)).

The orchestrator also reads no clock and mints no run id. Both arrive as arguments: `collectedAt` is "the instant every age in the run is measured against", and `runId` is "minted by the caller" ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:131-139](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L131-L139)). This makes the run repeatable in tests.

### Services

A service owns exactly one table or one row and reaches the database only through the client it is built from ([.claude/rules/services.md:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/services.md#L7)). The naming is fixed.

| Item | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| File | `lib/services/{subject}-service.ts` | `settings-service.ts` |
| Type | `{Subject}Service` | `SettingsService` |
| Builder | `create{Subject}Service(db)` | `createSettingsService(db)` |
| Shared stand-in | `fake{Subject}Service()` in `{subject}-service.fake.ts` | `fakeSettingsService()` |
| Row it reads back | `{Subject}Record` | `CompanyRecord` |

Source for the table: [.claude/rules/services.md:9-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/services.md#L9-L13). The full list of services is on [Services](../data/services.md).

### Tools

A tool wraps one thing outside the app, owns no table, and takes no job list ([.claude/rules/tools.md:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/tools.md#L7)). A tool that keeps something open between calls, such as a browser, is set up by a builder that starts with `create`, for example `createResolutionBrowser()`. A tool that makes one request per call exports plain functions ([.claude/rules/tools.md:10-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/tools.md#L10-L11)).

The orchestrator shows the pattern. It takes `openBrowser`, a factory, rather than a browser. It takes `parserFor` and `launchParsingBrowser` as optional "substitution points" so tests can run offline ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:114-124](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L114-L124)). The real script hands over `createResolutionBrowser` by name ([scripts/job-search.ts:87-90](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L87-L90)).

### Stand-ins instead of mocks

Every service and many tools have a shared stand-in, a `.fake.ts` file. The settings stand-in answers real seeded defaults instead of empty values, because "zero is not a blank for any of these settings" ([lib/services/settings-service.fake.ts:5-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.fake.ts#L5-L10)). The work-log stand-in sorts its list the way the real service does, so a page test cannot pass against an order the database never produces ([lib/services/work-log-service.fake.ts:30-35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.fake.ts#L30-L35)). See [Testing](../quality/testing.md).

## Direction of dependency

Plain functions sit at the bottom. A util "never imports from `lib/handlers/` or `lib/orchestrators/`, including imports that bring in only types" ([.claude/rules/utils.md:13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/utils.md#L13)). A test enforces it: `lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts` exists for this purpose (inferred: from its name, not read).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["util imports a handler?"] -->|yes| B["Defect:<br>move the code or the type"]
    A -->|no| C["Allowed"]
    D["Handler reads a table directly?"] -->|yes| E["Defect:<br>use a service"]
    D -->|no| F["Allowed"]
    G["Part branches on which<br>collector made a job?"] -->|yes| H["Defect:<br>push the difference<br>into the collector or parser"]
    G -->|no| I["Allowed"]

    style A fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style D fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style G fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style B fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style E fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style H fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style C fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style F fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style I fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```

<!-- Sources: .claude/rules/part-ownership.md:9-11, .claude/rules/part-ownership.md:52-54, .claude/rules/handler-contract.md:17 -->

## No part assumes it is inside a job search

The same saving code runs for a job search, for a status change made by hand, and for scoring. Nothing in a part depends on a run id, on being partway through a list, or on another part having run first. A caller hands down whatever a part needs, including which step name to record against ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:19-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L19-L23)).

The proof is in the code. `letJobsThrough` writes a trace row only when it is handed `trace`, `runId` and `step`. Without them "a step ... still does its work and stays silent", which "is what lets the same function run outside a job search" ([lib/handlers/let-through.ts:86-90](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L86-L90)).

Each stretch of the pipeline also ends at the database. A stretch writes its results and stops. The next stretch asks the database for the jobs carrying the right marker ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:25-27](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L25-L27)). The orchestrator's header says the same: "the database is the only handoff between steps" ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:5-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L5-L8)). The run is walked through step by step on [The Job Search Run](./job-search-run.md).

## Knowledge about a job site is data, never code

The project's working agreement says a rule may read a list of websites but may not contain one. Source-specific judgement lives in collectors and parsers and nowhere else (`CLAUDE.md`, "Working Agreements"). The code follows this by storing site knowledge in the database.

| Knowledge | Where it lives | Why it is data | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Which source wins a contested field | `Setting.source_priority_list`, one ordered list of `parser:{name}` and `collector:{name}` entries | The user reorders it by hand, and a seed never reorders it | [prisma/schema.prisma:301-309](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L301-L309) |
| Which query values identify a job | `Setting.identifying_query_values` | UltiPro keeps a job's only identity in a query value | [prisma/schema.prisma:310-315](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L310-L315) |
| Title vocabulary | `Setting.title_head_nouns`, `title_levels`, `title_suffixes`, `title_removal_words` | The lists grow from real titles, not from a list fitted in advance | [scripts/db-seed.ts:16-51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L16-L51) |
| Which boards an employer posts on | The `AtsSlug` table | Promotion fills a collector in later | [prisma/schema.prisma:212-218](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L212-L218) |
| Resolution pacing | `Setting.resolution_fast_concurrency` and two siblings | The setting names no host. Which host ends up slow is decided by how it behaved during the run. | [prisma/schema.prisma:316-322](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L316-L322) |

When a collector or parser is added or renamed, the seed must run in the same change. It appends the new name to the bottom of the priority list, because a source missing from the list "ranks below every source in it, so it loses every field two sources contest" ([.claude/rules/source-registry.md:7-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/source-registry.md#L7-L9)). See [Database Commands and Safety](../data/database-commands.md).

## Design decisions at a glance

| Decision | Reason | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Folders by kind, not by feature | A new rule has one obvious home | A feature touches several folders |
| Every step ends in a database write | A run that stops keeps its finished work | Each step re-reads its list from the database |
| Handlers take and return lists | The orchestrator treats all steps alike | A one-job tool must call the per-entry helper |
| Services and tools are passed in | Tests run offline against stand-ins | Option lists in the orchestrator are long |
| Site knowledge is data | A new site changes a row, not a rule | A seed must run when a source is added |

<doc title="The Job Search Run" path="./deep-dive/architecture/job-search-run.md">
# The Job Search Run

## Overview

`npm run job-search` is one command that runs the whole deterministic pipeline. "Deterministic" means no agent has to judge anything while it runs. Scoring, which does need an agent, runs afterward through its own commands (see [Scoring](../agent-workflows/scoring.md)).

The run has two layers. A thin script, `scripts/job-search.ts`, builds what the run shares and prints the result. An orchestrator, `runJobSearch`, decides which handlers run and in what order. This split is stated in the script's first lines: "Which steps run, and in what order, is the orchestrator's to know rather than this script's" ([scripts/job-search.ts:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L1-L3)).

The most important design choice is that every step ends in a database write. If a later step fails, the earlier steps have already saved their work. The orchestrator's header says so directly ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:1-16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L1-L16)).

| Component | Responsibility | Key file | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Script | Checks the database, builds services, mints the run id, prints results | `scripts/job-search.ts` | [scripts/job-search.ts:40-140](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L40-L140) |
| Orchestrator | Calls every handler in order and turns a throw into a report | `lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts` | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:151-667](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L151-L667) |
| Failure tracker | Names the spot a run stopped at and keeps the first failure | `lib/utils/run-failure.ts` | [lib/utils/run-failure.ts:18-39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-failure.ts#L18-L39) |
| Schema check | Refuses to start when the database does not match the code | `lib/db/schema-check.ts`, `lib/db/schema-drift.ts` | [lib/db/schema-drift.ts:17-28](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-drift.ts#L17-L28) |
| Let-through handler | Sends hand-added jobs on to scoring when the pipeline cannot judge them. Not used by this orchestrator. | `lib/handlers/let-through.ts` | [lib/handlers/let-through.ts:68-103](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L68-L103) |

## The command, step by step

The script runs these actions in order ([scripts/job-search.ts:40-137](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L40-L137)).

1. It reads the optional `--limit N` flag. A limit of 0 reaches no source at all, which is how the tests run the command without touching a job site ([scripts/job-search.ts:27-38](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L27-L38)).
2. It opens the database and runs the schema check. If the check fails, it sets the exit code to 1 and returns before anything else ([scripts/job-search.ts:49-52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L49-L52)).
3. It builds the services and the geocoder ([scripts/job-search.ts:54-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L54-L70)).
4. It mints a run id with `crypto.randomUUID()` and prints `Run: {run-id}` first. The scoring skill reads that line so it can file its own trace rows under the same run ([scripts/job-search.ts:73-76](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L73-L76)).
5. It reads the clock once into `collectedAt`, so every job in a run shares one timestamp even when collection takes minutes ([scripts/job-search.ts:77-79](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L77-L79)).
6. It calls `runJobSearch` ([scripts/job-search.ts:81-97](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L81-L97)).
7. It prints errors, warnings, the failure if there is one, the trace failure count, and the summary ([scripts/job-search.ts:99-130](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L99-L130)).
8. It sets the exit code to 1 if the run failed, and always disconnects from the database ([scripts/job-search.ts:132-139](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L132-L139)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User
    participant Script as scripts/job-search.ts
    participant Check as schemaHasDrifted
    participant Orch as runJobSearch
    participant Trace as TraceService
    participant DB as pipeline.db

    User->>Script: npm run job-search
    Script->>Check: probe every table
    Check->>DB: findFirst on each model
    DB-->>Check: ok or error per table
    alt any table unreadable
        Check-->>Script: true, prints migrate hint
        Script-->>User: exit code 1
    else all tables readable
        Check-->>Script: false
        Script->>Script: build services, mint run id
        Script-->>User: Run: {run-id}
        Script->>Orch: runJobSearch with services and runId
        Orch->>DB: handlers write as they go
        Orch-->>Script: report with failure or null
        Script->>Trace: countsForRun(runId)
        Trace->>DB: group trace rows
        Script-->>User: errors, warnings, summary
    end
```

<!-- Sources: scripts/job-search.ts:49-52, scripts/job-search.ts:73-76, scripts/job-search.ts:81-97, scripts/job-search.ts:123-130, lib/db/schema-drift.ts:17-28, lib/db/schema-check.ts:37-47 -->

### Why the schema check comes first

The check exists because of a real failure. A column was added to the schema but never pushed to the live database. Every trace write of that run failed, the trace service swallowed each one, and the whole run's history was lost without a word ([lib/db/schema-check.ts:1-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-check.ts#L1-L11)).

The check does not compare column lists. It reads one row from each table. Prisma names every column it knows in the SELECT it builds, so a read that succeeds proves the database holds them all. Nothing in the check has to be kept in step with the schema by hand ([lib/db/schema-check.ts:7-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-check.ts#L7-L11)). A test reads the list of checked models against `schema.prisma`, so the list cannot go stale unnoticed ([lib/db/schema-check.ts:21-33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-check.ts#L21-L33)).

Every probe runs, even after a failure, so one trip through the rebuild loop fixes every table ([lib/db/schema-check.ts:49-63](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-check.ts#L49-L63)). On failure the user sees three lines: the mismatch, the tables that could not be read, and `Migrate it with: npm run db:migrate` ([lib/db/schema-drift.ts:24-26](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-drift.ts#L24-L26)). More on this on [Database Commands and Safety](../data/database-commands.md).

## The pipeline order

The orchestrator runs three stretches after an opening cleanup. Each stretch ends with a save. The table lists every handler call. The "Handler label" is the name the orchestrator records in its finished list. The "Trace step" is the step name written on trace rows.

| # | Handler label | Handler | Trace step | Source |

<!-- Sources: lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:192-216, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:222-272, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:276-361, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:369-457, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:464-551, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:558-637 -->

## Each stretch in detail

### Settings read once

Before any handler runs, the orchestrator reads the settings the whole run shares. It reads the expiry threshold, the two score-expiry limits, the source priority list and the identifying query values ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:188-216](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L188-L216)). The reason is consistency. Backlog cleanup, promotion and classification all judge age. A run where they disagreed about what counts as expired would contradict itself ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:189-191](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L189-L191)).

A missing setting throws, because the settings service throws on a missing value. The title vocabularies are read after collection but before the handlers that use them, "deliberately", so a missing vocabulary stops the whole run instead of looking like one handler failing ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:294-302](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L294-L302)).

### Backlog cleanup opens the run

Cleanup runs first so the backlog that collection is about to add to has already been swept ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:218-221](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L218-L221)). It has a job half and a company half. The company half empties stale employer scores, and the orchestrator copies the two counts into the report ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:249-250](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L249-L250)).

### The collect stretch

Collection takes no list. It builds the first one from the collectors and returns jobs, errors and warnings ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:276-292](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L276-L292)). The orchestrator then runs normalization, association, dedupe and save over the same list. See [Collection](../pipeline/collection.md), [Normalization and Association](../pipeline/normalization-and-association.md) and [Dedupe and Save](../pipeline/dedupe-and-save.md).

### The resolution stretch

This stretch takes nothing from the collect stretch. It asks the database for every job still needing a source link, whenever it was collected. That means it also picks up jobs from earlier runs ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:364-369](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L364-L369)).

If the list is empty, no browser is launched. A headed browser holds the machine for as long as it runs, so an empty list must never reach the launch ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:371-373](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L371-L373)). The three pacing settings are read before the browser opens, so a missing setting costs no browser ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:374-386](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L374-L386)).

The browser is closed in a `finally` block under its own name, `browser_close`. A browser that will not shut is then reported as that, not as whatever ran before it ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:451-456](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L451-L456)). After the save, the resolved list is merged into the report by job id. The later version wins because its fields are newer. A job without an id is appended, because two jobs without ids are two jobs ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:436-450](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L436-L450)). See [Resolution](../pipeline/resolution.md).

### The parsing stretch

Parsing also reads its own list: jobs already resolved but not yet parsed ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:459-464](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L459-L464)). It has no length check, because "five handlers over an empty list cost nothing". It opens a browser lazily, only on the first page a parser asks to be rendered, and reuses that session. The browser closes in a `finally`, but only if one was opened ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:466-501](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L466-L501)).

Normalization runs before association here. Association matches on the cleaned company name, and normalization is what cleans it. Running association first would split one employer across two company rows ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:504-506](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L504-L506)). See [Parsing](../pipeline/parsing.md).

### The home point, promotion and classification

Before promotion, the orchestrator settles the point every job is measured against. It reads the location and radius settings, looks the location text up in the place table, and only asks the map service when the table has never seen it ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:553-575](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L553-L575)). If the location cannot be placed, the run stops, "because measuring against nothing would mark every job as not matching" ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:555-557](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L555-L557)). This happens after parsing has been saved, so parsing's work survives.

Promotion runs near the end, not at the start. An expired job only earns a fresh date once collection has found the new listing and dedupe has merged it in ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:579-581](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L579-L581)). Classification reads its list after promotion's save, so jobs returned to the backlog are judged by this run ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:606-610](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L606-L610)). See [Judging Steps](../pipeline/judging-steps.md).

## Failure handling

A throw anywhere in the chain stops the run where it happened. It does not escape to the caller. One `try` and one empty `catch` wrap the body ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:188-658](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L188-L658)). The catch is empty on purpose. It has nothing to read off the throw, because the failure tracker already named the spot and wrote the reason on the way past ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:653-657](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L653-L657)).

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Running
    Running --> Running: step finishes, handler listed
    Running --> Failed: a step throws inside at()
    Failed --> Failed: later cleanup throws, ignored
    Running --> Finished: classification save done
    Finished --> [*]: failure is null
    Failed --> [*]: failure holds first spot and reason

    note right of Failed
        The tracker keeps only the first failure.
        Work already written stays in the database.
    end note
```

<!-- Sources: lib/utils/run-failure.ts:18-39, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:163-186, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:653-666 -->

### The failure tracker

Every lookup and handler call goes through a wrapper named `at(spot, run)`. If `run` throws, `at` records the spot and the reason, then re-throws ([lib/utils/run-failure.ts:23-33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-failure.ts#L23-L33)). The tracker keeps only the first failure it sees, using `failure ??= ...` ([lib/utils/run-failure.ts:30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-failure.ts#L30)).

This is a bug fix recorded in the file's header. Three runners had each kept their own copy, and two of them overwrote the first failure with the last one. Cleanup runs after the thing it cleans up after. A browser that will not shut throws second and would bury the reason the run actually stopped ([lib/utils/run-failure.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-failure.ts#L1-L6)).

The spot name is passed in as text, not tracked in a variable. A handler added later cannot be reported under the last handler's name ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:163-168](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L163-L168)).

### What the report holds

| Field | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `jobs` | Every job the run acted on, joined across stretches | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:74](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L74) |
| `companyScoresCleared`, `companyGuessesCleared` | How many companies lost all four scores, and how many lost only guessed ones | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:75-78](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L75-L78) |
| `errors`, `warnings` | Collection issues the user needs to see | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:79-80](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L79-L80) |
| `handlers` | One entry per handler that finished, in order. A handler that threw has no entry. | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:81-84](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L81-L84) |
| `failure` | Where the run stopped and why, or `null`. Always present. | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:85-88](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L85-L88) |
| `traceFailures` | How many trace writes the run lost. Always present, `0` when nothing failed. | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:89-92](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L89-L92) |

### What a stopped run keeps

| Stopped at | Already in the database | Not done |
|---|---|---|
| A settings read | Nothing from this run | Everything |
| Collection | The backlog cleanup writes | Normalization onward |
| Resolution | Collect stretch saved | Dedupe, save and parsing for resolution |
| Home location | Parse stretch saved | Promotion and classification |
| Classification | Everything up to promotion's save | Classification save |

This table is inferred from the order of writes in the code, not from a test. The statement it rests on is in the header: "Every step has already written to the database by the time a later one can fail" ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:13-16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L13-L16)).

### What the script prints on failure

When `report.failure` is set, the script prints `Run stopped at {spot}: {reason}`, then `Finished before it stopped:` and one line per finished handler with its entry count. This list is printed only on failure, because a clean run has no question to answer about which steps got that far ([scripts/job-search.ts:102-111](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L102-L111)). The summary still prints afterward, because the trace rows are already written. The block the run died in is marked `stopped early` ([scripts/job-search.ts:123-130](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L123-L130)). See [Tracing and the Run Summary](./tracing-and-run-summary.md).

### Lost trace rows

A trace write that fails is counted and never thrown. The trace service increments a counter and carries on ([lib/services/trace-service.ts:136-143](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L136-L143)). The orchestrator reads that count once the run is over, whether it finished or stopped, and puts it in the report ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:660-663](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L660-L663)). The script prints `Trace failures: {n}` when it is above zero ([scripts/job-search.ts:113-115](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L113-L115)).

## The let-through handler

`lib/handlers/let-through.ts` is not part of the job search. The add-external-jobs orchestrator calls it at two positions ([lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts:217-218](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L217-L218), [lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts:243-244](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L243-L244)). A hand-added job often cannot be judged. It has no listing page to resolve and no location text to check. Without a rule, such a job would stay stuck, so the handler lets it through to scoring and records why ([lib/handlers/let-through.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L1-L5)).

| Position (`after`) | Condition | What changes | Trace reason | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `parsing` | Job status is `unparseable` | Status becomes `backlog`, and `is_resolved`, `is_parsed`, `is_classified` become true | `no_location` | [lib/handlers/let-through.ts:38-47](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L38-L47) |
| `classification` | Still in the backlog and `is_classified` is not true | `is_classified` becomes true. The job stays in the backlog. | `location_unusable` | [lib/handlers/let-through.ts:51-61](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L51-L61) |

It writes the event `job_let_through` ([lib/handlers/let-through.ts:21](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L21)). It returns a copy of each job and never changes the one handed in ([lib/handlers/let-through.ts:32-33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L32-L33)). A job without an id or a collector is let through silently, because a trace row is keyed by both ([lib/handlers/let-through.ts:82-84](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L82-L84)). The two trace step names, `post_parsing_let_through` and `post_classification_let_through`, are documented in the Trace model comment ([prisma/schema.prisma:372-378](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L372-L378)). See [External Jobs and Resumes](../agent-workflows/external-jobs-and-resumes.md).

## Contradictions found

| Source | Says | Code says |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/architecture.md`, "The collection step" | Seven collectors produce the job list | The collector registry lists 14 collectors ([lib/collectors/registry.ts:19-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/registry.ts#L19-L34)) |
| `docs/architecture.md`, "The parsing step" | Four parsers exist, and a job whose domain none owns is set aside as `unparseable` | The parser registry maps 11 owned domains to dedicated parsers ([lib/parsers/registry.ts:37-49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/registry.ts#L37-L49)), and any other web link goes to the general parser ([lib/parsers/registry.ts:72-75](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/registry.ts#L72-L75)). See [Parsing](../pipeline/parsing.md). |
| `lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:47-51` | `FinishedHandler.step` is the `Trace.step` name | For the two company cleanup handlers the label differs from the trace step |

<doc title="Tracing and the Run Summary" path="./deep-dive/architecture/tracing-and-run-summary.md">
# Tracing and the Run Summary

## Overview

A job search touches hundreds of jobs. A returned list can say how many jobs came out the end. It cannot say how many came from one collector, or why 40 jobs were dropped. Those numbers exist only if each step writes down what it did while it did it.

The Trace table holds those records. It has one row per event in a job's path through the pipeline. A job "enters at collection, passes through each step, and either reaches the end or hits a dead end recording when and why" ([prisma/schema.prisma:357-359](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L357-L359)). The summary printed at the end of a run is rebuilt from these rows, not from what the run returned.

| Component | Responsibility | Key file | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Trace` model | One row per event, with step, event, reason, collector and domain | `prisma/schema.prisma` | [prisma/schema.prisma:618-650](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L618-L650) |
| Trace service | Writes every row, counts rows by group, reads a job's rows back | `lib/services/trace-service.ts` | [lib/services/trace-service.ts:115-194](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L115-L194) |
| Detail cut | Limits a row's detail text to 200 characters | `lib/utils/trace-detail.ts` | [lib/utils/trace-detail.ts:9-15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/trace-detail.ts#L9-L15) |
| Summary builder | Turns counted groups into the lines the command prints | `lib/utils/run-summary.ts` | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:150-417](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L150-L417) |
| Summary rule | What the summary must look like | `.claude/rules/run-summary.md` | [.claude/rules/run-summary.md:5-90](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L5-L90) |
| Proof test | Runs a real job search and reads rows back with raw SQL | `lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts` | [lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts#L1-L5) |

## The shape of a trace row

Each row answers five questions. Which run? Which job or company? Where in the pipeline? What happened? Why?

| Column | Meaning | Nullable | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | Auto-increment integer, so two events in the same millisecond keep a reliable order | no | [prisma/schema.prisma:619-621](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L619-L621) |
| `run_id` | The job search during which the event happened | no | [prisma/schema.prisma:622-623](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L622-L623) |
| `job_id` | The job described. A plain column with no relation, so a trace outlives its job. Empty on a company event. | yes | [prisma/schema.prisma:624-627](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L624-L627) |
| `company_id` | The company described, on company events. A row names a job or a company, never both. | yes | [prisma/schema.prisma:628-631](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L628-L631) |
| `step` | Where in the pipeline the event happened | no | [prisma/schema.prisma:632-633](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L632-L633) |
| `event` | What happened | no | [prisma/schema.prisma:634-635](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L634-L635) |
| `reason` | Why a dead end happened, where the event was one | yes | [prisma/schema.prisma:636-637](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L636-L637) |
| `collector` | Which collector produced the job. Empty on a company event. | yes | [prisma/schema.prisma:638-640](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L638-L640) |
| `domain` | The domain a failing source owns. A column of its own so it can be grouped. | yes | [prisma/schema.prisma:641-646](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L641-L646) |
| `detail` | JSON specific to one event. "Nothing that gets counted goes here." | yes | [prisma/schema.prisma:647-648](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L647-L648) |
| `created_at` | When the row was written | no | [prisma/schema.prisma:649](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L649) |

The split between `reason`/`domain` and `detail` is the key design choice. `detail` is JSON with a different shape per event, and SQLite cannot group a web address out of it. A counted value must be groupable, so it gets its own column ([prisma/schema.prisma:641-646](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L641-L646)).

### Types that stop a row naming both a job and a company

The trace service uses TypeScript types to enforce the "never both" rule. A job event requires `job_id` and `collector` and types `company_id` as `never`. A company event requires `company_id` and types `job_id` and `collector` as `never`. Spelling both as `never` is "what makes a row carrying a job and a company fail to compile" ([lib/services/trace-service.ts:63-74](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L63-L74)).

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class TraceEventBase {
        +string run_id
        +string step
        +string event
        +string reason
        +string domain
        +TraceDetail detail
    }
    class JobTraceEvent {
        +string job_id
        +string collector
        +never company_id
    }
    class CompanyTraceEvent {
        +string company_id
        +never job_id
        +never collector
    }
    class TraceDetail {
        <<union>>
        string
        from and to pair
        DedupeTraceDetail
        DeleteRefusedDetail
    }
    TraceEventBase <|-- JobTraceEvent
    TraceEventBase <|-- CompanyTraceEvent
    TraceEventBase --> TraceDetail

    style TraceEventBase fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style JobTraceEvent fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style CompanyTraceEvent fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style TraceDetail fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/services/trace-service.ts:33-74 -->

The detail union has four shapes ([lib/services/trace-service.ts:37-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L37-L41)).

| Shape | Written by | Holds | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain string | Most events | A dead end names the offending value | [lib/services/trace-service.ts:33-36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L33-L36) |
| `{ from, to }` | Normalization | The value before and after | [lib/services/trace-service.ts:39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L39) |
| `DedupeTraceDetail` | Dedupe, when a job merges away | The id it became, the clause that matched, and enough of the losing side to check the merge | [lib/services/trace-service.ts:16-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L16-L23) |
| `DeleteRefusedDetail` | Save, when the active-status guardrail refuses a delete | The row that blocked it and its status | [lib/services/trace-service.ts:28-31](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L28-L31) |

Normalization detail is cut to 200 characters. The longest real title measured is 131 characters and the longest real company name is 50, so 200 fits every real value and still cuts a description a bug put in the wrong field ([lib/utils/trace-detail.ts:1-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/trace-detail.ts#L1-L9)). The front of the value survives, because that identifies the row ([lib/utils/trace-detail.ts:11-15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/trace-detail.ts#L11-L15)).

## The vocabularies

The Trace model's comment is the vocabulary. Handler rules say a step name "is one of the values listed in the `Trace` model's comment" ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L41)). A test in `prisma/schema.test.ts` checks the dedupe reasons against the schema comment so the two cannot drift ([lib/types/job-list-entry.ts:32-35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/types/job-list-entry.ts#L32-L35)).

### Steps

Steps are listed in pipeline order. The comment states "Every one of them writes today" ([prisma/schema.prisma:363-370](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L363-L370)).

| Group | Steps | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Cleanup | `backlog_cleanup`, `post_backlog_cleanup_save` | [prisma/schema.prisma:363-364](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L363-L364) |
| Collect stretch | `collection`, `post_collection_normalization`, `post_collection_association`, `post_collection_dedupe`, `post_collection_save` | [prisma/schema.prisma:364-366](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L364-L366) |
| Resolve stretch | `resolution`, `post_resolution_dedupe`, `post_resolution_save` | [prisma/schema.prisma:366-367](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L366-L367) |
| Parse stretch | `parsing`, `post_parsing_normalization`, `post_parsing_association`, `post_parsing_dedupe`, `post_parsing_save` | [prisma/schema.prisma:367-368](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L367-L368) |
| Judging | `promotion`, `post_promotion_save`, `classification`, `post_classification_save` | [prisma/schema.prisma:368-369](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L368-L369) |
| Written by scoring commands | `scoring`, `company_promotion` | [prisma/schema.prisma:369](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L369) |
| Written only by adding jobs by hand | `post_parsing_let_through`, `post_classification_let_through` | [prisma/schema.prisma:372-378](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L372-L378) |

### Events

Every event about a job carries the `job_` prefix, so the subject of a row reads off its event name alone ([prisma/schema.prisma:390-391](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L390-L391)). Company events use `company_` names. The table lists the main events by step.

| Step | Events | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Collection | `job_collected`, `job_abandoned`, `job_resolved` (for a job a collector resolved itself) | [prisma/schema.prisma:391-392](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L391-L392) |
| Normalization | `job_updated`, `normalization_failed` | [prisma/schema.prisma:393-394](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L393-L394) |
| Association | `company_associated`, `company_dbrow_updated`, `association_failed`, `company_update_failed` | [prisma/schema.prisma:395-398](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L395-L398) |
| Save | `job_dbrow_created`, `job_dbrow_updated`, `job_dbrow_status_updated`, `job_dbrow_deleted`, `job_dbrow_delete_refused` | [prisma/schema.prisma:399-408](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L399-L408) |
| Dedupe | `job_abandoned`, `job_added_to_list` | [prisma/schema.prisma:409-413](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L409-L413) |
| Resolution | `job_resolved`, `resolution_failed` | [prisma/schema.prisma:414-415](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L414-L415) |
| Parsing | `job_parsed`, `parsing_failed` | [prisma/schema.prisma:420-424](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L420-L424) |
| Judging | `job_entered`, `job_kept`, `job_expired`, `job_promoted`, `job_reposted`, `job_classified`, `classification_failed` | [prisma/schema.prisma:429-440](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L429-L440) |
| Scoring | `job_scored`, `scoring_failed`, `company_scored`, `company_partially_scored`, `company_scoring_failed` | [prisma/schema.prisma:588-603](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L588-L603) |
| Company promotion | `company_entered`, `company_promoted`, `company_promotion_skipped` | [prisma/schema.prisma:608-612](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L608-L612) |

`job_abandoned` ends a job's path. It makes no claim about whether a row existed. What became of the row is a separate event: `job_dbrow_deleted` if save carried out the delete, or `job_dbrow_delete_refused` if the active-status guardrail kept it ([prisma/schema.prisma:442-447](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L442-L447)).

### Reasons

A reason names why a dead end happened ([prisma/schema.prisma:449-450](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L449-L450)). One rule governs all of them: a reason string is never shared by two different populations, with a narrow exception. A step and an event may share a word where they describe one population split by where it happened. Examples are `location_unusable` (written by normalization and classification) and `past_expiration_threshold` (written by every expiry) ([prisma/schema.prisma:469-472](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L469-L472), [prisma/schema.prisma:562-573](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L562-L573)).

| Step | Reasons | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Collection | Six usability codes: `no_original_url`, `original_url_not_a_url`, `no_raw_title`, `no_company_identity`, `posting_date_unparseable`, `posting_updated_date_unparseable` | [prisma/schema.prisma:452-457](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L452-L457) |
| Normalization | Nine, such as `title_normalized`, `missing_role_noun`, `salary_unusable`, `work_mode_unusable`, plus `location_unusable` | [prisma/schema.prisma:459-472](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L459-L472) |
| Association | `matched_by_slug`, `matched_by_name`, `company_created`, `company_name_filled`, `no_company_name`, `company_name_clash` | [prisma/schema.prisma:474-485](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L474-L485) |
| Dedupe | `hard_match_in_list`, `repost_match_in_list`, `matched_db_row`, `matched_list_entry` | [prisma/schema.prisma:494-502](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L494-L502) |
| Resolution | Ten, such as `link_left_site`, `stayed_on_site`, `page_refused`, `page_unavailable`, `dead_end`, `blacklisted_url` | [prisma/schema.prisma:509-529](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L509-L529) |
| Parsing | `dead_page`, `no_location` | [prisma/schema.prisma:548-557](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L548-L557) |
| Judging | `past_expiration_threshold`, `no_location_match`, `location_unusable` | [prisma/schema.prisma:562-573](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L562-L573) |

Only some reasons warn the user. The comment names them: `salary_unusable`, `work_mode_unusable`, `no_company_name` and `company_name_clash` ([prisma/schema.prisma:467-469](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L467-L469), [prisma/schema.prisma:485](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L485)). The rest are analytics only. Each warning is also a trace row, which follows the "one event produces both" rule from [System Design](./system-design.md#trace-rows-versus-warnings).

## Why there is no run table

A run is identified by the id written on every event it produces. A table holding one row per run "earns nothing" ([docs/architecture.md:298](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L298)). The same row of that document also rules out shipped macro queries. The funnel questions are answered by SQL written where it is asked, in a test file or at the command line, so no query code lives in `lib/` ([docs/architecture.md:298](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L298)).

The proof test shows this in action. It runs two real runs against one scratch database and answers funnel questions with raw SQL grouped by `run_id` and `collector` ([lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts:227-260](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts#L227-L260), [lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts:276-310](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts#L276-L310)).

A second consequence follows. Scoring runs in a different process from the job search, yet its rows belong to the same run. The job search prints `Run: {run-id}` first so the scoring skill can read that line and "file its own trace rows under the same run" ([scripts/job-search.ts:73-76](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L73-L76)). One run's rows stay countable together without any run record.

## How a row is written

Handlers write their own trace rows. The caller hands a handler the trace service, the run id and the step name, because the same handler runs at more than one position ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L37)). A handler handed none of them writes no trace and still does its work.

The write never throws. The trace service wraps the create in a `try` and counts the failure ([lib/services/trace-service.ts:119-144](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L119-L144)). The comment gives the reason: this runs inside the collection step's per-collector block, where a throw reads as a collector failure and costs every remaining job from that source. "Losing a trace row is better than losing the rest of the run" ([lib/services/trace-service.ts:137-143](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L137-L143)).

`countsForRun` is the opposite. A throw there "is left to travel", because a summary that silently read back nothing would tell the user the run did nothing, "which is worse than an error reaching them instead" ([lib/services/trace-service.ts:150-153](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L150-L153)).

The work-log service takes the opposite choice from the trace service for the same reason. A work log row is a legal filing that cannot be regenerated, so its write has no `try` ([lib/services/work-log-service.ts:45-52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.ts#L45-L52)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant H as Handler
    participant TS as TraceService
    participant DB as Trace table
    participant Script as scripts/job-search.ts
    participant Sum as summaryFromTraceCounts

    H->>TS: write(event with run_id, step, event, reason)
    TS->>DB: trace.create
    alt write fails
        TS->>TS: failures += 1, nothing thrown
    else write succeeds
        DB-->>TS: row stored
    end
    Note over H,DB: run continues, many rows written
    Script->>TS: countsForRun(runId)
    TS->>DB: groupBy step, event, reason, collector, domain
    DB-->>TS: groups with counts
    TS-->>Script: TraceRunCount list
    Script->>Sum: counts, collector names, stoppedAt
    Sum-->>Script: lines to print
```

<!-- Sources: lib/services/trace-service.ts:119-170, scripts/job-search.ts:123-130, lib/utils/run-summary.ts:150-157 -->

## Rebuilding the summary

The summary is built by one function, `summaryFromTraceCounts(counts, collectors, stoppedAt)`. Its header explains the design. The value `runJobSearch` returns carries list lengths only. It cannot say how many jobs came from one collector or how many duplicates were reposts. Every number broken out by collector or reason "exists only in the trace rows" ([lib/utils/run-summary.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L1-L6)).

### The count helper

`countsForRun` groups rows by five columns and returns one count per group ([lib/services/trace-service.ts:154-158](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L154-L158)). Every number in the summary is the same question asked with different values: how many rows match this step, event and reason. A single helper, `total`, answers it by adding the counts of matching groups ([lib/utils/run-summary.ts:9-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L9-L14)).

### The block layout

The three judging steps and the scoring steps print one shape. The shape is written once in `stepBlock` ([lib/utils/run-summary.ts:85-148](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L85-L148)).

| Part | How it is built | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Heading | The step name and the number of entries, from the `{subject}_entered` rows | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:110-120](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L110-L120) |
| Stopped marker | ` — stopped early` is added when the step is where the run stopped | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:116-119](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L116-L119) |
| Outcome lines | One per way a job left, right-aligned to the heading's width. A zero earns no line. | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:122-138](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L122-L138) |
| Notes | After a blank line, prefixed `Note:`. A note is true of the jobs but is not a way out. | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:140-145](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L140-L145) |

The width is taken from the heading's own count, not shared across steps, "because the lines beneath a heading are read as summing to it and to nothing else" ([lib/utils/run-summary.ts:95-97](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L95-L97)).

An example from the rule file shows the output ([.claude/rules/run-summary.md:47-55](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L47-L55)).

```
Classification (157 jobs)
   32 jobs expired (reason: past_expiration_threshold)
   64 jobs were close enough
   48 jobs too far (reason: no_location_match)
   13 jobs could not be judged (reason: location_unusable)

  Note: 12 of these were also flagged as reposts
```

### What the summary prints

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    A["Backlog cleanup block<br>kept, expired, company notes"] --> B["Collected: N jobs<br>one line per collector"]
    B --> C{"Any duplicates found<br>in the collect stretch?"}
    C -->|yes| D["Dedupe post collection<br>in list, already saved"]
    C -->|no| E
    D --> E["Resolved: N jobs<br>could not be resolved"]
    E --> F["Parsed: N jobs<br>could not be parsed<br>top five failing domains"]
    F --> G["Promotion block<br>note: came from backlog"]
    G --> H["Classification block<br>note: reposts"]
    H --> I["Alignment scoring block"]
    I --> J["Company scoring block<br>note: added to polling list"]

    style A fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style B fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style C fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style D fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style E fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style F fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style G fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style H fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style I fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/utils/run-summary.ts:186-200, lib/utils/run-summary.ts:205-218, lib/utils/run-summary.ts:257-269, lib/utils/run-summary.ts:274-301, lib/utils/run-summary.ts:312-324, lib/utils/run-summary.ts:333-352, lib/utils/run-summary.ts:356-414 -->

| Block | What it counts | Notable detail | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backlog cleanup | `job_kept` and `job_expired` | Notes for companies that lost a stale score or a stale guessed score. The event separates the two, because both carry the same reason. | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:164-198](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L164-L198) |
| Collected | `job_collected` rows | Every collector gets a line, even at zero. A collector that collected nothing writes no row, so omitting it would read as "we did not run it". | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:202-219](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L202-L219) |
| Dedupe | `job_abandoned` rows at `post_collection_dedupe` | Prints only if there is something to say. A heading over nothing "only asks the reader what happened". | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:237-269](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L237-L269) |
| Resolved | `job_resolved` at the `resolution` step only | The step filter matters. Collection writes `job_resolved` too, and counting those would credit resolution with work it never did. | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:271-282](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L271-L282) |
| Parsed | `job_parsed`, `parsing_failed` | Lists the top five failing domains, highest cost first, ties by name. The label is `no parser` or `parser failed`. | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:285-301](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L285-L301), [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:52-83](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L52-L83) |
| Promotion | `job_promoted` | A note says these came from the backlog, not from this run's collection | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:306-324](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L306-L324) |
| Classification | `job_classified`, `job_expired`, two `classification_failed` reasons | A repost count is a note, never a line | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:326-352](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L326-L352) |
| Alignment scoring and company scoring | The `scoring` step, split by subject | Read the same step. The subject, `job` or `company`, tells the two apart. | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:354-414](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L354-L414) |

Two small rules show attention to the reader. Counts use the right singular or plural word, even for one: `1 job`, `2 jobs`, and zero keeps the plural ([lib/utils/run-summary.ts:16-24](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L16-L24)). The sort of failing domains breaks ties by name "so the list is stable between runs" ([lib/utils/run-summary.ts:74-78](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L74-L78)).

## The summary rules

`.claude/rules/run-summary.md` governs this file. The table lists each rule and whether the code follows it.

| Rule | Plain meaning | Followed in code? | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Every step prints | A step with no work shows its heading and its zero | Yes for the `stepBlock` steps. The heading prints at zero. | [.claude/rules/run-summary.md:7-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L7-L13), [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:125-131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L125-L131) |
| A heading carries what entered | The number is the jobs handed to the step | Yes for `stepBlock` steps | [.claude/rules/run-summary.md:15-19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L15-L19) |
| The lines account for every job | Each job leaves by exactly one line, and lines sum to the heading | By design in `stepBlock`. Not checked by code here. | [.claude/rules/run-summary.md:21-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L21-L23) |
| A reason names why a job left the happy path | The text is the value written to `Trace.reason` | Yes | [.claude/rules/run-summary.md:32-36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L32-L36), [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:136](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L136) |
| A note is not a path | Notes sit after a blank line and never count toward the heading | Yes | [.claude/rules/run-summary.md:43-45](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L43-L45), [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:143-145](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L143-L145) |
| A step the run died inside says so | ` — stopped early` on the heading | Yes | [.claude/rules/run-summary.md:80-86](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L80-L86), [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:119](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L119) |
| The numbers come from trace rows | Never from what a handler returned | Yes | [.claude/rules/run-summary.md:88-90](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L88-L90), [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L1-L6) |

### Where the code differs from the rule file

The rule file and the code do not fully agree. These are observations from reading both.

| Rule says | Code does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Collection's heading carries the sources it ran, for example `Collection (7 sources)`, with each source nested below | Prints `Collected: N jobs` and a `  - {collector} collected N jobs` line per collector. There is no `Collection` heading with a source count. | [.claude/rules/run-summary.md:73-78](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L73-L78), [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:205-219](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L205-L219) |
| Every step prints, even at zero | The Dedupe block prints only when a count is above zero. `Resolved:` and `Parsed:` print as one headline line with no entered count, not as blocks with a heading. | [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:255-269](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L255-L269), [lib/utils/run-summary.ts:274-301](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L274-L301) |
| Sub-steps nest | Only the per-collector lines and the failing-domain lines nest | [.claude/rules/run-summary.md:68-78](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L68-L78) |

The rule file reads as the target shape. The deterministic steps from collection through parsing do not yet follow the block shape that backlog cleanup, promotion, classification and scoring do (inferred from comparing the two files, not stated in either).

## A schema comment that is out of date

A job search, scoring's two commands and adding jobs by hand all write trace rows ([prisma/schema.prisma:360-361](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L360-L361)). Scoring and company promotion are the two steps the pipeline itself never reaches ([prisma/schema.prisma:380-383](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L380-L383)), and adding jobs by hand writes two steps a job search never reaches ([prisma/schema.prisma:372-378](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L372-L378)). The add-external-jobs runner also reads a job's rows back through the trace service, using `rowsForJobs`, and asks for the narrower `TraceService & TraceJobRowsReader` type ([lib/services/trace-service.ts:100-105](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L100-L105), [lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts:66](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L66)).
