<doc title="Data Model" path="./deep-dive/data/data-model.md">
# Data Model

## Overview

All state lives in one SQLite database, described by one file: `prisma/schema.prisma`. Seven models make up the whole pipeline. Because every step ends in a database write, this schema is also the hand-off between steps. A job's flags and status say which step should pick it up next.

Two design habits show up across all seven tables. First, a collected value and a cleaned value live in separate columns, so a later step can tell what still needs doing. Second, some tables are deliberately not linked to others, so a record can outlive the thing it describes.

| Model | What a row is | Related to | Key file | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Job` | One job posting | Belongs to a `Company` | `prisma/schema.prisma` | [prisma/schema.prisma:14-142](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L14-L142) |
| `Company` | One employer and what an agent researched about it | Has many `Job` and `AtsSlug` rows | `prisma/schema.prisma` | [prisma/schema.prisma:147-210](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L147-L210) |
| `AtsSlug` | One hiring-system board we know about | Belongs to a `Company` | `prisma/schema.prisma` | [prisma/schema.prisma:219-241](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L219-L241) |
| `Place` | One looked-up place on the map | None | `prisma/schema.prisma` | [prisma/schema.prisma:251-270](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L251-L270) |
| `Setting` | The single configuration row | None | `prisma/schema.prisma` | [prisma/schema.prisma:275-355](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L275-L355) |
| `Trace` | One event in a job's or company's path through a run | Names a job or company by plain id only | `prisma/schema.prisma` | [prisma/schema.prisma:618-650](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L618-L650) |
| `WorkLogEntry` | One filed job search activity for the Texas Workforce Commission | Names a job by plain id only | `prisma/schema.prisma` | [prisma/schema.prisma:657-673](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L657-L673) |

The database client is generated into `generated/pipeline` and the datasource is SQLite ([prisma/schema.prisma:3-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L3-L10)). The baseline migration creates the same seven tables ([prisma/migrations/0_init/migration.sql:2-131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/migrations/0_init/migration.sql#L2-L131)).

## Entity relationships

Only two real database relations exist. Both point at `Company`. Everything else that looks like a link is a plain text id on purpose.

```mermaid
erDiagram
    Company ||--o{ Job : "has (company_id, optional)"
    Company ||--o{ AtsSlug : "has (company_id, required)"
    Job }o..o{ Trace : "job_id, no relation"
    Company }o..o{ Trace : "company_id, no relation"
    Job }o..o{ WorkLogEntry : "job_id, no relation"

    Job {
        string id PK
        string company_id FK
        string raw_title
        string title
        string status
        boolean is_resolved
        boolean is_parsed
        boolean is_classified
        boolean is_judged
        datetime collected_at
        int alignment_score
    }
    Company {
        string id PK
        string name UK
        string match_key UK
        int employee_satisfaction
        int customer_satisfaction
        int work_life_balance
        int political_alignment
        datetime scored_at
        datetime enriched_at
    }
    AtsSlug {
        string id PK
        string slug UK
        string company_id FK
        string parser
        string collector
    }
    Place {
        string id PK
        string lookup_text UK
        float latitude
        float longitude
    }
    Setting {
        int id PK
        json search_terms
        json source_priority_list
        int expiry_threshold
    }
    Trace {
        int id PK
        string run_id
        string job_id
        string company_id
        string step
        string event
        string reason
    }
    WorkLogEntry {
        string id PK
        string job_id
        string company_name
        string job_title
        string activity
    }
```

<!-- Sources: prisma/schema.prisma:14-142, prisma/schema.prisma:147-210, prisma/schema.prisma:219-241, prisma/schema.prisma:254-273, prisma/schema.prisma:275-355, prisma/schema.prisma:618-650, prisma/schema.prisma:657-673 -->

The diagram shows a subset of columns. The dotted lines are the deliberate non-relations. The two real relations are `Job.company` ([prisma/schema.prisma:128](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L128)) and `AtsSlug.company` ([prisma/schema.prisma:236](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L236)). In the database, the job link sets `company_id` to null if the company is deleted, and the slug link refuses to delete a company that still holds a slug ([prisma/migrations/0_init/migration.sql:39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/migrations/0_init/migration.sql#L39), [prisma/migrations/0_init/migration.sql:77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/migrations/0_init/migration.sql#L77)).

### Why some links are deliberately missing

| Column | Why it is a plain id | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Trace.job_id` | "A plain column with no relation, so a trace outlives the job it describes." The pipeline may delete a job row. | [prisma/schema.prisma:624-627](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L624-L627) |
| `Trace.company_id` | Same reason as `job_id` | [prisma/schema.prisma:628-631](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L628-L631) |
| `WorkLogEntry.job_id` | The entry is a legal filing that cannot be regenerated, so it stands free of the job. An entry that read through to the row "would be destroyed with it". | [prisma/schema.prisma:652-662](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L652-L662) |
| `WorkLogEntry.company_name` and `job_title` | Copied onto the row, not read through. "A later write to that row must not change what was filed." | [prisma/schema.prisma:663-668](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L663-L668) |

## The Job model

`Job` is the largest table. It follows a rule: "Collection fills what its source supplied and leaves the rest empty, so a later phase can tell what still needs doing" ([prisma/schema.prisma:12-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L12-L13)). Most columns are optional for that reason. A test checks that the only required columns without a default are the database-written and orchestrator-written ones (inferred from the test name `AC17` in `prisma/schema.test.ts:483`, not read in full).

### The raw_ prefix convention

A column starting with `raw_` holds a value exactly as the source published it. The cleaned version has no prefix. A collector writes only the `raw_` columns. A normalizer fills the clean columns from them. The rule is in the ownership table: a collector writes "each into a `raw_` field exactly as it arrived", and a normalizer "reshapes raw data that is already there" and never goes looking ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:33-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L33-L34)).

| Raw column | Clean column | What normalization does | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `raw_title` | `title` | Reshapes into `{level} {role} - {team}`, so two sources publishing one role produce one title | [prisma/schema.prisma:25-30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L25-L30) |
| `raw_company_name` | `Company.name` (via `company_id`) | The normalized name lives on the company record | [prisma/schema.prisma:19-21](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L19-L21) |
| `raw_company_slug` | `AtsSlug` lookup | A stronger identity than a name. Association looks it up first. | [prisma/schema.prisma:22-24](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L22-L24) |
| `raw_location_list` | `normalized_location_list` | Cuts each entry into single places, dropping words that surround a place | [prisma/schema.prisma:63-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L63-L72) |
| `raw_mode_list` | `normalized_mode_list` | Translates into `remote`, `hybrid` or `in-person`, each held once. Other words are dropped. | [prisma/schema.prisma:73-79](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L73-L79) |
| `raw_salary` | `salary_low`, `salary_high`, `salary_period` | Reshapes the five-key envelope into whole-currency figures and a period | [prisma/schema.prisma:91-100](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L91-L100) |
| `original_url` | `original_url_match_key` | A squashed form for matching: scheme, lowercased host, path without trailing slash. The published link is never altered. | [prisma/schema.prisma:31-38](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L31-L38) |
| `resolved_url` | `resolved_url_match_key` | The same squashing | [prisma/schema.prisma:39-42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L39-L42) |

The salary envelope has a fixed shape of five keys: `salary_min`, `salary_max`, `salary_period`, `salary_currency` and `salary_unit`. `salary_unit` exists because "no figure carries its unit on its face". Only the collector knows whether its API sends cents ([lib/types/job-list-entry.ts:15-30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/types/job-list-entry.ts#L15-L30)).

### Field groups

| Group | Columns | Written by | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity | `id`, `company_id`, `collector`, `parser`, `collected_at` | `collected_at` is written once by the orchestrator and "nothing overwrites this" | [prisma/schema.prisma:15-18](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L15-L18), [prisma/schema.prisma:80-90](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L80-L90) |
| Dates | `posting_date`, `posting_updated_date`, `created_at`, `modified_at` | Source, plus the database | [prisma/schema.prisma:43-49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L43-L49) |
| Phase gates | `is_resolved`, `is_parsed`, `is_classified`, `is_judged` | Each phase sets its own | [prisma/schema.prisma:50-57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L50-L57) |
| Lifecycle | `status` | See the status table below | [prisma/schema.prisma:58-63](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L58-L63) |
| Location judgement | `location_match`, `location_match_place`, `location_match_mode`, `is_repost` | Classification | [prisma/schema.prisma:104-118](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L104-L118) |
| Posting text | `description` | The source, as supplied. Scoring reads it instead of fetching the page again. | [prisma/schema.prisma:100-103](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L100-L103) |
| Alignment | `alignment_score`, `alignment_rationale` | Scoring | [prisma/schema.prisma:119-127](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L119-L127) |

`location_match` has three states, not two. Empty means no place on the job could be read, which is not the same answer as too far. A job left empty stays in the backlog for a later run to retry ([prisma/schema.prisma:104-108](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L104-L108)).

`alignment_score` carries no default. "Empty is what says the job still needs scoring". A job that returns to the backlog after being posted again is emptied, because the posting it was judged on is not the one now on offer ([prisma/schema.prisma:119-123](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L119-L123)).

### Phase-gate flags

The four flags are booleans that default to false. A step asks the database for jobs with the right combination, which is why steps need no list from each other.

| Flag | Set by | Read by | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `is_resolved` | Resolution (or a collector that resolves itself) | `findUnresolved` wants `false`. `findUnparsed` wants `true`. | [lib/services/job-service.ts:416-433](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L416-L433) |
| `is_parsed` | Parsing | `findUnparsed` wants `false`. `findUnclassified` wants `true`. | [lib/services/job-service.ts:427-433](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L427-L433), [lib/services/job-service.ts:488-494](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L488-L494) |
| `is_classified` | Classification, or the let-through handler | `findUnclassified` wants `false`. `findNeedingScores` wants `true`. | [lib/services/job-service.ts:468-486](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L468-L486) |
| `is_judged` | Scoring, "once the job holds a fit score or its employer holds any score, and nothing else writes it" | The dashboard shows a job with `false` as unjudged | [prisma/schema.prisma:54-57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L54-L57) |

All four reads also require `status = "backlog"`. The list reads omit the five gate fields from what they return. An entry carried on to a save "should hold no stale copy of a flag another phase owns" ([lib/services/job-service.ts:162-171](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L162-L171)).

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Collected: collector writes raw_ fields
    Collected --> Resolved: is_resolved = true
    Resolved --> Parsed: is_parsed = true
    Parsed --> Classified: is_classified = true
    Classified --> Judged: is_judged = true after scoring
    Judged --> [*]

    Collected --> Unresolvable: resolution gives up
    Resolved --> Unparseable: no place found
    Parsed --> Expired: dead page
    Classified --> TooFar: no place close enough
    Classified --> Expired: too old

    state "backlog" as Collected
    state "status unresolvable" as Unresolvable
    state "status unparseable" as Unparseable
    state "status expired" as Expired
    state "status too far" as TooFar
```

<!-- Sources: prisma/schema.prisma:50-63, lib/services/job-service.ts:416-494, .claude/rules/part-ownership.md:44-46 -->

The diagram shows the gate order, not every path. The steps for each exit follow the status rule: resolution sets `unresolvable`, the parser sets `unparseable` or `expired`, classification sets `too far` or `expired` ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:44-46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L44-L46)).

<!-- Sources: lib/services/job-service.ts:416-433, lib/services/job-service.ts:469-494 -->

### Status

`status` is a plain string with a default of `backlog`, not a database enum. The twelve valid values are declared once in code ([lib/utils/job-status.ts:22-37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L22-L37)). Because the database does not enforce the list, a typo would create a state no query reads, and the single declaration is what prevents it.

| Group | Statuses | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-active, in play | `backlog` | Waiting to be worked on | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L25) |
| Ruled out | `expired`, `too far`, `won't apply`, `unresolvable`, `unparseable`, `rejected` | Ruled out by the pipeline or the user | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:67-74](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L67-L74) |
| Active | `app. sent`, `screening`, `interview`, `test`, `offer` | The user has applied and has not been rejected. "Frozen except for its status." | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:8-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L8-L14) |
| Counted by Texas | `app. sent`, `screening`, `interview` | These write a work log entry. `test` and `offer` do not. | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:49-53](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L49-L53) |
| Rechecked when re-added | `expired`, `too far`, `unresolvable`, `unparseable` | Adding the link again sends the job back through every step | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:84-89](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L84-L89) |

### Indexes

Dedupe finds matches by three clauses, and each has an index so the query reads an index rather than scanning. None is unique, because two rows for one posting hold the same key between the saves and the pass that collapses them ([prisma/schema.prisma:130-141](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L130-L141)).

| Index | Serves | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `original_url_match_key` | Dedupe's first link clause | [prisma/schema.prisma:135](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L135) |
| `resolved_url_match_key` | Dedupe's second link clause | [prisma/schema.prisma:136](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L136) |
| `company_id`, `title` together | Dedupe's third clause. `company_id` leads because it narrows hardest. | [prisma/schema.prisma:137-141](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L137-L141) |

## The Company model

A company is an employer plus what an agent researched about it. Its `name` is optional, because a company met only as a board slug has no name "and nothing invents one for it" ([prisma/schema.prisma:149-151](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L149-L151)).

| Group | Columns | Notes | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity | `name`, `match_key` | Both unique. `match_key` is the name lowercased, stripped of non-alphanumerics and trailing legal words. The database refuses a duplicate employer "whatever the matching code does". | [prisma/schema.prisma:149-156](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L149-L156) |
| Scores | `employee_satisfaction`, `customer_satisfaction`, `work_life_balance`, `political_alignment` | Each 1 to 5. No default: "a seeded middle value would read as a judgement nobody made". | [prisma/schema.prisma:157-164](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L157-L164) |
| Rationales | Four `_rationale` columns | One per category, so re-scoring one writes one field | [prisma/schema.prisma:165-172](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L165-L172) |
| Score metadata | `scored_at`, `scores_guessed` | One date covers all four. `scores_guessed` lists categories the agent found nothing public for, because the rubric awards a 3 either way. | [prisma/schema.prisma:173-182](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L173-L182) |
| Contact details | `address`, `phone`, `website` | Filled in by an internet search the first time a job takes a status that writes a work log entry | [prisma/schema.prisma:183-189](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L183-L189) |
| Search state | `enriched_at`, `enrichment_status`, `enrichment_uncertain`, `enrichment_flags` | `enriched_at` is the only thing that marks a company done. A search that found nothing leaves it empty, so the company is searched again. | [prisma/schema.prisma:190-205](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L190-L205) |

Four score categories are named in one list in code, so a fifth could be added in one place ([lib/services/company-service.ts:13-21](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L13-L21)). See [Services](./services.md) and [Scoring](../agent-workflows/scoring.md).

## The AtsSlug model

This table replaced a pair of columns on `Company`. That pair forced two facts to travel together: that a company posts on a hiring system, and that we poll its board every run. Now the slug and the parser carry the first fact. The collector carries the second ([prisma/schema.prisma:212-218](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L212-L218)).

| Column | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `slug` | The board slug. Unique across the table, "because a job carries a slug without carrying which board it came from". | [prisma/schema.prisma:221-224](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L221-L224) |
| `company_id` | The company whose board this is. Required. | [prisma/schema.prisma:225-226](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L225-L226) |
| `parser` | Which parser read the posting the slug was found on | [prisma/schema.prisma:227-230](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L227-L230) |
| `collector` | Which collector polls this board. Empty until promotion. "Filling it in is what starts the polling." | [prisma/schema.prisma:231-233](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L231-L233) |

An index on `collector` lets each ATS collector ask for its own boards without reading every row ([prisma/schema.prisma:238-240](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L238-L240)).

## The Place model

One row per place the map service was asked about, so a run only pays for places it has never seen. The comment records the payoff: 3,975 lookups resolve to 789 distinct places ([prisma/schema.prisma:243-247](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L243-L247)). A place is found again by its `lookup_text`, "the whole identity here" ([prisma/schema.prisma:253-256](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L253-L256)). Only a place that resolved is stored. A text with no result writes no row, so it is tried again next run ([prisma/schema.prisma:248-250](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L248-L250)). `outline` holds the place's shape. It is absent for a line or a single point, which fall back on distance ([prisma/schema.prisma:264-268](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L264-L268)).

## The Setting model

`Setting` is a single-row table. The row id defaults to 1 and the code always reads `id: 1` ([prisma/schema.prisma:276](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L276), [lib/services/settings-service.ts:45-47](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L45-L47)). Every settings column is nullable except the id and the two date columns, because a seed fills what is absent (see [Database Commands and Safety](./database-commands.md)).

| Group | Columns | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Search | `search_terms`, `location`, `radius`, `expiry_threshold` | [prisma/schema.prisma:277-285](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L277-L285) |
| Title vocabulary | `title_head_nouns`, `title_levels`, `title_suffixes`, `title_removal_words` | [prisma/schema.prisma:286-300](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L286-L300) |
| Source ranking | `source_priority_list`, `identifying_query_values` | [prisma/schema.prisma:301-315](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L301-L315) |
| Resolution pacing | `resolution_fast_concurrency`, `resolution_slow_concurrency`, `resolution_slow_pause_seconds` | [prisma/schema.prisma:316-335](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L316-L335) |
| Ageing and promotion | `repost_gap_days`, `promotion_threshold`, `score_expiry_days`, `guessed_score_expiry_days` | [prisma/schema.prisma:336-352](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L336-L352) |

## The Trace and WorkLogEntry models

`Trace` is covered fully on [Tracing and the Run Summary](../architecture/tracing-and-run-summary.md). `WorkLogEntry` has six columns: `id`, `job_id`, `company_name`, `job_title`, `activity` and `created_at`. It has no last-changed column because "nothing revises an entry" ([prisma/schema.prisma:654-656](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L654-L656)). The activity is written in the wording Texas accepts: "Applied for job", "Had phone screen" or "Had interview" ([prisma/schema.prisma:669-671](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L669-L671)). See [Status Change and Work Log](../agent-workflows/status-change-and-work-log.md).

## From database row to in-memory job

A job travels through the pipeline as a `JobListEntry`, not a database `Job`. The entry type "maps one to one onto the Job database row". Every field is optional because a collector fills only what its source supplied ([lib/types/job-list-entry.ts:1-12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/types/job-list-entry.ts#L1-L12)).

Two differences exist. Five Json columns are retyped as real arrays or objects ([lib/types/job-list-entry.ts:83-97](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/types/job-list-entry.ts#L83-L97)). And one field, `delete_on_save`, is not a column. A later step sets it on an entry it wants removed ([lib/types/job-list-entry.ts:96](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/types/job-list-entry.ts#L96)). A list, `JOB_LIST_ENTRY_FIELDS`, names every column in schema order plus `delete_on_save`, and a `satisfies` clause ties it to the type ([lib/types/job-list-entry.ts:99-141](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/types/job-list-entry.ts#L99-L141)).

The job service does the cast in one place. Its comment calls it "the single documented cast that bridges the two" ([lib/services/job-service.ts:234-239](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L234-L239)).

## Migrations

The folder `prisma/migrations/` holds three migrations and a lock file naming the provider as `sqlite` ([prisma/migrations/migration_lock.toml:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/migrations/migration_lock.toml#L1-L3)).

| Migration | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `0_init` | Creates the seven tables, their indexes and the two foreign keys | [prisma/migrations/0_init/migration.sql:2-162](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/migrations/0_init/migration.sql#L2-L162) |
| `20260919000000_add_is_judged` | Adds `Job.is_judged` as a non-null boolean defaulting to false. Then marks existing jobs once: judged only if resolved, parsed and classified, and the job or its employer holds a score. | [prisma/migrations/20260919000000_add_is_judged/migration.sql:1-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/migrations/20260919000000_add_is_judged/migration.sql#L1-L23) |
| `20260923155709_add_identifying_query_values` | Adds the nullable `Setting.identifying_query_values` column | [prisma/migrations/20260923155709_add_identifying_query_values/migration.sql:1-2](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/migrations/20260923155709_add_identifying_query_values/migration.sql#L1-L2) |

The `is_judged` migration includes a data fill, not just a column. A test builds the database from the baseline migration, because the fill has to run against rows that predate the column ([prisma/is-judged-migration.test.ts:15-19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/is-judged-migration.test.ts#L15-L19)). After editing the schema, run `npx prisma generate`, and use `db:migrate` to apply the change (`CLAUDE.md`, "Commands"). See [Database Commands and Safety](./database-commands.md).

## Getting Started


<doc title="Job Search Assistant Wiki" path="./index.md">
# Job Search Assistant Wiki

The Job Search Assistant is a personal command-line tool, driven by Claude Code skills, that finds job postings, ranks them, tracks applications, and files the Texas unemployment work log. It is one pipeline written in TypeScript and run through `tsx`, with a single SQLite database behind Prisma ([CLAUDE.md:1-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L1-L14)). The only code shaped to a particular job site is its collectors and parsers. Every other step acts on a job's data alone ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:7-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L7-L11)).

This page is the entry point for developers. The repository's `README.md` gives a short overview; start here or at [Overview](./getting-started/overview.md) for depth.

## Quick Start

Full detail, including the order and the reasons behind each step, is in [Environment Setup](./getting-started/setup.md).

```bash
# 1. Install packages; postinstall runs `npx prisma generate`
npm install

# 2. Create .env from the template, then set PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL and any API keys
cp .env.example .env

# 3. Build, migrate and seed the database
npm run db:create ./pipeline.db   # refuses the database .env names; see the setup page
npm run db:migrate                # writes a dated backup first
npm run db:seed                   # fills absent settings, overwrites nothing

# 4. Get the browser resolution and parsing drive (inferred, standard Playwright step)
npx playwright install chromium

# 5. Check the install
npm run test                      # Vitest
npm run lint                      # ESLint, then the type check

# 6. Use it
npm run job-search                # run the whole pipeline; prints its run id first
npm run serve                     # read-only dashboard, default port 3001
```

| Command | Script | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run job-search` | `scripts/job-search.ts` | [package.json:11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L11) |
| `npm run score:gather` / `score:save` | `scripts/score-gather.ts`, `scripts/score-save.ts` | [package.json:17-18](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L17-L18) |
| `npm run find-jobs` / `change-status` | `scripts/find-jobs.ts`, `scripts/change-status.ts` | [package.json:13-15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L13-L15) |
| `npm run serve` | `scripts/serve.ts` | [package.json:6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L6) |
| `npm run db:create` / `db:migrate` / `db:seed` | `scripts/db-*.ts` | [package.json:8-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L8-L10) |
| `npm run lint` / `test` | ESLint and `tsc`, Vitest | [package.json:19-21](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L19-L21) |

Every command and the skill that calls it is listed in [Commands and Skills](./getting-started/commands-and-skills.md).

## Architecture Overview

A job search is one call to `runJobSearch`. It runs three stretches, collect, resolve and parse, and each one ends in a database write. A later stretch does not take a list from the one before it. It asks the database for the jobs that still need its work ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:1-16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L1-L16)). Backlog cleanup opens the run, and promotion and classification close it. Scoring is not part of this run. The `job-search` skill runs it afterwards through two separate commands, with an agent doing the judging in between.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CLI["npm run job-search<br>scripts/job-search.ts"] --> CHK{"Schema drifted?"}
    CHK -- yes --> STOP["Exit 1: run db:migrate"]
    CHK -- no --> RUN["runJobSearch<br>run id, collectedAt, services"]

    subgraph S0["Open: backlog cleanup"]
        BC["Expire old jobs,<br>clear stale company scores"] --> BCS["Save"]
    end

    subgraph S1["Collect stretch"]
        COL["Collection<br>14 collectors"] --> N1["Normalize"] --> A1["Associate company"] --> D1["Dedupe"] --> SV1["Save"]
    end

    subgraph S2["Resolve stretch"]
        Q2[("Find unresolved")] --> RES["Resolution<br>visible browser"] --> D2["Dedupe"] --> SV2["Save"]
    end

    subgraph S3["Parse stretch"]
        Q3[("Find unparsed")] --> PAR["Parsing<br>parser by domain"] --> N3["Normalize"] --> A3["Associate company"] --> D3["Dedupe"] --> SV3["Save"]

    RUN --> BC
    BCS --> COL
    SV1 --> Q2
    SV2 --> Q3
    SV3 --> PRO
    SV5 --> SUM["Summary rebuilt<br>from Trace rows"]

    DB[("pipeline.db")]
    SV1 -.-> DB
    SV2 -.-> DB
    SV3 -.-> DB
    SV5 -.-> DB

    classDef default fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3

    style S2 fill:#161b22,stroke:#30363d,color:#e6edf3
```

# Overview

## Why this project exists

Checking many job boards by hand is slow and repetitive. The Job Search Assistant is a personal command-line tool that does the repetitive part. It collects job postings from many sources, removes duplicates, judges which ones are close enough to apply to, and asks an AI agent to rank them. It also keeps the record that the Texas unemployment program requires. The user then looks at the results on a small local web page.

The tool is driven by Claude Code "skills". A skill is a written procedure that Claude follows. Each skill runs one or more `npm run` commands and then explains the output to the user. The earlier description in `docs/APP.md` still speaks of "scrapers" and a "status pipeline". That file is dated. This page describes the system as the code builds it today ([docs/APP.md:5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/APP.md#L5)). The project's own description is in [CLAUDE.md:3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L3).

## The four jobs

| Job | What it means in plain words | Where it happens | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Find** | Pull job lists from 14 sources, follow each link to the employer's own posting, and read it | `npm run job-search` | [lib/collectors/registry.ts:19-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/registry.ts#L19-L34) |
| **Rank** | An agent scores each job against the user's profile and each employer against a company rubric | The `score-backlog` skill with `score:gather` and `score:save` | [.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:22-26](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L22-L26) |
| **Track** | Each job has one of twelve statuses, changed by hand when the user applies, is rejected, and so on | The `change-status` skill and `npm run change-status` | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:24-37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L24-L37) |
| **File the work log** | Some status changes write a Texas Workforce Commission job-search entry that cannot be rebuilt later | `npm run change-status` | [scripts/change-status.ts:1-12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L1-L12) |

A fifth, smaller job is **view**: a read-only local dashboard shows the backlog, active jobs, ruled-out jobs, and the work log ([scripts/serve.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L1-L5)). See [Dashboard](../deep-dive/dashboard/dashboard.md).

The folder layout inside `lib/` follows one rule: every file sits in a folder named for the kind of thing it is ([.claude/rules/naming.md:7-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L7-L25)). See [System Design](../deep-dive/architecture/system-design.md).

## Why the design looks the way it does

The design rests on one idea: **every step ends in a database write**. The orchestrator says so in its header comment: each of the three stretches "ends in a database write, so a run's work outlives the run whether or not the next step gets to it" ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:1-16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L1-L16)). The next step does not receive a list from the one before. It asks the database for the jobs that carry the right marker. This gives three benefits.

| Benefit | Why it matters | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A run that crashes keeps its finished work | A long run that dies at step 9 does not lose steps 1 to 8 | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:653-658](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L653-L658) |
| The same step can serve many callers | Saving is called by a job search, a hand status change, and scoring | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:19-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L19-L23) |
| Knowledge of a job site stays in two places | Only collectors and parsers are written to fit a site | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:7-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L7-L11) |

Scoring is the one step that is not inside the command. Scoring needs an agent to think, and a single command cannot pause while an agent thinks. So the `job-search` skill runs the pipeline command first and then hands the work to the `score-backlog` skill ([.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:60](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L60)).

## What one job search does

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Backlog cleanup<br>expire old jobs and old scores"] --> B["Collection<br>14 collectors"]
    B --> C["Normalize, associate,<br>dedupe, save"]
    C --> D["Resolution<br>follow links in a browser"]
    D --> E["Dedupe and save"]
    E --> F["Parsing<br>read each posting"]
    F --> G["Normalize, associate,<br>dedupe, save"]
    G --> H["Promotion<br>reposted jobs return"]
    H --> I["Classification<br>close enough? expired?"]
    I --> J["Save"]
    classDef default fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```

<!-- Sources: lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:222-262, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:276-362, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:390-434, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:480-551, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:586-637 -->

The order matters. Cleanup opens the run so the backlog collection adds to has already been swept ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:218-220](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L218-L220)). Normalization runs before company association, because association matches on the cleaned company name ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:504-506](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L504-L506)). Promotion and classification close the run, because an expired job only earns a fresh date after collection finds its new listing ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:579-581](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L579-L581)). The full walk-through is in [Job Search Run](../deep-dive/architecture/job-search-run.md).

## A typical session

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as User
    participant C as Claude Code
    participant P as npm run job-search
    participant S as score-backlog skill
    participant D as Dashboard
    U->>C: Run the job-search skill
    C->>P: Start the pipeline
    P-->>C: Run id, errors, warnings, summary
    C->>U: Paste the summary exactly as printed
    C->>S: Hand over the run id
    S-->>C: Scores saved, summary
    C->>D: Start the serve skill
    D-->>U: Address of the local page
    U->>C: Later: change-status skill when a job moves
```

<!-- Sources: .claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:11-55, .claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:17-126, scripts/job-search.ts:73-76 -->

The command prints `Run: {run-id}` first so scoring can file its own records under the same run ([scripts/job-search.ts:73-76](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L73-L76)). The skill also tells the user that a visible browser window opens partway through and holds the screen ([.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:21](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L21)). The code confirms this: resolution launches with `headless: false` because headless requests were refused in a measured test ([lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts:19-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts#L19-L23)).

## Where the code differs from the older docs

| Claim in older docs | What the code shows | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |

<doc title="Environment Setup" path="./getting-started/setup.md">
# Environment Setup

## Overview

Setup has four jobs: install the packages, build the database, tell the app where its database is and give it any API keys, and fill the database with default settings. The order matters, because each step needs the one before it. This page also explains why each step exists, so a failure message makes sense when it appears.

Everything below was read from the code. Steps that the repository does not state are marked "inferred".

## At a glance

| Step | Command or file | What it does | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Install | `npm install` | Installs packages, then `postinstall` generates the Prisma database client | [package.json:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L7) |
| 2. Create database | `npm run db:create {file}` | Deletes the named file, then builds it from the schema | [scripts/db-create.ts:71-75](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L71-L75) |
| 3. Environment | copy `.env.example` to `.env` | Names the database file and holds API keys | [.env.example:1](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.env.example#L1) |
| 4. Migrate | `npm run db:migrate` | Backs up the database, then applies any pending schema change | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:68-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L68-L72) |
| 5. Seed | `npm run db:seed` | Fills absent settings and the source priority list | [scripts/db-seed.ts:222-230](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L222-L230) |
| 6. Browsers | `npx playwright install chromium` (inferred) | Gets the browser that resolution and parsing drive | [lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts:52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts#L52) |
| 7. Profile | copy the example profile (inferred) | Gives the scoring agent the candidate to score against | [.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L65) |
| 8. Check | `npm run test` and `npm run lint` | Runs the test suite, linter, and type check | [package.json:19-21](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L19-L21) |

## The setup order

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["npm install"] --> B["postinstall: npx prisma generate"]
    B --> C["npm run db:create FILE<br>fresh copy only, before .env"]
    C --> D["Copy .env.example to .env<br>set PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL and keys"]
    D --> E["npm run db:migrate"]
    E --> F["npm run db:seed"]
    F --> G["npx playwright install chromium<br>inferred"]
    G --> H["Add the private scoring profile"]
    H --> I["npm run test and npm run lint"]
    I --> J["First: Claude Code job-search skill"]
    classDef default fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```

<!-- Sources: package.json:7, .env.example:5, scripts/db-create.ts:33-77, scripts/db-migrate.ts:60-99, scripts/db-seed.ts:222-230, .claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:65 -->

## Step 1. Install

The project runs TypeScript directly through `tsx` with no build step ([CLAUDE.md:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L7)). No Node version is pinned: there is no `.nvmrc` file and `package.json` has no `engines` field. The type package is `@types/node` version 20 ([package.json:38](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L38)), so Node 20 or newer is the safe choice (inferred).

`npm install` runs `postinstall`, which runs `npx prisma generate` ([package.json:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L7)). This builds the typed database client into the `generated/pipeline` folder ([prisma/schema.prisma:3-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L3-L6)). That folder is not tracked, and the app imports it from `lib/db/pipeline-db.ts` ([lib/db/pipeline-db.ts:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/pipeline-db.ts#L7)). Without it, nothing that touches the database will start.

After you edit `prisma/schema.prisma`, run `npx prisma generate` by hand. Neither database command regenerates the client ([CLAUDE.md:43](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L43)). That includes `db:migrate` when it applies a real schema change ([scripts/db-migrate.ts:85-88](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L85-L88)). This was tested with Prisma 7.10 on a throwaway database.

## Step 2. Create the database

`db:create` builds a database from the schema with `prisma db push`. Before that, it removes the target file and the SQLite side files `-journal`, `-wal` and `-shm`, so the build starts from nothing ([scripts/db-create.ts:58-66](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L58-L66)).

Because it deletes, it has two safety rules:

| Rule | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| It takes no default target. You must pass a path | A mistyped bare command cannot land on a database anyone cares about | [scripts/db-create.ts:33-36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L33-L36) |
| It refuses the database named by `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL` in the repo's own `.env` | A wipe of the real file must not be possible | [scripts/db-create.ts:42-56](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L42-L56) |
| It reads `.env` directly, not `process.env` | A shell that exports a different value cannot make a wipe look safe | [scripts/db-create.ts:4-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L4-L7) |
| It asks the filesystem whether two paths are one file | Case-folding disks and shortcuts defeat plain text comparison | [lib/utils/same-file.ts:1-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/same-file.ts#L1-L9) |

### A catch on a fresh clone

On a first setup, `.env` names `file:./pipeline.db`, and `db:create` refuses that very file. When neither path exists yet, `isSameFile` falls back to comparing the paths as lowercase text, so a not-yet-created `pipeline.db` still counts as the protected file ([lib/utils/same-file.ts:56-59](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/same-file.ts#L56-L59)). The script also skips the check when `.env` is missing or holds no `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL` ([scripts/db-create.ts:40-46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L40-L46)).

On a fresh copy of the project only, with no `pipeline.db` yet, create the database before you create `.env`: run `npm run db:create ./pipeline.db`. With no `.env`, the command has no real database to protect, so it accepts the target ([scripts/db-create.ts:40-46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L40-L46)). Never run this once `pipeline.db` exists: the command deletes the file it is given ([scripts/db-create.ts:58-66](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L58-L66)). This order was read from the code, not run.

## Step 3. Environment file

`.env` is ignored by git, and only `.env.example` is committed ([.gitignore:4-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.gitignore#L4-L7)). Copy the template and fill it in.

### What each key powers

| Variable | What it powers | Where the code reads it | If missing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL` | The one database the app uses, for example `file:./pipeline.db` | [lib/db/pipeline-env.ts:7-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/pipeline-env.ts#L7-L17) | Throws and stops the command |
| `ADZUNA_APP_ID`, `ADZUNA_API_KEY` | The Adzuna collector | [lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:123-124](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/adzuna.ts#L123-L124) | That collector returns an error line and no jobs |
| `RAPIDAPI_KEY` | The JSearch collector | [lib/collectors/jsearch.ts:116](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/jsearch.ts#L116) | That collector returns an error line and no jobs |
| `GEOCODE_MAPS_API_KEY` | Turns a job's location into coordinates so it can be measured against the home location | [lib/tools/geocoder.ts:104](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L104) | Throws "no place can be looked up" |
| `APIFY_API_TOKEN` | Finds an employer's address, phone and website for the work log | [lib/tools/company-search.ts:74](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L74) | Raises a missing-credential error at search time |
| `DATABASE_URL` | The old database, read only by the one-time data move | [scripts/db-migrate-data.ts:277](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate-data.ts#L277) | Not needed for normal use |
| `PORT` (optional, not in the template) | Dashboard port, default 3001 | [scripts/serve.ts:56](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L56) | Falls back to 3001 |
| `COLLECTOR_FIXTURE_DIR` (optional, not in the template) | Folder of saved pages for the offline fixture collector | [lib/collectors/fixture.ts:30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/fixture.ts#L30) | Uses `lib/collectors/fixtures` |

### Why the database variable has no fallback

`getPipelineDatabaseUrl()` is the function that reads `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL`. It throws when the value is missing and does not fall back to the old `DATABASE_URL`. The comment gives the reason: a Prisma command run without it should fail loudly instead of quietly reaching the old database ([prisma.config.ts:14-16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma.config.ts#L14-L16)). The lookup runs when the function is called, not at load time, so a test can delete the variable and prove the failure ([lib/db/pipeline-env.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/pipeline-env.ts#L1-L6)).

`createPipelineDb()` loads `.env` itself, because it is "the one door to the database". A caller that already set the variable wins, since dotenv never overwrites an existing value ([lib/db/pipeline-db.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/pipeline-db.ts#L1-L6)). Only `lib/db/` builds a database connection ([.claude/rules/naming.md:25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L25)).

```mermaid
graph LR
    ENV[".env file"] --> DOT["dotenv"]
    SHELL["Shell variable"] --> DOT
    DOT --> GET["getPipelineDatabaseUrl<br>throws if empty"]
    GET --> CFG["prisma.config.ts<br>Prisma commands"]
    GET --> DB["createPipelineDb<br>app commands"]
    DB --> FILE[("pipeline.db")]
    CFG --> FILE
    classDef default fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```

<!-- Sources: lib/db/pipeline-env.ts:7-17, lib/db/pipeline-db.ts:6-18, prisma.config.ts:3-17 -->

## Step 4. Migrate

`db:migrate` is the only way to change the schema ([CLAUDE.md:41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L41)). Its order of work shows why it is safe:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as User
    participant M as db-migrate.ts
    participant F as pipeline.db
    participant P as prisma migrate
    U->>M: npm run db:migrate {name}
    M->>F: Does the file exist?
    F-->>M: Yes (else stop: run db:create first)
    M->>F: Copy to pipeline.db.{timestamp}.backup
    M->>F: Is there a _prisma_migrations table?
    alt No history, built by db push
        M->>P: migrate resolve --applied (each folder)
    end
    M->>P: migrate dev --name {name}
    P-->>F: Apply pending change
```

<!-- Sources: scripts/db-migrate.ts:20-99 -->

| Behavior | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stops if no database file exists | There is nothing to migrate; it tells you to run `db:create` | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:62-65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L62-L65) |
| Writes a dated `.backup` copy first | A botched migration must never leave you without the old data | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:68-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L68-L72) |
| Marks every existing migration as applied if the file has no migration table | `db:create` uses `db push`, which lays down the schema but no history | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:40-57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L40-L57) |
| Passes an optional name to `prisma migrate dev` | Names a new migration | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:79-83](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L79-L83) |

Backups end in `.backup` after the database name, and git ignores them ([.gitignore:12-15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.gitignore#L12-L15)). Before any command reads or writes data, it checks that the database matches the code. If it does not, it prints the three drift lines and tells you to run `npm run db:migrate` ([lib/db/schema-drift.ts:15-27](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-drift.ts#L15-L27)). The check exists because the trace service swallows write failures, so a run on a mismatched database would otherwise work for minutes and leave no record ([scripts/job-search.ts:44-52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L44-L52)). See [Database Commands](../deep-dive/data/database-commands.md).

## Step 5. Seed the settings

`db:seed` fills the single `Setting` row. It fills what is empty and overwrites nothing, so it is safe after every schema change ([scripts/db-seed.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L1-L5)).

| What it seeds | Behavior | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Defaults for search terms, home location, radius, expiry, title vocabularies, resolution pacing, thresholds | Creates the row if absent; otherwise fills only the columns that are `null` | [scripts/db-seed.ts:120-184](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L120-L184) |
| The source priority list | Appends any collector or parser name that is missing, to the bottom; never reorders | [scripts/db-seed.ts:189-219](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L189-L219) |

The seed starts the list with `collector:user`, then every dedicated parser, then every collector, then the general parser ([scripts/db-seed.ts:88-95](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L88-L95)). The order is only a starting point, because the owner reorders the list by hand. A source missing from the list ranks below all listed sources, so it loses every contested field. That is why the rule says to run `db:seed` whenever a registry changes ([.claude/rules/source-registry.md:7-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/source-registry.md#L7-L9)).

The default home location is the postal code `78701`, with a radius of 30 miles ([scripts/db-seed.ts:13-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L13-L14)). Every setting is explained in [Quick Reference](./quick-reference.md#settings). A missing setting makes the settings service throw, which stops the run instead of guessing ([lib/services/settings-service.ts:39-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L39-L41)).

## Step 6. Browsers (inferred)

Two browser tools use Playwright's Chromium. Resolution opens a visible browser ([lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts:23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts#L23)). Page rendering for parsing and for `fetch-rendered-page` uses a hidden one ([lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts:77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L77)). `postinstall` only generates the database client, so nothing in the repository downloads the browser. Running `npx playwright install chromium` is the standard Playwright step (inferred).

## Step 7. The scoring profile (inferred)

The `score-backlog` skill reads a private profile file, `.alignment-info.md`, in its own folder ([.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L65)). Git ignores it ([.gitignore:21-22](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.gitignore#L21-L22)). A made-up public example sits beside it as `.alignment-info.example.md`. Copy the example to `.alignment-info.md` and replace its content with your own profile. This wiki does not describe any real profile.

## Step 8. Check the install

| Command | What it checks | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run test` | The whole Vitest suite, with the time zone fixed to UTC | [vitest.config.ts:11-18](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/vitest.config.ts#L11-L18) |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint, then the TypeScript type check | [package.json:19-20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L19-L20) |

The test run excludes `docs/` ([vitest.config.ts:14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/vitest.config.ts#L14)), and lint ignores `docs`, `node_modules` and `generated` ([.eslintignore:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.eslintignore#L1-L4)). One comment in the test config says "No tests yet", which is out of date: many test files exist ([vitest.config.ts:15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/vitest.config.ts#L15)). See [Testing](../deep-dive/quality/testing.md).

<doc title="Commands and Skills" path="./getting-started/commands-and-skills.md">
# Commands and Skills

## Overview

The project has two layers. A **command** is a small TypeScript script run with `npm run`. It does one deterministic thing and prints text. A **skill** is a written procedure that Claude Code follows. A skill exists where a human or an agent has to decide something, because a command cannot pause to think. The skill runs commands, reads their output, and reports it to the user. Together they let one request such as "run the job search" cover collecting, scoring, and showing results.

## At a glance

| Layer | Count | Where it lives | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| npm scripts in `package.json` | 17 (16 commands plus `postinstall`) | `package.json` and `scripts/` | [package.json:5-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L5-L23) |
| Project skills for the app | 6 | `.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md` | [.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L1-L4) |
| Helper notes for the code-graph tool | 4 | `.claude/skills/*.md` (loose files) | [.claude/skills/debug-issue.md:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/debug-issue.md#L1-L4) |

## Which skill calls which command

<!-- Sources: .claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:13-53, .claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:22-120, .claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md:41-70, .claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md:47-70, .claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md:38-72 -->

The `serve` skill is not in this repository. It is a user-level skill that the `job-search` skill invokes ([.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:53](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L53)). Its command, `npm run serve`, is in `package.json` ([package.json:6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L6)).

## Commands

### Day-to-day commands

| Command | What it does and why it exists | Flags | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run job-search` | Runs the whole pipeline. Prints `Run: {id}` first, then errors, warnings, and a summary read back from trace rows. Exits non-zero if the run stopped early | `--limit N` for tests only | [scripts/job-search.ts:40-140](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L40-L140) |
| `npm run score:gather` | Writes every unscored job and company to a file for an agent to judge. Exists because scoring needs judgment, not a fixed rule | `--out FILE`, `--run-id ID` | [scripts/score-gather.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-gather.ts#L1-L4), [scripts/score-gather.ts:27-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-gather.ts#L27-L41) |
| `npm run score:save` | Writes the agent's scores back. Runs once per batch so a run that stops halfway keeps the research it paid for | `--in FILE`, `--summary` | [scripts/score-save.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-save.ts#L1-L5), [scripts/score-save.ts:45-48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-save.ts#L45-L48) |
| `npm run find-jobs` | Finds a job by its link, otherwise by part of the employer's name. Only reads. Prints one JSON object | `--url`, `--company`, `--statuses` | [scripts/find-jobs.ts:1-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L1-L9), [scripts/find-jobs.ts:86-95](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L86-L95) |
| `npm run change-status` | Sets job statuses by hand. Files a work log entry where Texas counts the status as an activity. Refuses a whole submission if one entry is bad | `--in FILE` | [scripts/change-status.ts:1-12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L1-L12), [scripts/change-status.ts:36-40](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L36-L40) |
| `npm run add-external-jobs` | Takes links the user found elsewhere and runs only those through the pipeline's steps | `--in FILE` | [scripts/add-external-jobs.ts:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/add-external-jobs.ts#L1-L3), [scripts/add-external-jobs.ts:26](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/add-external-jobs.ts#L26) |
| `npm run fetch-rendered-page` | Prints a page's finished HTML after its scripts have run. Many postings build their text in the browser, so a plain fetch gets an empty shell | `--url URL` | [scripts/fetch-rendered-page.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/fetch-rendered-page.ts#L1-L4), [scripts/fetch-rendered-page.ts:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/fetch-rendered-page.ts#L19) |
| `npm run serve` | Starts the read-only dashboard, default port 3001 | `PORT` environment variable | [scripts/serve.ts:20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L20), [scripts/serve.ts:55-58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L55-L58) |

### One-off and maintenance commands

| Command | What it does and why it exists | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run recover-unparseable-jobs` | Moves every `unparseable` job whose link a parser now claims back to `backlog`. Run by hand after shipping a new parser. Takes no flags. No skill calls it. It runs through the same status-change code a hand change uses | [scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts:1-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts#L1-L17), [scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts:61-78](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts#L61-L78) |
| `npm run db:create {file}` | Rebuilds a named database from the schema. Deletes the target first. Refuses the real database | [scripts/db-create.ts:1-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L1-L7) |
| `npm run db:migrate` | Backs up the database, then applies schema changes | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:68-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L68-L72) |
| `npm run db:seed` | Fills absent settings and the source priority list, overwriting nothing | [scripts/db-seed.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L1-L5) |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint, then the type check | [package.json:19-20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L19-L20) |
| `npm run typecheck` | The TypeScript check alone, with no output files | [package.json:20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L20) |
| `npm run test`, `npm run test:watch` | Vitest, once or watching | [package.json:21-22](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L21-L22) |
| `postinstall` | Runs automatically after `npm install`; generates the Prisma client | [package.json:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L7) |

`scripts/db-migrate-data.ts` is not an npm command. It is the one-time move of data from the old database, which reads `DATABASE_URL` from the environment ([scripts/db-migrate-data.ts:277](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate-data.ts#L277)).

### Shared start-up check

Every command that reads or writes data runs the same first step: compare the database to the code, and stop with a three-line message on a mismatch ([scripts/job-search.ts:49-52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L49-L52), [scripts/change-status.ts:115-118](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L115-L118)). The dashboard does the check inside its server because a dashboard must refuse to listen, not just exit ([scripts/serve.ts:6-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L6-L8)).

## Skills

### Summary

| Skill | When it runs | What it does | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job-search` | Only when the user invokes it (`disable-model-invocation`) | Runs the pipeline, reports every error and warning, pastes the summary, scores, then starts the dashboard | [.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L1-L4) |
| `score-backlog` | After a job search, or when the user asks to score | Gathers, researches each company, scores jobs, saves | [.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L1-L4) |
| `change-status` | Only on user request | Finds each job, then writes its new status | [.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md:1-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L1-L9) |
| `add-external-jobs` | Only on user request | Reads pasted links, runs only those jobs through the steps, scores, and reports where each landed | [.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md:1-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md#L1-L9) |
| `generate-resume` | Only on user request | Looks up a job, reads its live posting, picks resume items from an inventory, renders a PDF | [.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md:1-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L1-L10) |

### job-search

Five phases: run the pipeline, read the output, report, score, show results ([.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:11-55](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L11-L55)). It forbids describing the command's internals and forbids running any part of the pipeline separately ([.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L19)). The reason for pasting the summary verbatim is stated in the skill: the user never sees the command's output, so the paste is the only copy ([.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L42)). A test reads the skill file and checks that it names the `Run: ` line and passes the identifier on ([scripts/run-identifier-skills.test.ts:19-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/run-identifier-skills.test.ts#L19-L25)).

### score-backlog

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant S as score-backlog skill
    participant G as score:gather
    participant H as Helper agents
    participant V as score:save
    participant DB as pipeline.db
    S->>G: npm run score:gather -- --out FILE
    G->>DB: Read unscored jobs and companies
    G-->>S: FILE with runId, jobs, companies, warnings, failure
    S->>H: One helper per company, with company-rubric.md
    H-->>S: JSON scores with a guessed flag
    S->>H: Jobs in groups of 10, or one helper per job with no description
    H-->>S: alignment_score and rationale
    S->>V: npm run score:save -- --in ANSWERS
    V->>DB: Write scores through the shared save code
    S->>V: Last batch with --summary
    V-->>S: Summary block
```

<!-- Sources: .claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:17-126, scripts/score-gather.ts:27-41, scripts/score-save.ts:45-48 -->

Key rules from the skill: one helper per company because scoring a company means live web research ([.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L42)). Jobs with the posting's words go to helpers ten at a time. Jobs without them get one helper each, because that helper must open the posting first ([.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:69-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L69-L70)). It reads a private profile and two rubrics ([.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L65)). When no public information exists for a category, the rubric awards a 3 and the helper sets `guessed` to true ([.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L57)). See [Scoring](../deep-dive/agent-workflows/scoring.md).

### change-status

The skill maps each requested status to the list of statuses worth searching. For example, `app. sent` only searches `backlog`, while `rejected` searches the five active statuses ([.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md:33-39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L33-L39)). It never passes a role to the lookup, because the user writes shorthand that no stored title contains ([.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md:18](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L18)). If a job has no employer on file, the command holds it back and the skill asks the user for the name ([.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md:72-82](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L72-L82)). See [Status Change and Work Log](../deep-dive/agent-workflows/status-change-and-work-log.md).

### add-external-jobs

The skill reads each pasted posting for a title, employer, and description. It sets aside any link that shows a sign-in wall or a bot check and asks the user for the title and employer ([.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md:26-31](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md#L26-L31)). It writes a submission file, runs `npm run add-external-jobs -- --in FILE`, then invokes `score-backlog` and reports where each job landed ([.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md:36-49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md#L36-L49)). It forbids running `npm run job-search` beside it ([.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md:17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md#L17)). See [External Jobs and Resumes](../deep-dive/agent-workflows/external-jobs-and-resumes.md).

### generate-resume

It restricts itself to a short list of allowed tools ([.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md:11-19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L11-L19)). Its rule is "pick-only": no resume text is written or edited, only which inventory items are shown ([.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md:26](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L26)). It uses `find-jobs` to pick the job and `fetch-rendered-page` to read the live posting ([.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md:38-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L38-L72)).

## Execution policy pattern

Four of the skills open with an "Execution Policy" list of things never to do. It is how the owner keeps an agent from improvising. Examples: do not change a status without running the lookup first ([.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md:15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L15)), do not score after a stopped run ([.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md#L19)), and ask the user before deviating from any step.

## Choosing what to run

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q{"What do you want?"}
    Q -->|Find and rank new jobs| A["job-search skill"]
    Q -->|Add links you found elsewhere| B["add-external-jobs skill"]
    Q -->|A job moved: applied, rejected, interview| C["change-status skill"]
    Q -->|Score what is unscored| D["score-backlog skill"]
    Q -->|Tailored PDF resume| E["generate-resume skill"]
    Q -->|New parser shipped| F["recover-unparseable-jobs command"]
    Q -->|Look at results| G["serve command"]
    classDef default fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```

## Other files in the skills folder

The four loose `.md` files in `.claude/skills/` (`debug-issue`, `explore-codebase`, `refactor-safely`, `review-changes`) are guides for the code-graph tool, not part of the job search ([.claude/skills/debug-issue.md:1-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/debug-issue.md#L1-L8)).
