## Job statuses

There are twelve. They are declared once so a typo cannot create a state no query reads ([lib/utils/job-status.ts:22-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L22-L23)). The table shows which named lists each status belongs to.

| Status | Active | Work log | Ruled out | Rechecked on re-add | Who normally sets it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backlog` | | | | | Promotion, or letting an added job through |
| `expired` | | | yes | yes | Backlog cleanup, classification, or the parser for a dead page |
| `too far` | | | yes | yes | Classification |
| `won't apply` | | | yes | | The user |
| `unresolvable` | | | yes | yes | Resolution |
| `unparseable` | | | yes | yes | The parser |
| `rejected` | | | yes | | The user |
| `app. sent` | yes | yes | | | The user |
| `screening` | yes | yes | | | The user |
| `interview` | yes | yes | | | The user |
| `test` | yes | | | | The user |
| `offer` | yes | | | | The user |

<!-- Sources: lib/utils/job-status.ts:8-14, lib/utils/job-status.ts:24-37, lib/utils/job-status.ts:49-53, lib/utils/job-status.ts:67-74, lib/utils/job-status.ts:84-89, .claude/rules/part-ownership.md:44-46 -->

| List | Meaning and why it is separate | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ACTIVE_STATUSES` | Applied and not rejected. The row is frozen except for its status, and save refuses to delete it | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:1-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L1-L14) |
| `WORK_LOG_STATUSES` | Texas counts activities, not job states, so `test` and `offer` are active without being activities. Kept in one file so the two lists cannot drift | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:44-53](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L44-L53) |
| `RULED_OUT_STATUSES` | Read by the dashboard to show disqualified jobs | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:61-74](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L61-L74) |
| `RECHECKED_STATUSES` | Verdicts the pipeline reached itself. Adding the link again reruns those checks | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:81-89](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L81-L89) |

The three work log statuses map to the commission's own wording: "Applied for job", "Had phone screen", "Had interview" ([lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts:10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L10), [lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts:17-21](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L17-L21)). The rule for who sets a status: a step sets only the status that names its own outcome ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:44-46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L44-L46)).

### How a job moves

The state diagram shows the usual moves, drawn from the "who sets a status" rule and the skills. It is not a full list of every allowed transition.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> backlog: collected
    backlog --> unresolvable: resolution fails
    backlog --> unparseable: parser fails
    backlog --> expired: too old or dead page
    backlog --> toofar: too far away
    backlog --> appsent: user applies
    appsent --> screening
    screening --> interview
    interview --> test
    test --> offer
    appsent --> rejected
    unparseable --> backlog: new parser recovers it
    expired --> backlog: reposted job promoted
    classDef dark fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class backlog, unresolvable, unparseable, expired, toofar, appsent, screening, interview, test, offer, rejected dark
```

<!-- Sources: .claude/rules/part-ownership.md:44-46, .claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md:33-39, scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts:1-17, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:579-604 -->

`toofar` and `appsent` are diagram names for `too far` and `app. sent`. The change-status skill lets `screening`, `interview`, `test`, `offer` and `rejected` be set from any of the five active statuses ([.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md:36-37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L36-L37)), so the order drawn above is the usual path, not a rule.

### Does a status write a work log entry?

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S["A status is set by hand"] --> W{"isWorkLogStatus?"}
    W -->|app. sent| E1["Entry: Applied for job"]
    W -->|screening| E2["Entry: Had phone screen"]
    W -->|interview| E3["Entry: Had interview"]
    W -->|any other status| N["No entry written"]
    classDef default fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```

<!-- Sources: lib/utils/job-status.ts:49-59, lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts:17-30 -->

`activityFromStatus` is the function that returns the wording, and it returns nothing for any status outside the three ([lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts:27-30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L27-L30)). See [Status Change and Work Log](../deep-dive/agent-workflows/status-change-and-work-log.md).

## Trace steps

A trace row records what happened to one job or company at one pipeline position. Rows feed the run summary and change nothing ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:31](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L31)). A handler's step name must be one of the values in the `Trace` model comment ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L41)).

| Order | Step | Written by | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `backlog_cleanup` | Old job and company sweep | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:222-248](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L222-L248) |
| 2 | `post_backlog_cleanup_save` | Save after cleanup | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:262-271](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L262-L271) |
| 3 | `collection` | Collectors | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:276-287](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L276-L287) |
| 4 to 7 | `post_collection_normalization`, `_association`, `_dedupe`, `_save` | Tidy, attach a company, remove duplicates, write | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:307-360](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L307-L360) |
| 8 | `resolution` | Follow links in a visible browser | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:390-403](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L390-L403) |
| 9 to 10 | `post_resolution_dedupe`, `post_resolution_save` | Dedupe and write | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:408-433](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L408-L433) |
| 11 | `parsing` | Read each posting | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:480-489](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L480-L489) |
| 12 to 15 | `post_parsing_normalization`, `_association`, `_dedupe`, `_save` | Tidy, attach, dedupe, write | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:507-550](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L507-L550) |
| 16 to 17 | `promotion`, `post_promotion_save` | Reposted jobs return to backlog | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:586-603](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L586-L603) |
| 18 to 19 | `classification`, `post_classification_save` | Close enough? Expired? | [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:612-635](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L612-L635) |
| 20 | `scoring` | Scoring commands, not the pipeline | [lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts:162](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L162) |
| 21 | `company_promotion` | Scoring commands, promote a scored employer | [lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts:435](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L435) |
| extra | `post_parsing_let_through`, `post_classification_let_through` | Only when adding jobs by hand | [lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts:218-244](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L218-L244) |

The list is written out in the schema comment ([prisma/schema.prisma:362-368](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L362-L368)). The `Trace` table keeps rows free of any link to a job, so a trace outlives the job it describes ([prisma/schema.prisma:623-625](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L623-L625)). One schema comment says "Only a job search writes traces", but scoring also writes them under the same run id ([prisma/schema.prisma:360-361](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L360-L361), [prisma/schema.prisma:377-380](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L377-L380)). See [Tracing and Run Summary](../deep-dive/architecture/tracing-and-run-summary.md).

## Settings

There is one row in the `Setting` table, with `id` 1 ([prisma/schema.prisma:275-276](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L275-L276)). `db:seed` fills any empty column and never overwrites ([scripts/db-seed.ts:129-131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L129-L131)). A getter on the settings service throws when its column is empty, which stops the run ([lib/services/settings-service.ts:39-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L39-L41)).

| Setting | Type | Seed default | What it controls | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search_terms` | list of text | Product Design, UX, Founding Design | Terms every collector searches | [prisma/schema.prisma:278](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L278), [scripts/db-seed.ts:12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L12) |
| `location` | text | `78701` | Home location every job is measured against | [prisma/schema.prisma:280](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L280), [scripts/db-seed.ts:13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L13) |
| `radius` | whole number | 30 | Search radius in miles | [prisma/schema.prisma:282](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L282), [scripts/db-seed.ts:14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L14) |
| `expiry_threshold` | whole number | 8 | Days old before a posting counts as expired | [prisma/schema.prisma:285](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L285), [scripts/db-seed.ts:15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L15) |
| `title_head_nouns` | list | designer, engineer, manager, and others | Words that name a job; tells the title rule which part is the role | [prisma/schema.prisma:289](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L289), [scripts/db-seed.ts:18-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L18-L23) |
| `title_levels` | list of objects | Intern through Chief | Each stored seniority spelling and the spellings that match it | [prisma/schema.prisma:293](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L293), [scripts/db-seed.ts:30-44](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L30-L44) |
| `title_suffixes` | list | `-er`, `-or`, `-ist`, and others | Word endings that name a person doing a job, used when no head noun matched | [prisma/schema.prisma:297](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L297), [scripts/db-seed.ts:47](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L47) |
| `title_removal_words` | list | w2, c2h, evergreen | Words removed from a title's team part only | [prisma/schema.prisma:300](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L300), [scripts/db-seed.ts:51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L51) |
| `source_priority_list` | ordered list | `collector:user` first, then parsers, collectors, general parser | Which source wins a contested field; the owner reorders it | [prisma/schema.prisma:309](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L309), [scripts/db-seed.ts:88-95](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L88-L95) |
| `identifying_query_values` | list | `opportunityid` | Link query values kept when matching links; all others are dropped | [prisma/schema.prisma:315](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L315), [scripts/db-seed.ts:68](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L68) |
| `resolution_fast_concurrency` | whole number | 3 | Jobs the fast lane resolves at once | [prisma/schema.prisma:327](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L327), [scripts/db-seed.ts:52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L52) |
| `resolution_slow_concurrency` | whole number | 1 | Jobs the slow lane resolves at once (hosts that already refused us) | [prisma/schema.prisma:330](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L330), [scripts/db-seed.ts:53](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L53) |
| `resolution_slow_pause_seconds` | whole number | 12 | Wait between slow-lane jobs | [prisma/schema.prisma:335](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L335), [scripts/db-seed.ts:54](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L54) |
| `repost_gap_days` | whole number | 3 | How far apart two dates must be before a job counts as reposted | [prisma/schema.prisma:340](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L340), [scripts/db-seed.ts:55](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L55) |
| `promotion_threshold` | decimal | 3.5 | Average of a company's four scores must exceed this before its board joins a polling list | [prisma/schema.prisma:345](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L345), [scripts/db-seed.ts:60](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L60) |

| `guessed_score_expiry_days` | whole number | 30 | Days a guessed category stands | [prisma/schema.prisma:352](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L352), [scripts/db-seed.ts:64](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L64) |

The seed also lists the setting names inside its patch type ([scripts/db-seed.ts:101-118](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L101-L118)), which must stay in step with the defaults object. See [Data Model](../deep-dive/data/data-model.md) for the other tables.

## Deep Dive


<doc title="Collection" path="./deep-dive/pipeline/collection.md">
# Collection

## Overview

Collection is the first step of every job search. Its job is to build the first job list. Nothing earlier exists, so this is the one handler that takes no list as input ([lib/handlers/collection.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L1-L5)).

The design has one rule behind it. Only collectors and parsers know about a particular job site. Every later step works on a job's data alone and cannot tell where the job came from ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L9)). So each collector hides one source's quirks behind one small contract, and the handler knows only that contract.

A collector gathers raw jobs and every field its source hands over for free. It writes each into a `raw_` field exactly as it arrived. It does not interpret anything ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L33)).

`docs/architecture.md` describes seven collectors. The code lists 14 ([lib/collectors/registry.ts:19-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/registry.ts#L19-L34)). This page follows the code.

### At a glance

| Component | Responsibility | Key file | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Collector` contract | The two-method shape every collector implements: a `name` and a `collect` function | `lib/collectors/collector.ts` | [lib/collectors/collector.ts:28-33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/collector.ts#L28-L33) |
| `COLLECTORS` registry | The ordered list of collectors a search runs. Being listed here is the only way to join | `lib/collectors/registry.ts` | [lib/collectors/registry.ts:19-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/registry.ts#L19-L34) |
| `collectJobs` handler | Runs each collector in turn, isolates failures, tags each job, runs the usability check | `lib/handlers/collection.ts` | [lib/handlers/collection.ts:54-175](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L54-L175) |
| `unusableReason` | Says why a job cannot travel, or returns null when it can | `lib/utils/job-usable.ts` | [lib/utils/job-usable.ts:45-92](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-usable.ts#L45-L92) |
| `readAtsBoards` | Reads the list of boards one ATS collector polls from the database | `lib/collectors/ats-boards.ts` | [lib/collectors/ats-boards.ts:25-36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/ats-boards.ts#L25-L36) |

| `fetchWithTimeout`, `safeJson`, `httpError` | Shared request helpers: a 15 second timeout, a named JSON failure, a readable status message | `lib/utils/fetch-utils.ts` | [lib/utils/fetch-utils.ts:4-42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/fetch-utils.ts#L4-L42) |

## Architecture

The handler sits between the registry and the rest of the pipeline. It hands every collector a context with the settings, the ATS slug service (the table of known hiring-system boards) and a job limit ([lib/collectors/collector.ts:9-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/collector.ts#L9-L17)). A collector hands back jobs, errors and warnings, however its run went ([lib/collectors/collector.ts:22-26](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/collector.ts#L22-L26)).

## The 14 collectors

The three kinds differ in how they reach the source and in what the source already tells them.

- **Aggregator APIs** search many employers at once. Their links are redirects, so the job still needs resolution ([lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:56-57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/adzuna.ts#L56-L57)).
- **ATS board pollers** read one employer's board on a hiring system such as Greenhouse. The board list comes from the database. The link they build is already the employer's own posting, so the job is marked resolved ([lib/collectors/greenhouse.ts:22-36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/greenhouse.ts#L22-L36)).
- **Page readers** fetch a website's results page and read the job cards off it ([lib/tools/fetch-page.ts:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/fetch-page.ts#L1-L3)).

"Arrives resolved" means the collector sets `is_resolved: true` and fills `resolved_url`. The [resolution step](./resolution.md) then skips the job.

| # | Collector | Kind of source | How it reaches the source | Arrives resolved? | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `adzuna` | Aggregator API | GET to Adzuna's search API. Two searches per term: remote nationwide, and anchored to the user's location and radius. Needs `ADZUNA_APP_ID` and `ADZUNA_API_KEY` | No. The link is a redirect | [lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:119-184](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/adzuna.ts#L119-L184), [lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/adzuna.ts#L72) |
| 2 | `jsearch` | Aggregator API | GET to JSearch through RapidAPI. All terms fold into one query, so a run is two requests: remote and local. Needs `RAPIDAPI_KEY` | No. The link is a redirect | [lib/collectors/jsearch.ts:112-157](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/jsearch.ts#L112-L157), [lib/collectors/jsearch.ts:77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/jsearch.ts#L77) |
| 3 | `greenhouse` | ATS board poller | GET to the Greenhouse boards API for each board slug | Yes | [lib/collectors/greenhouse.ts:39-91](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/greenhouse.ts#L39-L91), [lib/collectors/greenhouse.ts:33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/greenhouse.ts#L33) |
| 4 | `lever` | ATS board poller | GET to the Lever postings API for each board slug. The reply names no employer, so the job keeps the slug | Yes | [lib/collectors/lever.ts:36-52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/lever.ts#L36-L52), [lib/collectors/lever.ts:29](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/lever.ts#L29) |
| 5 | `ashby` | ATS board poller | GET to Ashby's job board API for each slug. Ashby supplies the posting link itself | Yes | [lib/collectors/ashby.ts:42-58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/ashby.ts#L42-L58), [lib/collectors/ashby.ts:35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/ashby.ts#L35) |
| 6 | `dribbble` | Page reader | Fetches Dribbble's jobs page twice per term (location, remote) and reads the cards | Yes. The card link is the posting | [lib/collectors/dribbble.ts:76-169](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/dribbble.ts#L76-L169), [lib/collectors/dribbble.ts:70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/dribbble.ts#L70) |
| 7 | `uiuxjobsboard` | Page reader | Fetches one page per matched category. Search terms are matched to the site's six fixed categories, not sent as a query | No | [lib/collectors/uiuxjobsboard.ts:61-162](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/uiuxjobsboard.ts#L61-L162), [lib/collectors/uiuxjobsboard.ts:55](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/uiuxjobsboard.ts#L55) |
| 8 | `workday` | ATS board poller | POST to Workday's job-search endpoint, one search per term, 20 results a page, up to 50 pages | Yes | [lib/collectors/workday.ts:88-153](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/workday.ts#L88-L153), [lib/collectors/workday.ts:46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/workday.ts#L46) |
| 9 | `ultipro` | ATS board poller | POST to UltiPro's list endpoint. It takes no search text, so each board is read in full, 200 jobs a page, then filtered | Yes | [lib/collectors/ultipro.ts:87-131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/ultipro.ts#L87-L131), [lib/collectors/ultipro.ts:44](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/ultipro.ts#L44) |
| 10 | `gem` | ATS board poller | GET to the Gem job-board API. The whole list arrives in one reply. The reply names no employer | Yes | [lib/collectors/gem.ts:38-54](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/gem.ts#L38-L54), [lib/collectors/gem.ts:31](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/gem.ts#L31) |
| 11 | `smartrecruiters` | ATS board poller | GET to the SmartRecruiters postings API, 100 per page, until a page is empty or the total is reached | Yes | [lib/collectors/smartrecruiters.ts:76-119](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/smartrecruiters.ts#L76-L119), [lib/collectors/smartrecruiters.ts:40](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/smartrecruiters.ts#L40) |
| 12 | `bamboohr` | ATS board poller | GET to the board's careers list address on `{slug}.bamboohr.com`, with an explicit accept header so it answers with data and not a web page | Yes | [lib/collectors/bamboohr.ts:43-59](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/bamboohr.ts#L43-L59), [lib/collectors/bamboohr.ts:36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/bamboohr.ts#L36) |
| 13 | `rippling` | ATS board poller | GET to Rippling's board API. The listing names no employer, so the parser fills the name later | Yes | [lib/collectors/rippling.ts:39-55](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/rippling.ts#L39-L55), [lib/collectors/rippling.ts:32](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/rippling.ts#L32) |
| 14 | `workable` | ATS board poller | GET to Workable's widget API. The widget names the employer, so the job keeps both the name and the slug | Yes | [lib/collectors/workable.ts:46-62](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/workable.ts#L46-L62), [lib/collectors/workable.ts:39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/workable.ts#L39) |

Totals: 2 aggregators, 10 ATS pollers, 2 page readers. 11 of the 14 arrive resolved. The three that do not are `adzuna`, `jsearch` and `uiuxjobsboard`. The `uiuxjobsboard` card builder leaves `resolved_url` unset ([lib/collectors/uiuxjobsboard.ts:45-59](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/uiuxjobsboard.ts#L45-L59)). Dribbble sets it, with this reason in the code: three listings were measured sharing one "View job" link, and following them would give three different jobs one resolved link, which dedupe reads as proof that they are one job ([lib/collectors/dribbble.ts:54-58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/dribbble.ts#L54-L58)).

Every collector's `name` matches its filename, and it joins the pipeline only by being listed in the registry ([.claude/rules/sources.md:11-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/sources.md#L11-L14)). Adding or renaming one also means running `npm run db:seed`, so the new name joins the source priority list used by [dedupe](./dedupe-and-save.md) ([.claude/rules/source-registry.md:7-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/source-registry.md#L7-L9)).

### How an ATS collector decides what to poll

An ATS board poller does not hold a list of boards in code. The list lives in the ATS slug table. A row that carries a collector name is a board polled every run. A row with none is only a board the company is known to post on ([lib/collectors/ats-boards.ts:14-19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/ats-boards.ts#L14-L19)).

`readAtsBoards` turns the rows into boards. If a collector has none, it returns a warning, so a collector switched off on purpose can be told apart from one emptied by accident ([lib/collectors/ats-boards.ts:21-35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/ats-boards.ts#L21-L35)). This also follows the project rule that knowledge about a job site is data, never code. See [Project Rules](../quality/project-rules.md).

Most boards cannot be searched, so the collector fetches the whole reply and filters titles itself. `matchesSearchTerms` stems both the title and the term, then needs every word of at least one term to be present in the title ([lib/utils/search-term-analyzer.ts:27-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/search-term-analyzer.ts#L27-L41)). Words of three characters or fewer are not stemmed, because the stemmer turns "uxs" into "ux" ([lib/utils/search-term-analyzer.ts:7-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/search-term-analyzer.ts#L7-L14)). A blank term never matches, so one stray blank in settings does not match every job ([lib/utils/search-term-analyzer.ts:35-38](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/search-term-analyzer.ts#L35-L38)).

The mapping of a raw posting to job fields lives in a shared `*-fields` util for each hiring system, for example `jobFieldsFromGreenhousePosting`. The collector and the parser both use it, so they cannot disagree about what a field means ([lib/collectors/greenhouse.ts:22-32](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/greenhouse.ts#L22-L32)). See [Parsing](./parsing.md).

### How the page readers stop

Dribbble and the UI/UX Jobs Board share `paginate`. It knows nothing about a browser. The caller supplies a way to read cards and a way to go to the next page ([lib/collectors/paginate.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/paginate.ts#L1-L4)).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Read a page of cards"] --> Fail{"Did the read throw?"}
    Fail -- yes --> WF["Warn, stop: failure"]
    Fail -- no --> Age{"Card age readable?"}
    Age -- no --> WA["Warn, stop: unreadable age"]
    Age -- yes --> Old{"Card at or past<br>the expiry threshold?"}
    Old -- yes --> SO["Stop: threshold"]
    Old -- no --> Keep["Keep card"]
    Keep --> Lim{"Reached the limit?"}
    Lim -- yes --> SL["Stop: limit"]
    Lim -- no --> Empty{"Page had no cards?"}
    Empty -- yes --> SE["Stop: exhausted"]
    Empty -- no --> Next{"Next page exists<br>and under 6 turns?"}
    Next -- yes --> Start
    Next -- no --> SX["Stop: exhausted or ceiling"]

    style Start fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Fail fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Age fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/collectors/paginate.ts:57-59, lib/collectors/paginate.ts:95-195 -->

Two design choices are worth knowing.

- An unreadable age stops the search with a warning. Failing open would let a reworded site rewrite its whole history every run in silence ([lib/collectors/paginate.ts:124-130](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/paginate.ts#L124-L130)).
- Two self-checks guard against a broken card selector. One fires when no cards are found. One fires when fewer than half the matched elements yield a card ([lib/collectors/paginate.ts:177-192](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/paginate.ts#L177-L192)). `noCardsWarnings` then says one line for the whole collector if every search was empty, and one line per search if only some were ([lib/collectors/paginate.ts:208-214](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/paginate.ts#L208-L214)).

Both page readers currently pass `advance: async () => false`, because each site serves its whole result set on one page. The paging code stays wired up for the day that changes ([lib/collectors/dribbble.ts:125-128](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/dribbble.ts#L125-L128), [lib/collectors/uiuxjobsboard.ts:117-121](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/uiuxjobsboard.ts#L117-L121)).

The UI/UX Jobs Board browses by six fixed categories. `matchCategories` picks a category when every word of a search term appears in its label ([lib/utils/match-categories.ts:10-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/match-categories.ts#L10-L13)). If no category matches, the collector returns a warning, not an error ([lib/collectors/uiuxjobsboard.ts:73-78](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/uiuxjobsboard.ts#L73-L78)).

## The collection handler

`collectJobs` runs the collectors one after another in registry order. Running in sequence means a job list reads the way the run happened, and one collector's failure cannot cancel another's work ([lib/handlers/collection.ts:68-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L68-L70)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Orch as Orchestrator
    participant H as collectJobs
    participant C as Collector
    participant U as unusableReason
    participant T as TraceService

    Orch->>H: options with collectors, runId, collectedAt, limit
    loop each collector in order
        H->>C: collect with settings, atsSlugs, limit
        alt collector throws
            C-->>H: exception
            H->>H: record an error, log "failed", move on
        else collector returns
            C-->>H: jobs, errors, warnings
            loop each job
                H->>H: assign id with crypto.randomUUID
                H->>T: write job_collected
                H->>U: check the job
                alt unusable
                    U-->>H: reason code and message
                    H->>T: write job_abandoned with reason
                    H->>H: add a dropped warning
                else usable
                    H->>H: set collector name and collected_at
                    opt is_resolved is true
                        H->>T: write job_resolved, reason collector_provided
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
    H-->>Orch: jobs, errors, warnings
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/collection.ts:54-175, lib/utils/job-usable.ts:45-92 -->

### What the handler guarantees

| Behaviour | Why it exists | Source |
|---|---|---|
| A thrown collector becomes one error. The others still run | One source dropping out must not cost the run the others | [lib/handlers/collection.ts:165-171](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L165-L171) |
| The log says "failed", not "found=0" | Zero would read as a quiet week when the collector actually fell over | [lib/handlers/collection.ts:168-170](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L168-L170) |
| Each job gets a fresh id the moment it enters the loop | A job dropped by the usability check still needs an id to name it in a trace event | [lib/handlers/collection.ts:86-90](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L86-L90) |
| The handler writes `collector` and `collected_at` onto a copy | Collection is the authority on which collector found a job. No collector can supply the first-seen date | [lib/handlers/collection.ts:122-131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L122-L131) |
| `collected_at` arrives as an argument | Collection reads no clock, so one run shares a single date and a test can pin it | [lib/handlers/collection.ts:21-24](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L21-L24) |
| A `limit` of 0 returns at once | `??` is used, not `||`, because 0 is a real value meaning collect nothing | [lib/handlers/collection.ts:55-66](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L55-L66) |
| A `job_resolved` trace row is written for collector-resolved jobs | "Saved minus resolved" would count two different populations, because resolution also handles jobs an earlier run collected | [lib/handlers/collection.ts:133-147](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L133-L147) |
| The log shows `kept=` and `dropped=` | A count of what the collector handed over would hide the jobs that did not survive | [lib/handlers/collection.ts:159-164](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L159-L164) |

Progress lines go to stderr by default, so a job list printed on stdout stays clean ([lib/handlers/collection.ts:35-37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L35-L37)). The trace service never throws, so a failed diagnostics write cannot cancel a run ([lib/handlers/collection.ts:29-32](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L29-L32)). See [Tracing and Run Summary](../architecture/tracing-and-run-summary.md).

## The usability check

A job that cannot travel is dropped at collection. Otherwise it would fail somewhere later, where what went wrong is harder to read ([lib/handlers/collection.ts:102-103](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L102-L103)). The rule is: a field that is empty and needed, or filled and unusable, drops the job. A field that is empty and merely expected is fine ([lib/utils/job-usable.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-usable.ts#L1-L4)).

| Code | Fails when | Why it matters downstream | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_original_url` | The link is missing or blank | Nothing can resolve, parse, dedupe by URL or apply without a link | [lib/utils/job-usable.ts:46-50](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-usable.ts#L46-L50) |
| `original_url_not_a_url` | The `URL` constructor rejects it | The constructor is the one already-correct answer to what counts as a link | [lib/utils/job-usable.ts:52-62](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-usable.ts#L52-L62) |
| `no_raw_title` | The title is missing or blank | Classification, content dedupe and scoring all read the title | [lib/utils/job-usable.ts:64-67](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-usable.ts#L64-L67) |
| `no_company_identity` | Both the company name and the board slug are missing | Either one alone is enough, because association matches slug first and name second | [lib/utils/job-usable.ts:69-78](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-usable.ts#L69-L78) |
| `posting_date_unparseable` | The date is set and is an Invalid Date | An invalid date would travel unnoticed and throw at save time | [lib/utils/job-usable.ts:33-39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-usable.ts#L33-L39), [lib/utils/job-usable.ts:80-82](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-usable.ts#L80-L82) |
| `posting_updated_date_unparseable` | Same, for the updated date | Same | [lib/utils/job-usable.ts:84-89](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-usable.ts#L84-L89) |

An absent date is fine. JSearch leaves `posting_date` off some postings by design, and a parser fills it later ([lib/utils/job-usable.ts:33-36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-usable.ts#L33-L36)). The code, not the message, is what gets counted, because a message can embed a value such as the bad URL and split one failure into many groups ([lib/utils/job-usable.ts:7-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-usable.ts#L7-L9)).

A dropped job is named by its title or its link, whichever survived. The code uses `||` because a blank title is one of the reasons a job gets dropped ([lib/handlers/collection.ts:46-52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/collection.ts#L46-L52)). The next stage is [Normalization and Association](./normalization-and-association.md), which reads the company name or slug that this check guarantees.

## Failure model

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Running
    Running --> CollectorFailed: collect throws
    Running --> Returned: collect returns
    Returned --> JobDropped: usability check fails
    Returned --> JobKept: usability check passes
    Returned --> Warned: collector warnings
    CollectorFailed --> NextCollector: error recorded
    JobDropped --> NextCollector: warning recorded
    JobKept --> NextCollector
    Warned --> NextCollector
    NextCollector --> Running: more collectors
    NextCollector --> [*]: none left

    style Running fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Returned fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style NextCollector fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style CollectorFailed fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style JobDropped fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style Warned fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style JobKept fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/collection.ts:70-171, lib/collectors/collector.ts:19-26 -->

Collectors also degrade on their own. Inside a collector, a dead board or a dead search is a warning, not an error, so the other boards still get their turn ([lib/collectors/greenhouse.ts:54-69](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/greenhouse.ts#L54-L69), [lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:78-83](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/adzuna.ts#L78-L83)). Missing API keys are the exception. `adzuna` and `jsearch` return an error naming the missing variable ([lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:123-131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/adzuna.ts#L123-L131), [lib/collectors/jsearch.ts:116-123](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/jsearch.ts#L116-L123)). Errors and warnings are shown in the run summary. See [Job Search Run](../architecture/job-search-run.md).

## Things the code leaves open

- Adzuna returns one fixed page of 50. When more matched, the collector warns and does not fetch further pages. Whether to page is left until these numbers are read ([lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:103-113](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/adzuna.ts#L103-L113)).
- The code that saves a page fixture for the two page readers is commented out on purpose. A real job search used to overwrite the saved fixture and dirty the working tree each run ([lib/collectors/dribbble.ts:147-163](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/dribbble.ts#L147-L163)).
- Adzuna's minimum salary is an inline constant and not a setting. The comment says it moves to settings the day a second source needs it ([lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:10-22](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/adzuna.ts#L10-L22)).

<doc title="Normalization and Association" path="./deep-dive/pipeline/normalization-and-association.md">
# Normalization and Association

## Overview

Collectors write whatever their source sent, in the source's own spelling. One source says "Sr. UX Designer (m/w/d)", another says "Senior UX Designer". One says "On-site", another "in office". Later steps cannot compare jobs that read differently. They also cannot tell whether two jobs belong to one employer when each source spells the employer differently.

Two handlers fix this, and they always run as a pair.

- **Normalization** reshapes data that is already there into the tidy fields the rest of the app reads. It never goes looking for a value that is missing ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:1-12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L1-L12)). That is the line between reshaping and parsing, written in the project rule ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:48-50](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L48-L50)).
- **Association** decides which employer each job belongs to, and creates the employer row when none exists ([lib/handlers/association.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L1-L4)).

They run in this order because dedupe matches on company, and a newly collected job has no company row yet ([lib/handlers/association.ts:3-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L3-L4)). Both run twice per search: once after collection and once after parsing. See [Job Search Run](../architecture/job-search-run.md) for the full order.

### At a glance

| Component | Responsibility | Key file | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `normalizeJobs` | Step wrapper. Calls `normalizeJob` per entry, writes trace rows, folds warnings | `lib/handlers/normalization.ts` | [lib/handlers/normalization.ts:220-260](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L220-L260) |
| `normalizeJob` | Routes each raw field to the util that owns it. Returns the tidied job and its events | `lib/handlers/normalization.ts` | [lib/handlers/normalization.ts:40-201](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L40-L201) |
| `normalizeTitle` | Rebuilds a raw title as `{level} {role} - {team}` | `lib/utils/title.ts` | [lib/utils/title.ts:275-340](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L275-L340) |
| `normalizeSalary` | Turns a raw salary envelope into a low, a high and a period word | `lib/utils/salary.ts` | [lib/utils/salary.ts:55-86](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/salary.ts#L55-L86) |
| `splitLocation` | Cuts a location string into single places and lifts out work modes | `lib/utils/split-location.ts` | [lib/utils/split-location.ts:53-77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/split-location.ts#L53-L77) |
| `normalizeModeList` | Maps each source's mode spelling onto three words and drops unknown words | `lib/utils/work-mode-list.ts` | [lib/utils/work-mode-list.ts:29-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-mode-list.ts#L29-L41) |
| `normalizeCompanyName` | Cosmetic tidy of the employer name | `lib/utils/company-name.ts` | [lib/utils/company-name.ts:13-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/company-name.ts#L13-L23) |
| `associateCompanies` | Attaches each job to a company, one at a time | `lib/handlers/association.ts` | [lib/handlers/association.ts:221-303](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L221-L303) |
| `companyMatchKey` | Builds the key that two spellings of one employer share | `lib/utils/company-match-key.ts` | [lib/utils/company-match-key.ts:44-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/company-match-key.ts#L44-L70) |
| `AtsSlugService.record` | Writes down that a company posts on a hiring-system board | `lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts` | [lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:66-94](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L66-L94) |

<!-- Sources: lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:307-358, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:507-548 -->

The names on the boxes are the step names the orchestrator passes in. They are the labels written into trace rows ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:312](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L312), [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:326](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L326), [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:512](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L512), [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:523](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L523)). One handler serves both positions, as the handler contract requires ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L19)).

## Normalization

### Why it recomputes every time

Every present field is recomputed from its raw source on every call. The code does not check whether the target is already filled. Two results follow. A second pass over unchanged raw data ends on exactly the same job. And a pass after parsing can improve a figure the first pass got wrong or left out ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:6-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L6-L10)).

The one exception is a raw field with nothing in it. It is left alone, because finding a missing value is parsing ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:10-12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L10-L12)). Each route has its own empty check, so an empty raw value never wipes a value an earlier pass wrote. Examples are an empty title ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:49-52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L49-L52)) and an empty salary envelope ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:66-71](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L66-L71)).

### The five routes

| Raw field | Tidied field | Util | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `raw_title` | `title` | `normalizeTitle` | Finds the job noun, pulls out a seniority level, treats the rest as team | [lib/handlers/normalization.ts:52-64](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L52-L64) |
| `raw_salary` | `salary_low`, `salary_high`, `salary_period` | `normalizeSalary` | Whole currency units and a period word | [lib/handlers/normalization.ts:71-106](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L71-L106) |
| `raw_location_list` | `normalized_location_list` | `splitLocation` | Cuts at every delimiter, pools places, de-duplicates | [lib/handlers/normalization.ts:114-147](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L114-L147) |
| `raw_mode_list` plus modes found in locations | `normalized_mode_list` | `normalizeModeList` | Maps spellings to `remote`, `hybrid`, `in-person` | [lib/handlers/normalization.ts:149-185](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L149-L185) |
| `raw_company_name` | `raw_company_name` (overwritten) | `normalizeCompanyName` | Trims, collapses spaces, drops trailing punctuation | [lib/handlers/normalization.ts:188-198](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L188-L198) |

`normalizeJob` works on a shallow copy, so the job passed in is never changed ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:44-46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L44-L46)).

### Title: `{level} {role} - {team}`

The goal is that the same role published by two sources reads the same ([lib/utils/title.ts:1-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L1-L8)). The vocabularies are passed in by the caller: head nouns, levels, suffixes and removal words. The util reads no settings and no database ([lib/utils/title.ts:12-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L12-L17)). The orchestrator reads them from the settings service before the handlers run, so a missing vocabulary stops the whole run and does not read as one handler failing ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:294-302](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L294-L302)).

The steps, in order:

1. **Tidy.** Dash and quote variants fold to plain forms. Nine punctuation characters are handled by a fixed list: the full stop is deleted, and the brackets, semicolon and colon become spaces ([lib/utils/title.ts:43-77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L43-L77)).
2. **Cut into segments** at a comma, a pipe, or a dash with a space on either side. A dash glued on both sides, as in "AI-Enabled", stays inside the word ([lib/utils/title.ts:60-63](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L60-L63)).
3. **Drop junk by shape.** A token with digits and no letters is a requisition number. A token of single letters joined by slashes, like "m/w/d", is a gender marker. "UX/UI" survives because a part has more than one letter ([lib/utils/title.ts:84-106](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L84-L106)). Roman numerals are never removed, which keeps "UX Designer II" apart from "UX Designer III" ([lib/utils/title.ts:99-101](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L99-L101)).
4. **Pick the role segment.** It is the last segment holding a job noun. A head noun from the closed list beats a suffix match such as "-er". A segment of only level words is skipped unless it is the only one with a job noun ([lib/utils/title.ts:209-230](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L209-L230)).
5. **Take the level.** The longest run of level words is matched first, so "mid level" is taken whole ([lib/utils/title.ts:156-176](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L156-L176)). The level comes out of the role segment only if a job noun remains, so "Design Director" keeps "Director" ([lib/utils/title.ts:295-308](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L295-L308)).
6. **Everything else is team.** Removal words come out here only. Team items sort alphabetically ([lib/utils/title.ts:324-333](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L324-L333)).

If no job noun is found, the tidied string comes back with `matched: false` and the handler records `missing_role_noun`. It does not guess ([lib/utils/title.ts:286-289](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/title.ts#L286-L289)).

### Salary: whole units and a period word

`normalizeSalary` takes the envelope a collector wrote. It divides figures sent in cents by 100 before rounding, so a fractional total ends on a whole unit ([lib/utils/salary.ts:58-67](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/salary.ts#L58-L67)). A period or currency on its own is not a salary, so no numbers means an empty result ([lib/utils/salary.ts:69-71](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/salary.ts#L69-L71)).

The period rules are strict on purpose:

- An absent period reads as `year`, because Adzuna and Greenhouse publish annual figures without saying so ([lib/utils/salary.ts:41-53](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/salary.ts#L41-L53)).
- A leading count is dropped, so Ashby's "1 YEAR" matches JSearch's "YEAR".
- A word outside the five recognised ones gives `undefined`, never the nearest guess, so a wrong guess never reaches the database ([lib/utils/salary.ts:43-45](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/salary.ts#L43-L45)).

`salary_currency` travels in the envelope but has no column, so it is not stored ([lib/utils/salary.ts:82-83](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/salary.ts#L82-L83)).

The same file also holds `readSalaryFromText`, which reads a range out of a description ([lib/utils/salary.ts:219-229](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/salary.ts#L219-L229)). That one is for parsers. Normalization does not call it, because finding a salary in prose is going looking. See [Parsing](./parsing.md).

### Location and work mode

`splitLocation` cuts at every delimiter and glues nothing back. The comment reports a measurement: across 2,208 real jobs, cutting everywhere gained 32 matches and lost none ([lib/utils/split-location.ts:4-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/split-location.ts#L4-L9)). Pieces that name nothing on a map are kept, because ten of 796 such fragments were genuine local places ([lib/utils/split-location.ts:10-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/split-location.ts#L10-L13)). A small hand-kept list strips filler such as "based in" and noise such as a bare "HQ" ([lib/utils/split-location.ts:32-39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/split-location.ts#L32-L39)).

A work mode named inside a location, such as "Austin (Hybrid)", is lifted out and passed down to the mode route ([lib/utils/split-location.ts:24-28](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/split-location.ts#L24-L28), [lib/handlers/normalization.ts:108-111](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L108-L111)). So the job gets the mode even when the source published no mode words ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:151-156](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L151-L156)).

`normalizeModeList` keeps only words it recognises and drops the rest. The older `work-mode.ts` fallback assumes every word is already recognised because a regex matched it first. Sources send any word they like, so this version must not guess ([lib/utils/work-mode-list.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-mode-list.ts#L1-L6)). Duplicates collapse into one entry ([lib/utils/work-mode-list.ts:35-37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-mode-list.ts#L35-L37)).

### Company name tidy

`normalizeCompanyName` trims, collapses spaces and drops a trailing run of non-letter, non-digit characters. Case and inner spacing are left as the source wrote them, because deciding that two spellings name one employer is a matching judgement that belongs to association ([lib/utils/company-name.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/company-name.ts#L1-L6)). Because the cleaned name overwrites `raw_company_name` and no copy is kept, it must give the same result when run on its own output ([lib/utils/company-name.ts:8-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/company-name.ts#L8-L11)).

### Trace events and warnings

For every field that had a raw value, the handler records whether it came out whole, partial or not at all.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Raw["Field has a raw value?"] -- no --> Skip["Left alone, no event"]
    Raw -- yes --> Run["Run its normalizer"]
    Run --> Kind{"How many parts came out?"}
    Kind -- "all" --> Ok["job_updated<br>reason ..._normalized"]
    Kind -- "some" --> Part["job_updated<br>reason ..._partially_normalized"]
    Kind -- "none" --> Fail["normalization_failed<br>reason ..._unusable or missing_role_noun"]
    Ok --> Trace["Trace row written"]
    Part --> Trace
    Fail --> Trace
    Fail --> Warn{"salary_unusable or<br>work_mode_unusable?"}
    Warn -- yes --> Fold["Folded into one warning<br>per collector and reason"]
    Warn -- no --> Silent["Trace only"]

    style Raw fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Run fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Kind fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Warn fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Trace fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Skip fill:#2d2d3d,stroke:#7a7a8a,color:#e6edf3
    style Silent fill:#2d2d3d,stroke:#7a7a8a,color:#e6edf3
    style Ok fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style Part fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style Fail fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style Fold fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/normalization.ts:52-198, lib/handlers/normalization.ts:238-259, lib/utils/normalization-warnings.ts:17-60 -->

Details worth knowing:

- Salary counts only the three envelope keys that have a column. Counting currency would file every salary with a currency as partly done ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:78-87](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L78-L87)).
- Nothing-normalized is checked first, so an envelope holding only a currency reads as unusable and not as complete on a count of zero out of zero ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:96-105](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L96-L105)).
- Work mode counts recognised raw entries, not output length, so two spellings of one mode still count as both recognised ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:164-171](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L164-L171)).
- Locations have a failure row and no success row ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:135-137](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L135-L137)).
- Only two reasons ever warn the user: `salary_unusable` and `work_mode_unusable`. The rest go to the trace table only ([lib/utils/normalization-warnings.ts:15-18](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/normalization-warnings.ts#L15-L18)). A search collects around 1,800 jobs, so one broken source would otherwise print a line per job ([lib/utils/normalization-warnings.ts:1-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/normalization-warnings.ts#L1-L7)). Each warning shows a count and at most two examples ([lib/utils/normalization-warnings.ts:20-22](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/normalization-warnings.ts#L20-L22)).
- A trace row and a warning both need the job's id and collector. A job with neither is still normalized but leaves no record ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:232-236](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L232-L236)). Trace rows need `trace`, `runId` and `step` together, so the handler also runs outside a job search ([lib/handlers/normalization.ts:241-245](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/normalization.ts#L241-L245)).

## Association

### Why slug first, then name

A job from an ATS board knows which board it came from. That is a stronger identity than a spelled name, because it needs no matching on spelling ([lib/handlers/association.ts:95-96](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L95-L96)). Aggregator jobs have only a name. So the lookup order is:

1. **Board slug.** `findBySlug` asks whether any company owns a row in the ATS slug table with that slug ([lib/services/company-service.ts:209-215](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L209-L215)).
2. **Name match key.** `findByMatchKey` looks up the company by the unique `match_key` column ([lib/services/company-service.ts:217-220](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L217-L220)).
3. **Create.** If neither finds a company and the name is usable, a company is created ([lib/handlers/association.ts:107-122](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L107-L122)).

If the slug fails to find a company, the code falls through to the name, and does not create. The reason in the code: a board a parser found but the seed never polled must not split an employer the table already holds ([lib/handlers/association.ts:104-106](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L104-L106)).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    J["Job arrives"] --> HasSlug{"Has raw_company_slug?"}
    HasSlug -- yes --> BySlug["findBySlug"]
    HasSlug -- no --> HasName
    BySlug --> FoundSlug{"Found?"}
    FoundSlug -- yes --> MS["matched_by_slug"]
    FoundSlug -- no --> HasName{"Usable name?<br>match key not empty"}
    HasName -- yes --> ByKey["findByMatchKey"]
    HasName -- no --> NoMatch["association_failed<br>reason no_company_name"]
    ByKey --> FoundKey{"Found?"}
    FoundKey -- yes --> MN["matched_by_name"]
    FoundKey -- no --> Create["companies.create"]
    Create --> Made{"Row created?"}
    Made -- yes --> CC["company_created"]
    Made -- "no, a blocker holds the name" --> MN
    MS --> Fill{"Company has no name<br>and job has one?"}
    Fill -- yes --> FN["fillName"]
    Fill -- no --> Done["company_id set on job"]
    FN --> Done
    MN --> Done
    CC --> Done
    NoMatch --> Travel["Job travels on with no company"]

    style J fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style HasSlug fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style BySlug fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style FoundSlug fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style HasName fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style ByKey fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style FoundKey fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Create fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Made fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Fill fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style FN fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style MS fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style MN fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style CC fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style Done fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style NoMatch fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style Travel fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/association.ts:85-185, lib/services/company-service.ts:209-220, lib/services/company-service.ts:301-331 -->

### The match key

Two spellings of one employer must reach one company row. `companyMatchKey` builds a key both spellings produce. It lower-cases each run of letters and digits, drops a trailing run of legal-entity words, and joins the rest ([lib/utils/company-match-key.ts:44-58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/company-match-key.ts#L44-L58)). The list includes `inc`, `llc`, `gmbh` and also `group`, `holdings` and `holding`, because "Ryan Specialty" and "Ryan Specialty Group" are one employer ([lib/utils/company-match-key.ts:3-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/company-match-key.ts#L3-L6)).

| Design choice | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Whole words come off the end, never substrings | A substring strip of "sa" or "co" would eat the ends of "Visa" and "Cisco" | [lib/utils/company-match-key.ts:51-53](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/company-match-key.ts#L51-L53) |
| Each word is lower-cased on its own | A letter whose lowercase form carries a separate accent mark would drag the mark into the key | [lib/utils/company-match-key.ts:45-49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/company-match-key.ts#L45-L49) |
| A name of only legal words keys to its tidied name | Two such names stay apart | [lib/utils/company-match-key.ts:60-67](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/company-match-key.ts#L60-L67) |
| A name with no letter or digit keys to empty and counts as no name | SQLite treats an empty string as an ordinary unique value, so a second such company would throw instead of failing to match | [lib/handlers/association.ts:36-45](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L36-L45) |
| The key is a unique column | The database refuses a duplicate employer whatever the code does | [lib/utils/company-match-key.ts:40-43](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/company-match-key.ts#L40-L43) |

The service enforces the same rule on create. `create` throws on an empty name and computes the key itself ([lib/services/company-service.ts:301-310](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L301-L310)). If the database refuses with a unique-constraint error, the service finds the blocking company and returns it with `created` false ([lib/services/company-service.ts:318-325](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L318-L325)). The handler reads that as a match and not a creation, because counting `company_created` rows is how a run reports the companies it added ([lib/handlers/association.ts:113-120](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L113-L120)).

### Trace events by outcome

| Outcome | Event | Reason | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Found by slug | `company_associated` | `matched_by_slug` | [lib/handlers/association.ts:97-101](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L97-L101) |
| Found by name key | `company_associated` | `matched_by_name` | [lib/handlers/association.ts:107-110](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L107-L110) |
| New company made | `company_associated` | `company_created` | [lib/handlers/association.ts:116-120](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L116-L120) |
| Neither slug nor name worked | `association_failed` | `no_company_name` | [lib/handlers/association.ts:124-138](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L124-L138) |
| Nameless company took a name | `company_dbrow_updated` | `company_name_filled` | [lib/handlers/association.ts:155-162](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L155-L162) |
| Name already held by another company | `company_update_failed` | `company_name_clash` | [lib/handlers/association.ts:163-171](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L163-L171) |

The association row always comes first. A fill or clash row follows it and never replaces it ([lib/handlers/association.ts:140-142](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L140-L142)).

A company with no name takes one from the first job that supplies one. A name already held is never overwritten, so nothing logs a name change on every run ([lib/handlers/association.ts:152-154](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L152-L154)). On a clash, the job stays on the company it matched and the pair is reported as a warning. Merging two rows that name one employer is the user's call ([lib/handlers/association.ts:163-166](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L163-L166)).

### Recording board rows

After a job has a company, `recordBoardSlug` writes down that the company posts on a hiring-system board. The row holds the slug, the company and the parser name ([lib/handlers/association.ts:196-208](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L196-L208)). It only fires when the job has both a slug and a `parser`. The parser is what says the slug came off a posting that was actually read. A slug seen on a collected ATS job is not yet worth a row ([lib/handlers/association.ts:192-195](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L192-L195)).

Why here and not in the parsing handler: the parsing handler is handed no service, and matching runs again straight after a posting is read, by which point the job carries the real slug ([lib/handlers/association.ts:187-191](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L187-L191)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant H as associateCompanies
    participant C as CompanyService
    participant S as AtsSlugService
    participant T as TraceService

    loop each job, one at a time
        H->>C: findBySlug, then findByMatchKey
        alt no match and usable name
            H->>C: create name
            C-->>H: company and created flag
        end
        C-->>H: company record
        H->>H: set company_id on a copy of the job
        opt job has raw_company_slug and parser
            H->>S: record slug, company_id, parser
            alt slug already recorded
                S-->>H: existing row, created false
                H->>H: warn board_name_clash if the parser differs
            else new slug
                S-->>H: new row with collector null
            end
        end
        H->>T: write company_associated and any follow-up rows
    end
    H-->>H: return jobs and folded warnings
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/association.ts:221-303, lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:66-94 -->

`AtsSlugService.record` creates a row with `collector: null`. Recording a slug says only that the board was seen on a posting. It never says that anything polls it. Promotion fills the collector in later ([lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:73-82](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L73-L82)). A slug already held writes nothing. The common second call is a plain read ([lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:67-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L67-L70)). If two writes race, the unique-constraint error is caught and the winning row is returned ([lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:86-93](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L86-L93)). There is deliberately no way to remove a row ([lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:5-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L5-L8)).

A row that already existed under a different parser means the board's name arrived from a second hiring system. The code warns, changes nothing, and leaves the recorded row as it was ([lib/handlers/association.ts:210-216](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L210-L216)). See [Services](../data/services.md) and [Data Model](../data/data-model.md) for the tables behind this.

### Failure handling

| Case | What happens | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Jobs run strictly one after another | Two jobs naming the same absent employer must end on one company. The second lookup has to follow the first create | [lib/handlers/association.ts:229-232](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L229-L232) |
| Company lookup throws | Only that job is lost. It keeps its place, and a `company_lookup_failed` warning is raised | [lib/handlers/association.ts:240-255](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L240-L255) |
| Board row write throws | The job already has its company. Only the board note is lost, and the next run writes it again | [lib/handlers/association.ts:259-273](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L259-L273) |
| Job has no id or collector | It is still associated, but leaves no trace row or warning | [lib/handlers/association.ts:276-278](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L276-L278) |
| Handler not given `atsSlugs` | The step still works and records no board | [lib/handlers/association.ts:22-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L22-L25), [lib/handlers/association.ts:201](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L201) |

The handler opens no database of its own and reaches the company table only through the service it is handed, so a fake serves its tests ([lib/handlers/association.ts:6-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L6-L9)). It recomputes on every pass and never skips a job that already has a company, so a later parsing pass can correct a company the first pass got wrong ([lib/handlers/association.ts:7-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/association.ts#L7-L9)).
