## The Parser contract

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Parser {
        +string name
        +parse(context) Promise
        +claims(url) boolean
    }
    class ParserContext {
        +string url
        +readRenderedPage(url) Promise
        +Date referenceInstant
    }
    class ParsedFields {
        +added_location_list string[]
        +raw_title
        +raw_location_list
        +raw_mode_list
        +raw_salary
        +description
    }
    class DeadPosting {
        +true dead
    }
    class ParseResult {
        ParsedFields or DeadPosting
    }
    Parser --> ParserContext : receives
    Parser --> ParseResult : returns
    ParseResult --> ParsedFields
    ParseResult --> DeadPosting

    style Parser fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style ParserContext fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style ParsedFields fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style DeadPosting fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style ParseResult fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/parsers/parser.ts:14-65 -->

The contract lives in one file so the handler knows only this shape and never a parser's inside parts ([parser.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/parser.ts#L1-L5)).

| Part | Plain-words meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | The parser's one name, such as `greenhouse`. It becomes `parser:greenhouse` in the source priority list, which decides whether a parser's value or a collector's value survives when both supply the same field | [parser.ts:50-54](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/parser.ts#L50-L54) |
| `parse(context)` | Reads the job at the link and returns what it found. A parser that cannot read its source throws | [parser.ts:55-58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/parser.ts#L55-L58) |
| `claims(url)` | Optional. Answers "is this link mine even though my domain does not appear in it". The registry asks only when no domain matched | [parser.ts:59-64](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/parser.ts#L59-L64) |
| `ParserContext` | The link plus two optional helpers: `readRenderedPage` (read a page in a browser the caller already opened) and `referenceInstant` (the moment the run started, for working out ages) | [parser.ts:14-18](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/parser.ts#L14-L18) |
| `DeadPosting` | `{ dead: true }`. The page itself shows the job is gone. Different from throwing (could not read) and from returning `{}` (read nothing) | [parser.ts:20-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/parser.ts#L20-L25) |
| Empty result | A result with no fields is treated as a failed read. One field or more is a success, because a thin posting is not an unread one | [parser.ts:34-39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/parser.ts#L34-L39) |
| `added_location_list` | Places read from loose page text. They are added to the job's own locations, never used to replace them | [parser.ts:27-32](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/parser.ts#L27-L32) |

Only the general parser is typed to return a dead posting. Dedicated parsers are typed `Parser`, which defaults to plain fields, so they "can never find a page dead" ([parser.ts:41-49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/parser.ts#L41-L49)).

## The registry: picking a parser for a link

The registry is keyed by **owned domain**, which is the name a company registered, not the full host. Greenhouse serves boards from `boards.greenhouse.io`, `job-boards.greenhouse.io` and `job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io`. Keying by owned domain makes all three one entry, and it caught the `.eu` host that a hand-written list had missed. It also lets a platform like Workday, which gives every employer its own subdomain, count as one platform instead of many unrelated sites ([registry.ts:5-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/registry.ts#L5-L14)). The domain is worked out with the public suffix list, because "the last two labels" would misread `adzuna.co.uk` as `co.uk` ([registrable-domain.ts:10-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/registrable-domain.ts#L10-L14)). Only `http` and `https` addresses count ([registrable-domain.ts:25-27](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/registrable-domain.ts#L25-L27)).

`parserForUrl` makes three attempts, in this order ([registry.ts:51-79](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/registry.ts#L51-L79)).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    In["Resolved link"] --> D["registrableDomainFromUrl"]
    D --> Q1{"Domain in the<br>owned-domain list"}
    Q1 -- yes --> P1["Return that dedicated parser"]
    Q1 -- no --> Q2{"Does any dedicated parser<br>claim the link"}
    Q2 -- yes --> P2["Return the claiming parser"]
    Q2 -- no --> Q3{"Is it a web address<br>domain not null"}
    Q3 -- yes --> P3["Return generalParser"]
    Q3 -- no --> P4["Return null"]

    style In fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style D fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Q1 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Q2 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Q3 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style P1 fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style P2 fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style P3 fill:#1e3a5f,stroke:#4a9eed,color:#e6edf3
    style P4 fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/parsers/registry.ts:56-79 -->

**Why the order matters.** The registry measured on 2026-09-20 that all 309 postings already on a Greenhouse address also carry a Greenhouse job number. If claims were checked first, a Lever, Ashby or Dribbble link that happened to carry that number would be pulled away from the parser that owns its domain ([registry.ts:16-21](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/registry.ts#L16-L21)). Domain ownership therefore wins, and claims only rescue links on unowned domains.

The only parser that makes a claim today is Greenhouse. It claims any link carrying a `gh_jid` query value, because some employers host Greenhouse postings on their own careers page ([greenhouse.ts:127-133](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/greenhouse.ts#L127-L133)). `parserForUrl` returns `null` only for a string that is not a web address. It never returns `null` for a valid web address ([registry.ts:72-78](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/registry.ts#L72-L78)).

## All 12 parsers

Eleven dedicated parsers sit in the registry. The twelfth is the general parser, which sits outside the domain list and is the fallback ([registry.ts:37-49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/registry.ts#L37-L49), [general.ts:45](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L45)). None opens a browser itself except through the helper handed to the general parser.

| Parser | Owned domain | How it reads the posting | Employer name | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `greenhouse` | `greenhouse.io`, plus links carrying `gh_jid` | Public JSON feed at `boards-api.greenhouse.io`, with `pay_transparency=true` so pay is not withheld. Board and job id come from the link, or from the job number via a board-name lookup when the link names no board | Read from the posting itself | [greenhouse.ts:15-16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/greenhouse.ts#L15-L16), [101-122](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/greenhouse.ts#L101-L122), [124-162](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/greenhouse.ts#L124-L162) |
| `lever` | `lever.co` | Public JSON feed at `api.lever.co/v0/postings/{board}/{id}` | One extra request for the board page, name read from its title, because the feed never carries it | [lever.ts:14-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/lever.ts#L14-L17), [37-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/lever.ts#L37-L70) |
| `ashby` | `ashbyhq.com` | Fetches the whole board's JSON at `api.ashbyhq.com`, then finds the posting by a link match key because Ashby postings have no stable id | One extra request for the board page title | [ashby.ts:14-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/ashby.ts#L14-L17), [41-94](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/ashby.ts#L41-L94) |
| `dribbble` | `dribbble.com` | Plain fetch of the server-rendered page. Reads an inline `Dribbble.JobListing.initialize` block with targeted patterns, plus the page's `JobPosting` data. Translates Dribbble's own work-mode words | From the inline block or the `JobPosting` data | [dribbble.ts:106-145](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/dribbble.ts#L106-L145), [147-157](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/dribbble.ts#L147-L157) |
| `workday` | `myworkdayjobs.com` | JSON data address for each posting, built from the link's board and job path | Deliberately left out. Workday sends a legal entity name and using it would split one employer into two companies | [workday.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/workday.ts#L1-L6), [25-50](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/workday.ts#L25-L50) |
| `ultipro` | `ultipro.com` | Plain fetch of the posting page, which embeds the whole job in a `CandidateOpportunityDetail(...)` script call. The job's identity lives in the link's query string | From the posting | [ultipro.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/ultipro.ts#L1-L5), [16-44](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/ultipro.ts#L16-L44) |
| `gem` | `gem.com` | Public JSON feed at `api.gem.com/job_board/v0/{board}/job_posts/{id}` | None. The aggregator's name stands | [gem.ts:12-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/gem.ts#L12-L13), [34-59](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/gem.ts#L34-L59) |
| `smartrecruiters` | `smartrecruiters.com` | Public JSON feed. Only the number before the first dash in the link's id is sent, because the full slug returns Bad Request | Published by the feed | [smartrecruiters.ts:1-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/smartrecruiters.ts#L1-L7), [39-48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/smartrecruiters.ts#L39-L48), [50-75](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/smartrecruiters.ts#L50-L75) |
| `bamboohr` | `bamboohr.com` | Asks the board's `careers/{id}/detail` address for JSON. Also reads a free-text pay field with no currency sign needed | None. The aggregator's name stands | [bamboohr.ts:17-18](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/bamboohr.ts#L17-L18), [47-80](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/bamboohr.ts#L47-L80) |
| `rippling` | `rippling.com` | Public JSON feed at `api.rippling.com/platform/api/ats/v1/board/{board}/jobs/{id}` | Published on the job itself | [rippling.ts:12-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/rippling.ts#L12-L13), [37-62](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/rippling.ts#L37-L62) |
| `workable` | `workable.com` | Handles two sites. Company site `apply.workable.com/{board}/j/{code}` and the search site `jobs.workable.com/view/{id}/{slug}`, each with its own JSON feed | Company site: one extra request to the board's widget. Search site: the job names the employer but not its board, so it guesses three board names and keeps the first whose widget lists at least one job | [workable.ts:28-35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/workable.ts#L28-L35), [126-154](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/workable.ts#L126-L154), [209-224](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/workable.ts#L209-L224) |
| `general` (fallback) | None | Plain fetch. Reads the page's `JobPosting` data first, then the page's main text. Opens a browser only if both find nothing and a browser helper was supplied | Not read. Title, employer and pay stay with the collector | [general.ts:1-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L1-L17), [45-81](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L45-L81) |

Every dedicated parser follows the same plan. It cuts a board name and a posting id out of the link, calls the platform's data address, throws if the answer is not ok, maps the answer to raw fields, and then runs `withFieldsFromDescription`. A link it cannot read throws a "could not read" error ("a parse error, not an empty read", for example [lever.ts:42-45](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/lever.ts#L42-L45)). Each uses a browser-like user-agent header (`BROWSER_USER_AGENT`, [page-fetcher.ts:10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/page-fetcher.ts#L10)).

### Shared field maps

A source's field mapping lives in `lib/utils/{source}-fields.ts`, not inside the collector or parser. Both the collector and the parser call it, so the two cannot drift apart. For example, `jobFieldsFromGreenhousePosting` writes cents exactly as Greenhouse sends them, and records `salary_unit: "cents"` instead of converting. It does the mapping only. Building the link and setting the phase flags belongs to the caller, so one cannot overwrite the other's work ([greenhouse-fields.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/greenhouse-fields.ts#L1-L6), [36-48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/greenhouse-fields.ts#L36-L48)). Greenhouse publishes no work mode, so `raw_mode_list` is empty and the description fallback fills it ([greenhouse-fields.ts:61-64](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/greenhouse-fields.ts#L61-L64)).

### The description fallback

`withFieldsFromDescription` is the one shared step that reads work mode and pay out of description prose. A field the employer actually published always wins. The prose is read only when the published field is empty, because prose may describe a signing bonus or a different pay tier ([description-fallback.ts:6-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/description-fallback.ts#L6-L9), [20-27](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/description-fallback.ts#L20-L27)).

### How the general parser reads a page

| Step | What happens | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Fetch | `fetchPageAnswer` returns status, final address and HTML | [general.ts:48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L48), [page-fetcher.ts:27-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/page-fetcher.ts#L27-L34) |
| 2. Dead by status | 404 or 410 returns `{ dead: true }` | [general.ts:52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L52) |
| 3. Dead by address | An address carrying an error flag returns `{ dead: true }` | [general.ts:56](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L56) |
| 4. Refusal | Any other non-2xx (403, 429, 5xx) throws. A refusal is not proof the job is gone | [general.ts:58-62](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L58-L62) |
| 5. Plain read | Try `JobPosting` data, then main text. Return the fields if either works | [general.ts:25-43](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L25-L43), [66-67](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L66-L67) |
| 6. No browser helper | Return `{}` (nothing read). Some sites draw everything with scripts, so there is not enough evidence to call the page dead | [general.ts:69-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L69-L72) |
| 7. Browser read | Fetch the rendered page and read it the same way | [general.ts:74-76](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L74-L76) |
| 8. Still nothing | Return `{ dead: true }`. The page loaded in a browser and shows no job | [general.ts:78-79](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L78-L79) |

The general parser reads five things only: posted date, updated date, work mode, location and description. It never calls a posting dead from the job data's end date, because sites leave that as a placeholder ([general.ts:6-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L6-L17), [job-posting-data.ts:127-151](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-posting-data.ts#L127-L151)). Locations read from loose page text come back as `added_location_list`, so they add to the job's places rather than replace them ([general.ts:35-42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/general.ts#L35-L42)). The page-text reader uses Readability and treats fewer than 500 characters of article text as "not a real posting" ([page-text.ts:13-15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/page-text.ts#L13-L15)).

## The handler: one job at a time

`parseJobs` reads the list from the database (jobs that are `backlog`, resolved and not yet parsed, [job-service.ts:427-433](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L427-L433)). It runs sequentially. Each job is guarded on its own, so one failure never costs the jobs after it ([parsing.ts:157-158](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L157-L158)). A browser for the general parser is opened lazily, only when a parser first asks for a rendered page, and closed at the end of the step ([job-search.ts:466-501](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L466-L501)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant H as parseJobs
    participant Reg as parserForUrl
    participant Ded as Dedicated parser
    participant Gen as General parser
    participant Loc as Location rule
    participant T as Trace service

    H->>H: read resolved_url and its domain
    alt no resolved URL or not a web address
        H->>Loc: apply location rule to the job as it stands
    else web address
        H->>Reg: which parser owns this link
        Reg-->>H: dedicated parser, or the general parser
        opt a dedicated parser was returned
            H->>Ded: parse(url)
            alt result has at least one field
                Ded-->>H: fields
                H->>H: merge fields, keep status, is_parsed true, parser name set
                H->>T: job_parsed
            else empty result or a throw
                Note over H,Ded: nothing is recorded for this attempt
            end
        end
        H->>Gen: parse(url) as the safety net
        alt dead posting
            Gen-->>H: dead true
            H->>H: status expired, is_parsed true, parser general
            H->>T: job_parsed, reason dead_page
        else fields found
            Gen-->>H: fields
            H->>Loc: apply location rule to the merged job
        else empty or throw
            H->>Loc: apply location rule to the original job
        end
    end
    Loc-->>H: parsed, or unparseable
    H->>T: job_parsed, or parsing_failed with reason no_location
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/parsing.ts:80-152, lib/handlers/parsing.ts:154-177 -->

### What trust each path gets

| Path | Status change | Location rule applied | Parser name written | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dedicated parser read at least one field | None. Status is copied back as it was | No. The source that owns the domain already knows what kind of posting it is | The dedicated parser's name | [parsing.ts:94-106](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L94-L106) |
| General parser found the posting dead | `expired` | No | `general` | [parsing.ts:119-124](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L119-L124) |
| General parser found fields | None | Yes | `general` | [parsing.ts:126-144](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L126-L144) |
| General parser found nothing, or was refused | None. A refused read never expires a job | Yes, on the job as it stood | None | [parsing.ts:145-151](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L145-L151) |
| No resolved URL, or not a web address | None | Yes | None | [parsing.ts:85-89](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L85-L89) |

Both failure paths of a dedicated parser are silent. An empty answer or a throw falls through to the general parser, and no trace row is written for the dedicated attempt ([parsing.ts:107-111](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L107-L111)). Each job leaves parsing with exactly one trace row, however many parsers were asked ([schema.prisma:420-426](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L420-L426)). If the registry returns the general parser itself, the dedicated attempt is skipped and the general parser runs once ([parsing.ts:91-95](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L91-L95)).

## When a job becomes unparseable

`docs/architecture.md` still says a job no parser covers is set aside as `unparseable` ([architecture.md:212](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L212)). The code no longer works that way. The only place the parsing handler sets `unparseable` is `applyLocationRule`, and it does so for one reason ([parsing.ts:58-71](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L58-L71)).

A job becomes `unparseable` when all of these are true:

1. The step ended on the location rule. That means the job had no resolved web link, or the general parser read nothing, or the general parser read fields that added no place.
2. None of the job's `raw_location_list` strings yields a real place. `splitLocation` already strips work-mode words such as "Remote", so a list holding only "Remote" has no place ([parsing.ts:50-56](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L50-L56)).

The trace row is `parsing_failed` with reason `no_location`. It carries the owned domain and the resolved link, so failures can be counted by platform and chased back ([parsing.ts:64-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L64-L70)). A search of `lib/` and `scripts/` outside tests finds one place that writes the status `unparseable`: [parsing.ts:65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L65). Inferred: a manual status change can also choose it, since it is a listed status ([job-status.ts:30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L30)).

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Waiting: backlog, resolved, not parsed
    Waiting --> Parsed: dedicated parser read a field
    Waiting --> General: no dedicated parser, or it failed
    General --> Expired: posting is dead
    General --> LocationRule: fields found, or nothing found
    LocationRule --> Parsed: job holds a real place
    LocationRule --> Unparseable: no real place
    Parsed --> [*]: is_parsed true
    Expired --> [*]: status expired
    Unparseable --> Waiting: recovery script, once a parser claims the link

    classDef good fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    classDef bad fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    classDef warn fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    class Parsed good
    class Unparseable bad
    class Expired warn
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/parsing.ts:58-152, scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts:51-71 -->

### Recovery

Nothing in a job search reads jobs at status `unparseable` again, because the step that feeds parsing reads only `backlog` jobs ([recover-unparseable-jobs.ts:3-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts#L3-L7)). `scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts` is a one-time command run by hand. It reads every `unparseable` job, asks `parserForUrl` whether anything claims the link, and moves the ones that are claimed back to `backlog` through the same status-change code a manual change uses ([recover-unparseable-jobs.ts:61-86](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts#L61-L86)). It is not a handler and no orchestrator names it ([recover-unparseable-jobs.ts:13-15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts#L13-L15)).

Inferred: because `parserForUrl` now returns the general parser for any web address, this script's test (`parserForUrl(link) === null`) skips only jobs with no usable web link. It would move every other `unparseable` job back to `backlog`, including ones the general parser already failed on. Those would be tried again and, if they still hold no place, become `unparseable` again.

## Adding a parser

A parser joins the pipeline by being listed in `lib/parsers/registry.ts` and nowhere else ([sources.md:16-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/sources.md#L16-L17)). Its file is `lib/parsers/{subject}.ts`, its value is `{subject}Parser`, and its `name` matches its file name ([sources.md:12-15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/sources.md#L12-L15)). Adding or renaming a registry entry also requires `npm run db:seed`. The seed appends the new `parser:{name}` to the bottom of the source priority list, and a source missing from that list loses every field two sources contest ([source-registry.md:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/source-registry.md#L1-L3)).

# Backlog Cleanup, Promotion and Classification

## Overview

The pipeline collects more jobs than anyone wants to read. Three steps judge jobs instead of fetching or reshaping them. They answer questions like "is this job too old", "was this role listed again" and "is this somewhere the user could work". The pipeline's rules give judging to these steps alone: classification judges the job, and it "never reshapes a value or goes looking for a missing one" ([part-ownership.md:40](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L40)).

The three steps share one measure of age, so the clock cannot drift between them. They also share one reference moment: the instant the run started. A run that spends half an hour in a browser still judges every job against that one instant ([backlog-cleanup.ts:6-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L6-L11), [classification.ts:12-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L12-L13)).

The work-mode and location values used here were cleaned earlier. See [Normalization and Association](./normalization-and-association.md). The jobs come from [Parsing](./parsing.md).

### At a glance

| Component | Responsibility | Key file | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backlog cleanup, jobs (`cleanBacklogJobs`) | Marks backlog jobs past the expiry threshold as `expired`. Runs first in a run | `lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts` | [backlog-cleanup.ts:92-126](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L92-L126) |
| Backlog cleanup, companies (`cleanBacklogCompanies`) | Empties company scores that have gone stale, so scoring researches them again | `lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts` | [backlog-cleanup.ts:252-315](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L252-L315) |
| Promotion (`promoteJobs`) | Returns an expired job to the backlog once its age is back inside the threshold | `lib/handlers/promotion.ts` | [promotion.ts:69-102](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L69-L102) |
| Classification (`classifyJobs`) | Marks reposts, expires jobs that are too old, and matches location against the user's | `lib/handlers/classification.ts` | [classification.ts:201-239](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L201-L239) |
| Age measure (`jobAgeInDays`, `isPastThreshold`) | The one place a job's age is worked out | `lib/utils/job-age.ts` | [job-age.ts:61-63](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-age.ts#L61-L63), [85-91](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-age.ts#L85-L91) |
| Location match (`matchLocation`) | Decides if any place and work-mode pair is close enough to the user | `lib/utils/location-match.ts` | [location-match.ts:43-87](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/location-match.ts#L43-L87) |
| Point in shape (`pointInShape`) | Tests whether the user's home point lies inside a place's outline | `lib/utils/point-in-shape.ts` | [point-in-shape.ts:37-53](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/point-in-shape.ts#L37-L53) |
| Distance (`haversineDistanceMiles`) | Straight-line miles between two map points | `lib/utils/haversine.ts` | [haversine.ts:8-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/haversine.ts#L8-L25) |
| Geocoder (`createGeocoder`) | Turns a place's text into coordinates and an outline, one request a second | `lib/tools/geocoder.ts` | [geocoder.ts:92-136](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L92-L136) |
| Place service (`createPlaceService`) | Owns the `Place` table, a cache of every place looked up | `lib/services/place-service.ts` | [place-service.ts:60-93](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/place-service.ts#L60-L93) |

## Where the steps sit in a run

Backlog cleanup opens the run. Promotion and classification close the job-handling part of it, after parsing.

```mermaid

    end

    end
```

<!-- Sources: lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:218-272, lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:582-637 -->

The exact order inside the orchestrator is: cleanup of jobs, then cleanup of companies, then two saves ([job-search.ts:220-272](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L220-L272)). Later come the home-location lookup, promotion and its save, then classification and its save ([job-search.ts:558-637](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L558-L637)). Scoring is a separate agent workflow, described in [Scoring](../agent-workflows/scoring.md). The wider run is described in [The Job Search Run](../architecture/job-search-run.md).

Every step reads its work from the database, and every step ends by saving. The expiry threshold is read once for the run, because cleanup, promotion and classification all judge age and a run that disagreed with itself about what counts as expired would contradict itself ([job-search.ts:188-194](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L188-L194)).

## How a job's age is measured

`jobAgeInDays` picks an anchor date in this order: the date the source last updated the posting, then the date it was posted, then the date this pipeline first collected it ([job-age.ts:85-87](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-age.ts#L85-L87)). The reason is stated in the file. A source's last update date is closer to a posting's real age than its first date. The collected date is only a fallback because a source's own dates outrank our bookkeeping ([job-age.ts:73-77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-age.ts#L73-L77)).

The row's own `modified_at` and `created_at` are never read. Writing a status moves `modified_at`, so a rule reading it would make every job look freshly posted the moment its status was written ([job-age.ts:78-81](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-age.ts#L78-L81)).

| Rule | Behavior | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Exact duration | Age is a fractional number of days, not a count of calendar days. `DAY_MS` is a fixed 86,400,000 ms | [job-age.ts:82-84](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-age.ts#L82-L84), [durations.ts:11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/durations.ts#L11) |
| Future dates | A posting dated after the reference instant has age 0, never a negative age | [job-age.ts:88-90](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-age.ts#L88-L90) |
| Threshold is inclusive | A job exactly `threshold` days old counts as past it | [job-age.ts:58-63](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-age.ts#L58-L63) |
| Missing data | An undated job is read as collected this instant, which keeps it. Missing data alone never expires a job | [backlog-cleanup.ts:53-58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L53-L58), [classification.ts:129-133](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L129-L133) |

## Step 1: Backlog cleanup

### Jobs

The step is handed every job with status `backlog`, regardless of how far along the pipeline it got ([job-service.ts:437-443](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L437-L443)). For each job, `cleanBacklogJob` asks one question: has its age crossed the expiry threshold. If yes, only the status changes, to `expired`. Nothing else about the job is touched ([backlog-cleanup.ts:73-80](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L73-L80)). The step works on copies and never changes the job it was handed. It raises no warnings, because a job ageing out is the step working ([backlog-cleanup.ts:88-91](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L88-L91)).

Trace events are `job_entered`, then either `job_kept` or `job_expired` with reason `past_expiration_threshold` ([backlog-cleanup.ts:39-46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L39-L46)). A job with no `id` or no `collector` is judged but leaves no trace row, since a row needs both as its key ([backlog-cleanup.ts:103-105](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L103-L105)).

### Companies

A judgement about an employer goes stale the way a posting does. The company half of the sweep reads every company that has been scored (`scored_at` is not null, [company-service.ts:293-299](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L293-L299)). It uses two thresholds.

| Case | What is cleared | `scored_at` | Trace event | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Older than `scoreExpiryDays` | All four scores and their rationale sentences, and the list of guessed categories | Set to null | `company_scores_cleared` | [backlog-cleanup.ts:221-229](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L221-L229), [287-294](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L287-L294) |
| Older than `guessedScoreExpiryDays` and some categories were guessed | Only the guessed categories | Left as is, because the researched categories really are that old | `placeholder_company_scores_cleared` | [backlog-cleanup.ts:231-243](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L231-L243), [295-302](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L295-L302) |
| Never scored, or neither threshold passed | Nothing | Unchanged | `company_kept` | [backlog-cleanup.ts:214-217](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L214-L217), [303-310](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L303-L310) |

A "guessed" category is one the scoring agent filled in because nothing public could be found, so it expires sooner than a researched one ([backlog-cleanup.ts:128-131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L128-L131)). Full expiry is checked first on purpose, so a company old enough to lose everything does not walk away having lost only its guesses ([backlog-cleanup.ts:221-222](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L221-L222)). A company's age cannot reuse the job measure because a company has one date and a job has three, but the arithmetic matches, including a floor of zero for future dates ([backlog-cleanup.ts:159-166](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L159-L166)). The handler returns two counts, `scoresCleared` and `guessesCleared`, for the run summary ([backlog-cleanup.ts:146-153](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L146-L153)). The orchestrator saves the cleaned companies before it saves the cleaned jobs ([job-search.ts:252-271](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L252-L271)).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    C["A scored company"] --> N{"scored_at is null"}
    N -- yes --> K["company_kept"]
    N -- no --> A["Work out age in days"]
    A --> F{"Age at or past<br>scoreExpiryDays"}
    F -- yes --> X["Clear all four scores<br>and rationales<br>scored_at becomes null"]
    F -- no --> G{"Some categories guessed<br>and age at or past<br>guessedScoreExpiryDays"}
    G -- yes --> Y["Clear only the guessed<br>categories"]
    G -- no --> K
    X --> R["Scoring researches it again"]
    Y --> R

    style C fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style N fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style A fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style F fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style G fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style K fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style X fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style Y fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style R fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
```

## Step 2: Promotion

### Why promotion exists

An employer that lists a role again gives it a fresh posting date. That date pulls the job's age back inside the threshold. A job that expired earlier should then come back. Promotion does that ([promotion.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L1-L6)).

Promotion trusts the job service to decide which jobs qualify. The lookup `findExpiredWithin` returns jobs whose status is `expired` and whose age is back inside the threshold ([job-service.ts:454-466](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L454-L466)). The handler then promotes everything it is handed and checks no age or status of its own ([promotion.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L1-L6)).

It runs late for a reason. An expired job only gains a fresh date after collection has found the new listing and dedupe has merged it into the existing record. Run earlier, there would be nothing to find ([promotion.ts:8-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L8-L11)).

### What it changes

| Field | New value | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `backlog` | The job is back in the running | [promotion.ts:57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L57) |
| `is_classified` | `false` | Classification should reach its own conclusion about the relisted posting rather than inherit the one that expired it | [promotion.ts:13-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L13-L14), [58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L58) |
| `alignment_score`, `alignment_rationale` | `null` | The posting now on offer is not the one that was scored. A job with no score is picked up by the next scoring run | [promotion.ts:50-52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L50-L52), [59-60](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L59-L60) |
| Location match, matched place, matched mode, repost mark | Left alone | Classification overwrites them moments later, so clearing them first buys nothing | [promotion.ts:15-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L15-L17) |

Trace rows are `job_entered` and `job_promoted`, with no reason, because promotion has a single outcome ([promotion.ts:32-40](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L32-L40)). The orchestrator reads classification's work list after promotion's save, so promoted jobs are judged in the same run ([job-search.ts:606-610](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L606-L610)).

Inferred: `findExpiredWithin` filters on status `expired` and age only. It does not look at why a job expired. A job that parsing marked `expired` because its page was dead keeps a fresh posting date, so by this filter it also qualifies for promotion on the next run ([parsing.ts:119-124](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/parsing.ts#L119-L124), [job-service.ts:458-466](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L458-L466)). Whether that is intended is not written down in the files read for this page. Verify in the promotion tests (`lib/handlers/promotion.test.ts`).

## Step 3: Classification

### What it is handed

The step reads every job with status `backlog` that is resolved, parsed and not yet classified ([job-service.ts:488-494](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L488-L494)). It asks three questions about each. The order matters ([classification.ts:6-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L6-L10)).

1. **Is it a repost?** Decided first. The repost mark is a fact about the posting, not a verdict, so it survives whatever the other checks decide. A job can be both a repost and too old.
2. **Is it too old?** Before the location check, because a job the user cannot apply to is not worth a paced, paid mapping request.
3. **Is it somewhere the user could work?** The only check that reaches outside the app.

### The decision flow for one job

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S["Job handed in"] --> E["Write job_entered"]
    E --> RP{"Posting date and updated date<br>both present and further apart<br>than repostGapDays"}
    RP -- yes --> RM["is_repost true<br>write job_reposted"]
    RP -- no --> AG
    RM --> AG{"Age at or past<br>expiryThresholdDays"}
    AG -- yes --> EX["status expired<br>is_classified true<br>job_expired"]
    AG -- no --> LT{"Job names any places"}
    LT -- "yes" --> GEO["Look up each place text"]
    GEO --> ANY{"At least one place read"}
    ANY -- no --> UN["Leave in backlog, unjudged<br>classification_failed<br>location_unusable"]
    ANY -- yes --> M
    LT -- "no" --> M["matchLocation<br>places and modes, home, radius"]
    M --> MM{"Matched"}
    MM -- yes --> OK["location_match true<br>place and mode recorded<br>is_classified true<br>job_classified"]
    MM -- no --> TF["status too far<br>location_match false<br>is_classified true<br>classification_failed<br>no_location_match"]

    style S fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style E fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style RP fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style RM fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style AG fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style LT fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style GEO fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style ANY fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style M fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style MM fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style EX fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style UN fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style OK fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style TF fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/classification.ts:109-196 -->

### The three checks

| Check | Rule | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repost | Needs both `posting_date` and `posting_updated_date`. The gap between them, as an exact duration, must be greater than `repostGapDays` | Two dates far apart mean the role was listed again, not edited. One date says nothing either way. The gap is a duration so that two collectors disagreeing by hours about one posting are absorbed | [classification.ts:60-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L60-L70), [schema.prisma:336-340](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L336-L340) |
| Age | `isPastThreshold` on `jobAgeInDays`. If past, status becomes `expired` and `is_classified` is true | A relisted role has a fresh updated date, so it is not old. That is also why promotion can bring it back | [classification.ts:125-141](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L125-L141) |
| Location | Look up every place text on the job, then `matchLocation`. A match records the place and mode. No match sets status `too far` | The user needs a job they can do from where they live | [classification.ts:143-186](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L143-L186) |

The location texts come from `normalized_location_list`, and the modes from `normalized_mode_list` ([classification.ts:143](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L143), [164](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L164)). A job that names places but has none of them read is **left in the backlog, unjudged**. A place we could not read is not proof the job is far away ([classification.ts:152-157](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L152-L157)). A lookup that throws is handled the same way, with the same reason, so every job has exactly one outcome row ([classification.ts:188-194](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L188-L194)). A job that names no place at all is judged on its work mode alone, because a posting saying only "remote" names nowhere and is still work the user could do ([classification.ts:159-161](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L159-L161)).

### Trace events

| Event | Reason | When | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `job_entered` | none | Every job on arrival | [classification.ts:117](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L117) |
| `job_reposted` | none | The repost check fired. Written before the outcome so the outcome stays the last word | [classification.ts:122-123](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L122-L123) |
| `job_expired` | `past_expiration_threshold` | Too old | [classification.ts:139](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L139) |
| `job_classified` | none | Location matched | [classification.ts:170](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L170) |
| `classification_failed` | `no_location_match` | Places read, none close enough | [classification.ts:183](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L183) |
| `classification_failed` | `location_unusable` | Places named but none could be read, or a lookup threw | [classification.ts:155](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L155), [193](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L193) |

## Location matching: containment against distance

`matchLocation` pairs every place a job names with every work mode it offers. Any one pair passing is enough, so a posting offering several ways to work is judged on its best ([location-match.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/location-match.ts#L1-L5)). The two tests answer different questions.

| Work mode | Test used | Reason | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `remote` | Home point inside the place's outline, **or** place within the radius | Remote means working from home. Living inside the place is enough however large the place is, and a nearby anchor town still counts | [location-match.ts:6-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/location-match.ts#L6-L11), [39-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/location-match.ts#L39-L41) |
| `hybrid`, `in-person` | Place within the radius only | These mean showing up at an office. Living in a region the office also sits in is no help if the office is far away | [location-match.ts:7-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/location-match.ts#L7-L9) |
| Unknown mode word | Treated as on-site, the stricter test | A stray word must not let a whole country through on containment alone | [location-match.ts:37-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/location-match.ts#L37-L41) |
| No mode listed at all | Judged as one pair with mode `null`, which uses the containment test | An unknown mode is recorded as nothing, not invented as a word | [location-match.ts:49-51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/location-match.ts#L49-L51) |
| No place read, mode includes `remote` | Passes with no place named | A job saying only "remote" is work the user could do from home | [location-match.ts:53-58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/location-match.ts#L53-L58) |

Within the passing pairs, the strictly nearest place wins, so an exact tie keeps the place listed first. That decides only the name shown, never whether the job matched ([location-match.ts:76-80](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/location-match.ts#L76-L80)). The home point is the coordinates of the user's home location setting. The radius is the radius setting ([job-search.ts:558-575](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L558-L575)).

**Why containment is done with geometry, not names.** The file records that a name match once let a job in a different town with the same name as the user's read as local, and that any place sharing a name with the user's own neighbourhood would match it too. An outline cannot make that mistake ([point-in-shape.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/point-in-shape.ts#L1-L5)). `pointInShape` runs ray casting over a `Polygon` or `MultiPolygon`. A point inside a hole does not count. Any other shape, or no outline, contains nothing, and the caller falls back on distance ([point-in-shape.ts:32-53](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/point-in-shape.ts#L32-L53)). Distance is the haversine formula, which gives straight-line miles over the earth's surface, rounded to one decimal place ([haversine.ts:1-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/haversine.ts#L1-L25)).

```mermaid
graph TB
    Pair["One place and one work mode"] --> Dist["haversineDistanceMiles<br>home to place"]
    Pair --> Cont["pointInShape<br>home in place outline"]
    Dist --> Within{"Within radius"}
    Cont --> Inside{"Home inside outline"}
    Pair --> Mode{"Mode is remote<br>or unknown"}
    Mode -- "remote or null" --> OrTest["Passes if inside OR within radius"]
    Mode -- "hybrid, in-person, other" --> OnlyDist["Passes only if within radius"]
    Within --> OrTest
    Inside --> OrTest
    Within --> OnlyDist

    style Pair fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Dist fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Cont fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Within fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Inside fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style Mode fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style OrTest fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style OnlyDist fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/utils/location-match.ts:37-87, lib/utils/point-in-shape.ts:37-53, lib/utils/haversine.ts:8-25 -->

## Geocoding and the place cache

### Why there is a cache

The geocoder allows one request a second. Postings repeat the same places over and over. Across the real database, the file records that 3,975 lookups resolve to only 789 distinct places, so each place is looked up once and reused from the `Place` table ([place-service.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/place-service.ts#L1-L5)). Only the place service touches that table ([place-service.ts:1-2](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/place-service.ts#L1-L2)).

### The pace

| Rule | Behavior | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Spacing | `GEOCODE_PACING_MS = 1100`: one second plus a buffer for clock drift. The tool keeps its own timer, so no caller has to remember to wait | [geocoder.ts:4-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L4-L5), [15-16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L15-L16), [109-111](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L109-L111) |
| Timer lives in the geocoder | Held per geocoder, not in module state, so a test can pace a run without a reset hook | [geocoder.ts:93-95](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L93-L95) |
| No retry | A refusal returns `null` and stores nothing. A run resolving hundreds of places cannot afford to back off. The place is tried again next run | [geocoder.ts:6-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L6-L9), [127-133](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L127-L133) |
| Timeout | The request goes through `fetchWithTimeout`, so a hung request cannot stall every job waiting behind it | [geocoder.ts:113-119](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L113-L119) |
| Key | The `GEOCODE_MAPS_API_KEY` environment variable is read at call time and throws if missing. A missing key used to make every job fail to classify silently | [geocoder.ts:102-107](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L102-L107) |
| Request shape | Only the best match is asked for (`limit=1`), with the place outline simplified (`polygon_threshold=0.01`) because an unsimplified country outline runs to megabytes | [geocoder.ts:74-86](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L74-L86) |
| Bad numbers | A missing or unreadable coordinate returns `null` rather than NaN or zero, which would read as a place off the coast of Africa | [geocoder.ts:34-42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L34-L42) |

### The lookup order for one place text

`resolvePlace` goes through three levels before spending a request ([classification.ts:72-107](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L72-L107)).

1. **This run's dead-end set.** A text that already came back empty this run is not asked again. It is checked first because nothing is stored for an empty answer, so a text in the set cannot be in the table either.
2. **The `Place` table.** A place already held is used as is.
3. **The geocoder.** The answer is stored, or nothing is stored if it was empty. An empty text joins the dead-end set.

The dead-end set lives inside one call of `classifyJobs`, not in the module. One run therefore cannot inherit another's dead ends and skip a map service that has since learned the place ([classification.ts:208-211](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L208-L211)). The place service stores nothing for an empty answer, which leaves the text free to be tried again later, once a better text splitter or map might place it ([place-service.ts:73-78](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/place-service.ts#L73-L78)). It upserts on the lookup text ([place-service.ts:86-90](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/place-service.ts#L86-L90)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as classifyJob
    participant D as Dead-end set, this call only
    participant P as Place service
    participant G as Geocoder
    participant M as Map service

    C->>D: is this text in the set
    alt text is in the set
        D-->>C: yes, skip it
    else not in the set
        C->>P: findByText
        alt place held
            P-->>C: stored place
        else not held
            C->>G: lookUp
            G->>G: wait until 1100 ms since the last request
            G->>M: search, limit 1, simplified outline
            M-->>G: best match, or nothing
            G-->>C: place or null
            C->>P: store, writes nothing for null
            opt answer was empty
                C->>D: add the text
            end
        end
    end
    C->>C: matchLocation over all places read
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/classification.ts:80-107, lib/tools/geocoder.ts:92-136, lib/services/place-service.ts:60-93 -->

### The home point

Once per run, before classification, the orchestrator turns the user's home location setting into coordinates using the same cache. It asks the place service first and the geocoder only if the text has never been seen. A location that cannot be placed on a map ends the run, because measuring against nothing would mark every job as not matching ([job-search.ts:553-575](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L553-L575)).

## How a job's status moves through these steps

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> backlog
    backlog --> expired: cleanup, age past threshold
    backlog --> expired: classification, age past threshold
    backlog --> too_far: classification, no location match
    backlog --> backlog: classification, places unreadable, stays unjudged
    expired --> backlog: promotion, age back inside threshold

    classDef good fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    classDef bad fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    class backlog good
    class expired,too_far bad
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts:73-80, lib/handlers/promotion.ts:53-64, lib/handlers/classification.ts:138-186 -->

The state named `too_far` here is stored as the status string `too far`, with a space ([classification.ts:185](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/classification.ts#L185)). The diagram uses an underscore only because the diagram language does not allow a space in a state name. The part-ownership rule gives each status to one step: classification sets `too far`, or `expired` for an old posting, backlog cleanup sets `expired`, and promotion sets `backlog` ([part-ownership.md:46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L46)).

## Notes where code and docs differ

- The promotion handler's comment says it "runs late in the pipeline". In the orchestrator it runs after parsing's save and before classification, which is late for job handling but before scoring ([promotion.ts:8-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/promotion.ts#L8-L11), [job-search.ts:579-592](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L579-L592)).

# Services

## Overview

A service is the only code allowed to touch a table. Collectors, handlers and the dashboard never query the database themselves. They are handed a service and call its methods. This keeps each table's rules in one place. The job service says so in its opening lines: the save step, the status skill, the dashboard and scoring all go through it, "so the active-status freeze and the merge-on-arrival rules stay in one place instead of being re-solved at every call site" ([lib/services/job-service.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L1-L5)).

The project's word for this is "service". The glossary says it is "never called a store, a repository, or a DAO" (`CLAUDE.md`, "Terminology"). A service is built from the database connection and hands back a small object of functions (`CLAUDE.md`, "Terminology"; [.claude/rules/services.md:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/services.md#L7)).

| Service | Owns | Builder | Has a fake? | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Job | The `Job` table | `createJobService(db)` | Yes, stateful | [lib/services/job-service.ts:282](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L282) |
| Company | The `Company` table | `createCompanyService(db)` | Yes | [lib/services/company-service.ts:205](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L205) |
| AtsSlug | The `AtsSlug` table | `createAtsSlugService(db)` | Yes | [lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L58) |
| Place | The `Place` table | `createPlaceService(db)` | Yes | [lib/services/place-service.ts:60](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/place-service.ts#L60) |
| Settings | The single `Setting` row | `createSettingsService(db)` | Yes | [lib/services/settings-service.ts:89](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L89) |
| Trace | The `Trace` table | `createTraceService(db)` | No shared fake | [lib/services/trace-service.ts:115](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L115) |
| Work log | The `WorkLogEntry` table | `createWorkLogService(db)` | Yes | [lib/services/work-log-service.ts:43](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.ts#L43) |

## The pattern

Every service file follows the same naming ([.claude/rules/services.md:9-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/services.md#L9-L13)). The sections below show it applied.

<!-- Sources: scripts/job-search.ts:42-70, lib/db/pipeline-db.ts:14-18, lib/services/job-service.ts:11, lib/services/job-service.ts:539, lib/services/trace-service.ts:115 -->

The dotted line is the one place a service reaches past its own table. The job service imports the company service's column list and converter so a job read can bring its employer along. The comment explains that an employer built from a second column list "would drift from this one" ([lib/services/company-service.ts:111-116](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L111-L116), [lib/services/job-service.ts:535-551](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L535-L551)).

Each service gets the client through a type alias, `ReturnType<typeof createPipelineDb>`, so the type follows the builder ([lib/services/job-service.ts:160](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L160)).

### Why each read selects named columns

Every read in the company, AtsSlug and place services selects an exact column list. The comment states the reason: "the shape handed back always matches `CompanyRecord` regardless of what else the schema grows" ([lib/services/company-service.ts:111-113](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L111-L113), [lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:41-49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L41-L49), [lib/services/place-service.ts:27-37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/place-service.ts#L27-L37)). A new column can be added to the schema without silently changing what callers receive.

## The job service

This is the largest service. It has three jobs: write rows, find the lists each pipeline step needs, and answer lookup questions for skills and the dashboard.

### Writing a row

The single write method is `update(entry, priorityList, identifyingQueryValues)`. It needs an id, because the id is how the row is found. It reads the row. If none exists it creates one. Otherwise it writes to the existing row ([lib/services/job-service.ts:362-370](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L362-L370)). The `identifyingQueryValues` argument is required on purpose. Omitting it "would silently write match keys without the identifying value", so two different postings would look like one ([lib/services/job-service.ts:50-53](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L50-L53)).

The outcome tells the caller what happened, so it does not have to work it out from the returned row ([lib/services/job-service.ts:18-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L18-L25)).

| Outcome | Meaning | Trace event the save handler can write | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `created` | No row existed, so one was created with the id given at collection | `job_dbrow_created` | [lib/services/job-service.ts:309-310](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L309-L310) |
| `updated` | An existing row took merged fields | `job_dbrow_updated` | [lib/services/job-service.ts:349-351](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L349-L351) |
| `status_updated` | An active row took a different status and nothing else | `job_dbrow_status_updated` | [lib/services/job-service.ts:334-335](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L334-L335) |
| `unchanged` | An active row got an entry carrying no status, so nothing was written | none | [lib/services/job-service.ts:331-333](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L331-L333) |

The trace event column comes from the Trace model comment ([prisma/schema.prisma:399-408](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L399-L408)). The mapping from outcome to event is inferred from the names, since the save handler was not read for this page.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    A["update(entry)"] --> B{"entry.id present?"}
    B -->|no| X["throw: id is how the row is found"]
    B -->|yes| C["findUnique by id"]

    D -->|no| E{"collected_at set?"}
    E -->|no| Y["throw: no database default"]

    I -->|yes, entry has none| OUT3(["unchanged"])

    J --> OUT4(["updated"])

    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```
