<!-- Sources: lib/services/job-service.ts:285-352, lib/services/job-service.ts:362-370 -->

### The active-job freeze

A row whose status is active is frozen. The user has applied, so everything about the job is locked except its status. An entry carrying no status leaves the row alone ([lib/services/job-service.ts:328-336](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L328-L336)). The five active statuses are `app. sent`, `screening`, `interview`, `test` and `offer` ([lib/utils/job-status.ts:8-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L8-L14)). Save, the dashboard's job lists and the status skill all read this one list, so they cannot disagree about what the user has applied to ([lib/utils/job-status.ts:6-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L6-L7)).

Delete is guarded the same way. If the row is active, the delete is refused and the blocking job is handed back so the caller can warn naming it. A dedupe merge must not destroy application history ([lib/services/job-service.ts:372-384](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L372-L384), [lib/services/job-service.ts:43-47](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L43-L47)).

### The merge on arrival

For a row that is not active, the service merges the stored row with the arriving entry using `mergeJobs`, which ranks sources by the priority list ([lib/services/job-service.ts:342-344](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L342-L344)). It then drops the write-once fields before writing: `id` and `collected_at` ([lib/services/job-service.ts:346-349](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L346-L349), [lib/utils/job-merge.ts:57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-merge.ts#L57)). On a first-ever save it pools the posting dates against nothing, so a job with no posting date anywhere still leaves with one ([lib/services/job-service.ts:297-301](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L297-L301)). Two more details protect data:

| Detail | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `delete_on_save` and `created_at` are stripped before the write | The first is not a column. A merged job carries the surviving row's `created_at`, and writing it back would overwrite the database's own value. | [lib/services/job-service.ts:266-269](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L266-L269) |
| A link's match key travels with the link | A string link gets a fresh key. A `null` link clears its key. A link the write never mentions leaves the stored key alone. | [lib/services/job-service.ts:252-264](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L252-L264) |
| A unique-id clash on create falls back to the update path | Another save may take the id between lookup and write | [lib/services/job-service.ts:311-318](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L311-L318) |

See [Dedupe and Save](../pipeline/dedupe-and-save.md) for the handler that calls this.

### The list reads

Each pipeline step reads its own list from the database through the job service. The filters match the phase gates described on [Data Model](./data-model.md#phase-gate-flags).

| Method | Filter | Used by | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `findBacklog` | `status = backlog` | Backlog cleanup | [lib/services/job-service.ts:437-443](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L437-L443) |
| `findUnresolved` | `backlog` and `is_resolved = false` | Resolution | [lib/services/job-service.ts:416-422](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L416-L422) |
| `findUnparsed` | `backlog`, `is_resolved`, not `is_parsed` | Parsing | [lib/services/job-service.ts:427-433](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L427-L433) |
| `findExpiredWithin` | `status = expired`, then age is checked in code | Promotion | [lib/services/job-service.ts:458-466](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L458-L466) |
| `findUnclassified` | `backlog`, resolved, parsed, not classified | Classification | [lib/services/job-service.ts:488-494](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L488-L494) |
| `findNeedingScores` | `backlog`, no `alignment_score`, resolved, parsed and classified | Scoring | [lib/services/job-service.ts:469-486](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L469-L486) |
| `findBacklogByIds(ids, step)` | The given ids, `backlog`, and the one gate for that step | The add-external-jobs runner | [lib/services/job-service.ts:445-452](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L445-L452) |

`findExpiredWithin` filters in code because "the age rule lives in one function the whole pipeline shares, and SQL cannot ask it anything" ([lib/services/job-service.ts:103-112](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L103-L112)). The reference time is handed in, not read from the clock, so every job in a run is measured against one moment.

### The lookup reads

| Method | Purpose | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `findById` | Reads one whole row, writing nothing. A status change reads here first, because `update` would try to create a row and fail with a message about a missing column. | [lib/services/job-service.ts:60-65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L60-L65), [lib/services/job-service.ts:390-393](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L390-L393) |
| `findByOriginalUrlMatchKey`, `findByResolvedUrlMatchKey`, `findByCompanyAndTitle` | The three lookups dedupe's database compare runs. Each uses an index. | [lib/services/job-service.ts:66-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L66-L72), [lib/services/job-service.ts:397-410](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L397-L410) |
| `findByCompanyNameMatch`, `findByUrlMatchKey` | Back the find-jobs command. They return a small `JobSearchMatch`, not a full row, ordered newest posting first. An empty status list means every status. | [lib/services/job-service.ts:126-138](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L126-L138), [lib/services/job-service.ts:500-533](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L500-L533) |
| `findByStatuses`, `findByIds` | The dashboard and work log reads. They return a job and its employer side by side. An empty status list returns nothing, not everything. | [lib/services/job-service.ts:139-157](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L139-L157), [lib/services/job-service.ts:535-551](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L535-L551) |

`findByCompanyNameMatch` uses `contains`, which SQLite turns into case-insensitive `LIKE` for ASCII text. Prisma's SQLite provider rejects `mode: "insensitive"`, so it is not asked for ([lib/services/job-service.ts:496-499](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L496-L499)).

## The company service

The company service owns the name and match-key uniqueness rules. It never lets a clash escape as an error when a clash is ordinary news.

| Method | Behavior | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `create({ name })` | Requires a name. Computes `match_key`. On a unique-constraint clash it returns the existing company with `created: false`. | [lib/services/company-service.ts:301-326](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L301-L326) |
| `createNameless()` | Makes a company known only by a board slug, with no name and no match key. Nothing can clash. | [lib/services/company-service.ts:328-336](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L328-L336) |
| `fillName(id, name)` | Fills a nameless company's name. On a clash it leaves the target alone and returns `heldBy`, the company already holding the name. | [lib/services/company-service.ts:338-365](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L338-L365) |
| `findBySlug`, `findByMatchKey`, `findById` | Lookups. Slug lookup goes through the `AtsSlug` table. | [lib/services/company-service.ts:209-227](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L209-L227) |
| `findNeedingScores` | Companies with a backlog job and at least one empty score category | [lib/services/company-service.ts:272-288](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L272-L288) |
| `findScored` | Companies with a `scored_at` date, for the cleanup sweep | [lib/services/company-service.ts:293-299](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L293-L299) |
| `saveScores(id, scores, scoredAt)` | Merges only the categories given, and rebuilds the guessed list | [lib/services/company-service.ts:371-404](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L371-L404) |
| `writeScores(company)` | Writes the whole score block as held, empty fields included. Used after cleanup empties a stale judgement. | [lib/services/company-service.ts:452-470](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L452-L470) |
| `startEnrichment`, `saveEnrichment` | Contact-detail search state | [lib/services/company-service.ts:410-445](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L410-L445) |

The clash handling reads the driver's refusal to find which column clashed. If the error is not in the expected shape, it falls back to checking every value it tried to write, so a driver whose error format changes does not crash the caller ([lib/services/company-service.ts:186-203](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L186-L203), [lib/services/company-service.ts:234-261](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L234-L261)). A clash is only treated as ordinary if the blocking company is actually found. Otherwise the original error is re-thrown, because "a real fault" must not be filed "as everyday news" ([lib/services/company-service.ts:357-362](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L357-L362)).

`saveEnrichment` encodes a design decision. "There is no such thing as a permanently failed company." A search that found nothing writes `enrichment_status` as `failed` and leaves `enriched_at` empty, so the company is searched again next time ([lib/services/company-service.ts:419-445](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L419-L445)).

Two columns hold JSON lists, and the service narrows them when it reads. `scores_guessed` and `enrichment_flags` are checked against the known names, and a row holding another shape reads as an empty list. The reasoning is that wrongly reading a category as researched would let a guess outlive its shelf life, while wrongly reading it as a guess only costs an earlier re-score ([lib/services/company-service.ts:140-156](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L140-L156), [lib/services/company-service.ts:167-173](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L167-L173)).

## The AtsSlug service

This service has no way to remove a row. The file's header explains: "nothing in this phase takes a board off a polling list, and offering the function anyway would invite a caller nobody designed for" ([lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:5-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L5-L8)).

| Method | Behavior | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `record({ slug, company_id, parser })` | Returns the existing row with `created: false` if the slug is known. Otherwise creates one with an empty collector. Recording a slug "says only that we met this board on a posting, never that anything polls it". | [lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:66-94](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L66-L94) |
| `addCollector(slug, collector)` | Fills the collector in. If a collector is already set, it is kept: "a board is polled by whichever collector claimed it first". | [lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:96-108](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L96-L108) |
| `listForCollector` | The boards one collector polls | [lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:110-112](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L110-L112) |
| `listForCompany` | Every board one employer posts on, for promotion | [lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:114-118](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L114-L118) |
| `findBySlug` | Lookup by the unique slug | [lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts:59-61](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/ats-slug-service.ts#L59-L61) |

## The place service

The place service has two methods. `findByText(text)` reads a place by its lookup text, turning the stored outline back into a typed map shape or `null` ([lib/services/place-service.ts:62-71](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/place-service.ts#L62-L71)). `store(text, place)` upserts the place, and writes nothing when given `null`, so an unfound text is tried again next run ([lib/services/place-service.ts:73-91](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/place-service.ts#L73-L91)). A `null` outline must be written as Prisma's `JsonNull`, because a plain `null` "would mean leave the column alone" ([lib/services/place-service.ts:53-58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/place-service.ts#L53-L58)).

## The settings service

The settings service is read-only. It "reads only and throws when a setting is missing", so an empty default never reaches a collector ([prisma/schema.prisma:272-274](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L272-L274), [lib/services/settings-service.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L1-L4)). Every error points at the seed as the fix: `Setting.{field} is missing. Run "npm run db:seed" to fill it.` ([lib/services/settings-service.ts:37-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L37-L41)).

The validators differ by setting, and each difference has a reason.

| Setting | Check | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search_terms` | A list of strings. Empty is allowed. | "Emptying the search terms is how a search is switched off." | [lib/services/settings-service.ts:49-55](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L49-L55) |
| Title word lists | A non-empty list | An empty vocabulary "would quietly leave every title as it found it" | [lib/services/settings-service.ts:57-63](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L57-L63), [lib/services/settings-service.ts:93-102](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L93-L102) |
| `title_levels` | A non-empty list of `{ store, match }`, each with at least one spelling | A level with nothing to match can never fire | [lib/services/settings-service.ts:65-78](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L65-L78) |
| `source_priority_list` | Non-empty, and every entry parses as `kind:name` | An empty list would leave every contest between sources unresolved | [lib/services/settings-service.ts:80-87](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L80-L87) |
| `identifying_query_values` | A list of strings. Empty is a real answer. | It means no query value identifies a job | [lib/services/settings-service.ts:168-175](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L168-L175) |
| Resolution lane widths | Not null | A width of zero "looks like a lane that found none" | [lib/services/settings-service.ts:177-193](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L177-L193) |
| `resolution_slow_pause_seconds` | Not null. Zero is valid. | Zero means no pause at all | [lib/services/settings-service.ts:195-203](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L195-L203) |

## The trace service

The trace service is covered on [Tracing and the Run Summary](../architecture/tracing-and-run-summary.md). In short, `write` swallows and counts failures, `countsForRun` groups a run's rows, and `rowsForJobs` reads named jobs' rows back. `rowsForJobs` lives in a separate interface, `TraceJobRowsReader`, "so the ~21 hand-built TraceService stand-ins in other tests don't need this method too" ([lib/services/trace-service.ts:100-105](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/trace-service.ts#L100-L105)). This is why the trace service has no shared fake: tests build their own small stand-ins.

## The work log service

The work log service writes and lists. It has `write` and `findAll`. There is no update, "because nothing revises an entry". Its `write` has no `try`, the opposite of the trace service. A work log entry is a legal filing that cannot be regenerated once its week has passed, so a failure "has to reach the caller rather than leave the user believing a record exists" ([lib/services/work-log-service.ts:10-12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.ts#L10-L12), [lib/services/work-log-service.ts:45-52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.ts#L45-L52)). Writing the same entry twice is allowed. Telling a real second application from an accidental repeat "needs a decision of its own" ([lib/services/work-log-service.ts:10-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.ts#L10-L13)). `findAll` returns every entry, newest first, because the dashboard groups them into weeks and a week with nothing filed must still appear ([lib/services/work-log-service.ts:36-40](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.ts#L36-L40), [lib/services/work-log-service.ts:54-56](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.ts#L54-L56)).

## Fakes

A fake is an in-memory stand-in for a service, written once and shared. The naming is `fake{Subject}Service()` in `lib/services/{subject}-service.fake.ts` ([.claude/rules/services.md:12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/services.md#L12)). Each fake has its own `.fake.test.ts` file, so the stand-in is tested ([.claude/rules/naming.md:36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L36)).

| Fake | What makes it useful | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `fakeSettingsService(overrides)` | Answers real seeded defaults. A test overrides only the getters it cares about. Copied by hand from the seed, "the two move together". | [lib/services/settings-service.fake.ts:1-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.fake.ts#L1-L17) |
| `fakeJobService(jobs, overrides, companies)` | Stateful. "A job created by one call is then found by the next." It mirrors the real create, update and delete rules. | [lib/services/job-service.fake.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.fake.ts#L1-L5), [lib/services/job-service.fake.ts:65-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.fake.ts#L65-L72) |
| `fakeWorkLogService(entries, overrides)` | Holds entries in an array. Sorts on read the way the real service orders rows. | [lib/services/work-log-service.fake.ts:1-35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.fake.ts#L1-L35) |
| `fakeCompanyService`, `fakeAtsSlugService`, `fakePlaceService` | Same pattern. Present in the folder. Not read in detail here. | [lib/services/company-service.fake.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.fake.ts#L1-L5) |

The job fake shares code with the real service where it can. It imports `STEP_GATES` from the real file, so the two cannot disagree about which flag a step checks ([lib/services/job-service.ts:217-225](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L217-L225), [lib/services/job-service.fake.ts:11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.fake.ts#L11)). It also reuses `mergeJobs` and `poolJobDates` ([lib/services/job-service.fake.ts:6-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.fake.ts#L6-L7)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Test as Handler test
    participant H as saveJobs
    participant FJ as fakeJobService
    participant Real as createJobService

    Note over Test,FJ: In a unit test
    Test->>H: call with fakeJobService([])
    H->>FJ: update(entry, priorityList, queryValues)
    FJ-->>H: created
    H->>FJ: update(sameEntry, ...)
    FJ-->>H: updated, merged with held copy
    Note over Test,Real: In a flow test or a real run
    Test->>H: call with createJobService(db)
    H->>Real: update(entry, priorityList, queryValues)
    Real-->>H: created or updated or status_updated or unchanged
```

The trace proof test uses a real trace service with fake job, company and ATS-slug services, so one test covers a real database write with no job site involved ([lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts:6-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts#L6-L8), [lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts:239-251](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts#L239-L251)). <doc title="Database Commands and Safety" path="./deep-dive/data/database-commands.md">
# Database Commands and Safety

## Overview

The real `pipeline.db` holds work that cannot be recreated, such as filed work log entries and months of scored jobs. Three commands change the database, and each has a different level of danger. The design puts the danger in the command that needs it and puts a guard on that command.

| Command | What it does | Danger | Guard | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `npm run db:create FILE` | Deletes the named file and builds it fresh from the schema | Destroys data | Takes no default target and refuses the real database | [scripts/db-create.ts:33-56](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L33-L56) |
| `npm run db:migrate` | Changes the schema and keeps every row | Could fail partway | Writes a dated backup before anything else | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:67-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L67-L72) |
| `npm run db:seed` | Fills missing settings and the source priority list | Could overwrite a user's choices | Fills only what is absent, overwrites nothing | [scripts/db-seed.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L1-L5) |
| Schema check | Reads every table before a command runs | None | Stops the command if a table cannot be read | [lib/db/schema-drift.ts:17-28](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-drift.ts#L17-L28) |

The commands are registered in `package.json` ([package.json:8-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L8-L10)). `CLAUDE.md` states the rule: "`db:migrate` is the only way to change the schema", and `db:create` "takes an explicit file argument and refuses the database `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL` names in `.env`".

## How the database is found

Every command finds the database through one environment variable, `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL`. The lookup runs at call time, not when the file loads. That lets a test delete the variable and call the function, so the missing-variable case is testable ([lib/db/pipeline-env.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/pipeline-env.ts#L1-L6)).

If the variable is missing, the function throws. The message says the pipeline database "is separate from the legacy `DATABASE_URL` and does not fall back to it" ([lib/db/pipeline-env.ts:7-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/pipeline-env.ts#L7-L17)).

The same function is used in three places, so they cannot disagree.

| Caller | Use | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `createPipelineDb()` | Builds a Prisma client through the libsql adapter. A factory, not a cached singleton, because the url is read at call time. | [lib/db/pipeline-db.ts:11-18](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/pipeline-db.ts#L11-L18) |
| `prisma.config.ts` | Gives the Prisma command line its datasource. It throws when the variable is missing, "so a Prisma command run without it fails loudly instead of quietly reaching the old pipeline's database". | [prisma.config.ts:13-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma.config.ts#L13-L17) |
| `scripts/db-migrate.ts` | Finds the file to back up and migrate | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:60-61](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L60-L61) |

The connection file loads `.env` itself through `dotenv/config`. The comment explains that it sits there because this is "the one door to the database", so a service or collector never has to remember. A variable already set in the shell wins, because dotenv never overwrites one ([lib/db/pipeline-db.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/pipeline-db.ts#L1-L6)).

```mermaid
graph TB
    ENV[".env<br>PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL"] --> PE["getPipelineDatabaseUrl"]
    SHELL["shell variable<br>if set, wins"] --> PE
    PE --> PDB["createPipelineDb<br>libsql client"]
    PE --> PC["prisma.config.ts<br>Prisma command line"]
    PE --> MIG["scripts/db-migrate.ts"]
    PDB --> RUN["job-search, find-jobs,<br>score, change-status ..."]
    PC --> CRE["db-create: prisma db push"]
    PC --> MIG2["db-migrate: prisma migrate dev"]

    style ENV fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style SHELL fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style PE fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style PDB fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style PC fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style MIG fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style RUN fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style CRE fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style MIG2 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```

<!-- Sources: lib/db/pipeline-env.ts:7-17, lib/db/pipeline-db.ts:1-18, prisma.config.ts:13-17, scripts/db-migrate.ts:60-61 -->

## db:create

`db:create` rebuilds a named database from the Prisma schema. It exists to make scratch databases, such as the ones the tests use. It deletes its target, so it is built to be hard to point at the wrong file.

### What it does

1. It reads the target from the first command-line argument. With no argument it prints `Refusing: no target database given...` and exits with code 1 ([scripts/db-create.ts:33-36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L33-L36)).
2. It turns the target into an absolute path. A relative path resolves from the repo root, because Prisma resolves a relative url from the folder holding `prisma.config.ts` ([scripts/db-create.ts:15-26](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L15-L26), [scripts/db-create.ts:38](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L38)).
3. It checks the target against the real database (see below).
4. It removes the target and any sidecar files SQLite left behind: `-journal`, `-wal` and `-shm`. Rebuilding from nothing avoids merging onto an old file ([scripts/db-create.ts:58-66](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L58-L66)).
5. It runs `npx prisma db push` with the target passed through the child's environment, not whatever the parent had set ([scripts/db-create.ts:68-75](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L68-L75)).

### Why it takes no default

The script "takes no default, so a bare mistyped invocation cannot land on a database anyone cares about" ([scripts/db-create.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L1-L4)). A test helper shows the working use: the test passes the target as an argument for `db-create.ts` only, and reads the url from the environment for every other script ([lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts:58-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts#L58-L70)).

### How it recognizes the real database

The one database it refuses "no matter what" is the one named by `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL` in the repo's own `.env` file. It reads `.env` directly with `dotenv`'s parser, not from `process.env`, "so a shell that happens to export a different value cannot make a wipe of the real file look safe" ([scripts/db-create.ts:3-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L3-L7), [scripts/db-create.ts:40-47](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L40-L47)).

It then asks the filesystem whether the two paths are the same file, not whether the two strings match. The helper `isSameFile` compares the device and file number of each path ([scripts/db-create.ts:48-55](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L48-L55), [lib/utils/same-file.ts:32-48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/same-file.ts#L32-L48)). The comment gives the reasons. A disk that ignores letter case makes `Pipeline.db` another name for `pipeline.db`. A shortcut makes any name another name for it. A string comparison would hand the real database to the deletion ([scripts/db-create.ts:48-51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L48-L51), [lib/utils/same-file.ts:1-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/same-file.ts#L1-L9)).

The helper leans toward refusing. The table shows each case ([lib/utils/same-file.ts:20-59](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/same-file.ts#L20-L59)).

| Case | Answer | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Either path cannot be examined, for a reason other than "not found" | Same file (refuse) | "Refusing too much is the side of the mistake that keeps the data" |
| Both exist | Same if device and file number match | Survives capital letters, `..` segments, relative or absolute spelling, and shortcuts |
| One exists and the other does not | Different | They cannot be one file |
| Neither exists | Same if the lowercase absolute paths match | A path that does not exist yet must not be cleared as different from one it would collide with |

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    A["npm run db:create TARGET"] --> B{"Argument given?"}
    B -->|no| R1["Refuse: no target"]
    B -->|yes| C["Resolve to absolute path"]
    C --> D{".env exists and<br>names a real database?"}
    D -->|no| G
    D -->|yes| E{"isSameFile<br>target, real path?"}
    E -->|yes| R2["Refuse: this is the real database"]
    E -->|no| G["Delete target plus<br>journal, wal, shm files"]
    G --> H["prisma db push<br>with target in child env"]
    H --> I(["Created TARGET"])

    style A fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style B fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style C fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style D fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style E fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style G fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style H fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style R1 fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style R2 fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style I fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```

<!-- Sources: scripts/db-create.ts:33-77, lib/utils/same-file.ts:32-59 -->

If `.env` is missing, or has no `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL`, "there is no real file on record to protect, so any target is fine" ([scripts/db-create.ts:40-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-create.ts#L40-L41)).

Important: `db:create` uses `prisma db push`, which lays down the full current schema but no migration history. That fact is what the baseline adoption step in `db:migrate` exists for.

## db:migrate

`db:migrate` changes the schema of the real database and keeps every row. It reads the target from the environment, not from an argument, because its target is always the real database ([scripts/db-migrate.ts:59-61](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L59-L61)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User
    participant M as scripts/db-migrate.ts
    participant FS as File system
    participant L as libsql client
    participant P as prisma CLI

    User->>M: npm run db:migrate {name}
    M->>M: getPipelineDatabaseUrl, resolve path
    alt file does not exist
        M-->>User: No database, run db:create first
    else file exists
        M->>FS: copy to {db}.{timestamp}.backup
        M-->>User: Backed up database to ...
        M->>L: does _prisma_migrations exist?
        L-->>M: yes or no
        opt table missing
            loop each folder in prisma/migrations, sorted
                M->>P: migrate resolve --applied {name}
            end
        end
        M->>P: migrate dev, with --name if given
        P-->>User: applies pending change or reports already in sync
    end
```

<!-- Sources: scripts/db-migrate.ts:59-93, scripts/db-migrate.ts:23-37, scripts/db-migrate.ts:39-57 -->

### Step by step

| Step | What happens | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Find the file | Reads the url, resolves it, and refuses with `No database at ... Run db:create first` when the file is missing | There is nothing to migrate | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:59-65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L59-L65) |
| Back up | Copies the file to `{db}.{timestamp}.backup`, where the timestamp is the UTC time with colons replaced by hyphens | "A botched migration can never leave us without a copy of what came before." Written before anything else touches the file. | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:67-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L67-L72) |
| Check history | Opens the file with libsql and asks whether the `_prisma_migrations` table exists | Prisma's migrate commands assume history exists. This is how the script finds out. | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:23-37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L23-L37), [scripts/db-migrate.ts:74](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L74) |
| Adopt baseline | If there is no history table, marks every migration folder as already applied, in name order | A database built by `db:create` has the full schema but no history. Marking each migration applied "adopts that database into the normal migration workflow without replaying any of them". | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:39-57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L39-L57), [scripts/db-migrate.ts:75-77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L75-L77) |
| Migrate | Runs `prisma migrate dev`. A name given on the command line is passed as `--name`. | This is what writes and applies a new migration | [scripts/db-migrate.ts:79-93](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L79-L93) |

Each Prisma command runs with `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL` set to the resolved file, so the child process cannot reach a different database ([scripts/db-migrate.ts:51-55](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L51-L55), [scripts/db-migrate.ts:89-93](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L89-L93)).

### Safe to run when nothing changed

With no pending schema change, `migrate dev` reports "already in sync" and "touches neither the database nor the generated client — measured, which is what lets the test suite run this command safely". A real change does not regenerate the client either, so `npx prisma generate` still follows it ([scripts/db-migrate.ts:85-88](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-migrate.ts#L85-L88)).

### Backup file hygiene

Backups are written next to the database, as `pipeline.db.{timestamp}.backup`. A `.backup` file is never read for this wiki, and these files are untracked.

## db:seed

`db:seed` fills in the settings and the source priority list. It "fills what is absent and overwrites nothing", so running it after a schema change adds the new setting and leaves everything else as it was ([scripts/db-seed.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L1-L5)).

It creates no board rows and marks nothing as polled. "Polling is earned by promotion alone, and a slug list here would re-arm the boards on every reseed" ([scripts/db-seed.ts:3-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L3-L5)).

The `main` function opens the client, seeds settings, then the priority list, then disconnects in a `finally` ([scripts/db-seed.ts:222-231](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L222-L231)). The order matters. The settings step creates the row if it is missing, and the priority step needs that row ([scripts/db-seed.ts:191-193](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L191-L193), [scripts/db-seed.ts:226-227](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L226-L227)).

### Settings

If the settings row does not exist, the seed creates it with every default and prints `Settings: created the row with every default` ([scripts/db-seed.ts:121-127](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L121-L127)). If it exists, only columns holding `null` are filled. A value the user has set is never touched ([scripts/db-seed.ts:129-172](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L129-L172)). When nothing is absent, it writes nothing and says so, because `modified_at` moves on any update "and a run that changed nothing should not look like it did" ([scripts/db-seed.ts:174-180](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L174-L180)).

| Setting | Default | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `search_terms` | `Product Design`, `UX`, `Founding Design` | [scripts/db-seed.ts:12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L12) |
| `location`, `radius` | `78701`, 30 miles | [scripts/db-seed.ts:13-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L13-L14) |
| `expiry_threshold` | 8 days | [scripts/db-seed.ts:15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L15) |
| Title vocabularies | Head nouns, levels, suffixes and removal words | [scripts/db-seed.ts:18-51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L18-L51) |
| Resolution pacing | Fast lane 3, slow lane 1, pause 12 seconds | [scripts/db-seed.ts:52-54](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L52-L54) |
| `repost_gap_days` | 3 | [scripts/db-seed.ts:55](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L55) |
| `promotion_threshold` | 3.5, "just above the middle", so a flat 3 everywhere is never promoted on guesses alone | [scripts/db-seed.ts:56-60](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L56-L60) |
| `score_expiry_days`, `guessed_score_expiry_days` | 90 and 30 | [scripts/db-seed.ts:61-65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L61-L65) |
| `identifying_query_values` | `opportunityid` | [scripts/db-seed.ts:66-68](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L66-L68) |

The default `location` is a postal code, `78701`, in the seed. This is the public starting value, and the user's own value is stored in the database and never overwritten.

### The source priority list

This list is seeded apart from the other settings. It "is not filled when null and left alone after: this list is read while it holds the user's own ordering and appended to" ([scripts/db-seed.ts:71-74](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L71-L74)). The seed only appends names that are missing, and appends them at the bottom, "ranked below everything the user has already placed, rather than being slotted in on its behalf" ([scripts/db-seed.ts:186-190](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L186-L190), [scripts/db-seed.ts:213-219](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L213-L219)).

A fresh database starts with this order ([scripts/db-seed.ts:88-95](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L88-L95)).

| Order | Entries | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `collector:user`, a fixed entry for a hand-entered job. In neither registry. | [scripts/db-seed.ts:80-81](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L80-L81), [scripts/db-seed.ts:89](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L89) |
| 2 | `parser:{name}` for every distinct parser in the parser registry | [scripts/db-seed.ts:90-92](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L90-L92) |
| 3 | `collector:{name}` for every collector in the collector registry | [scripts/db-seed.ts:93](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L93) |
| 4 | `parser:{general parser name}`, last, "to reorder by hand, competing like any other source" | [scripts/db-seed.ts:86-87](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L86-L87), [scripts/db-seed.ts:94](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L94) |

Parser names are deduplicated, because the registry is keyed by domain and one parser could be reached by two domains ([scripts/db-seed.ts:83-85](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L83-L85), [scripts/db-seed.ts:90-92](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L90-L92)). Because the user's `collector:user` sits at the top, a job entered by hand wins every contested field ([prisma/schema.prisma:301-309](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L301-L309)).

### When the seed must run again

The registry rule says a change that adds, removes or renames a registry entry "runs `npm run db:seed` in the same change" ([.claude/rules/source-registry.md:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/source-registry.md#L7)). The reason is ranking. A source missing from the list "ranks below every source in it, so it loses every field two sources contest" ([.claude/rules/source-registry.md:9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/source-registry.md#L9)). The settings service also fails loudly on an invalid list, so a gap in the list does not go unnoticed for long ([lib/services/settings-service.ts:80-87](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.ts#L80-L87)). See [System Design](../architecture/system-design.md#knowledge-about-a-job-site-is-data-never-code).

A note on removals: the seed never removes entries. A renamed or removed source leaves its old name in the stored list. The code has no step that prunes it (read from `seedSourcePriority`, which only appends: [scripts/db-seed.ts:204-219](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L204-L219)).

## The schema check

Every command that reads or writes the pipeline database runs a schema check first. It exists because of a real failure. A column was added to the schema but never pushed to the live database. Every trace write of that run failed and was swallowed. A whole run's history was lost "without a word" ([lib/db/schema-check.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-check.ts#L1-L6)).

### How the check works

The check does not compare lists of columns. It reads one row from each table with `findFirst`. Prisma names every column it knows about in the SELECT it builds, "so a read that succeeds is proof the database holds them all" ([lib/db/schema-check.ts:7-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-check.ts#L7-L11)). A read on an empty table still asks for every column, so a mismatch is caught on a database with no rows at all ([lib/db/schema-check.ts:35-36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-check.ts#L35-L36)).

| Piece | Role | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `CHECKED_MODELS` | The seven model names, kept as a constant so a test can compare it against `schema.prisma` | [lib/db/schema-check.ts:21-33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-check.ts#L21-L33) |
| `schemaProbesFor(db)` | One probe per model, each a `findFirst` | [lib/db/schema-check.ts:35-47](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-check.ts#L35-L47) |
| `modelsFailingSchemaCheck(probes)` | Runs every probe, including those after a failure, and returns the failing names | [lib/db/schema-check.ts:49-63](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-check.ts#L49-L63) |
| `schemaHasDrifted(probes, print)` | Prints three lines and returns `true` when any table fails | [lib/db/schema-drift.ts:17-28](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-drift.ts#L17-L28) |

Every probe runs even after a failure, "so one trip round the rebuild loop fixes every table rather than one per table" ([lib/db/schema-check.ts:49-50](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-check.ts#L49-L50)).

The three lines it prints are ([lib/db/schema-drift.ts:24-26](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-drift.ts#L24-L26)):

```
The database does not match the schema this code expects.
Tables that could not be read: Job, Trace
Migrate it with: npm run db:migrate
```

The message names tables, not columns, because it "reads each table whole and reports only the table's name" ([lib/db/schema-drift.ts:9-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-drift.ts#L9-L10)).

### Which commands run it

Seven scripts call `schemaHasDrifted` right after opening the database. The table shows where.

| Script | Line of the check | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/job-search.ts` | 49 | [scripts/job-search.ts:49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L49) |
| `scripts/add-external-jobs.ts` | 45 | [scripts/add-external-jobs.ts:45](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/add-external-jobs.ts#L45) |
| `scripts/change-status.ts` | 115 | [scripts/change-status.ts:115](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L115) |
| `scripts/find-jobs.ts` | 106 | [scripts/find-jobs.ts:106](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L106) |
| `scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts` | 37 | [scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts:37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts#L37) |
| `scripts/score-gather.ts` | 48 | [scripts/score-gather.ts:48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-gather.ts#L48) |
| `scripts/score-save.ts` | 71 | [scripts/score-save.ts:71](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-save.ts#L71) |

`db:create`, `db:migrate` and `db:seed` do not run the check. That is deliberate in practice. `db:migrate` is the fix the check points to, and `db:create` builds from nothing. `db:seed` also skips it (inferred: the seed script has no call to `schemaHasDrifted`, which was checked by search).

The file header of `schema-drift.ts` says "Five commands each held a byte-for-byte copy" before the check was shared ([lib/db/schema-drift.ts:12-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/db/schema-drift.ts#L12-L14)). Seven commands use it now, so the number in the comment describes the history, not the current count.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> OpenDb: command starts
    OpenDb --> Probing: createPipelineDb
    Probing --> Drifted: any findFirst throws
    Probing --> Ready: all seven tables readable
    Drifted --> Stopped: print three lines, exit code 1
    Ready --> Working: command does its job
    Working --> [*]
    Stopped --> [*]

    note right of Drifted
        Fix: npm run db:migrate
    end note
```

<!-- Sources: lib/db/schema-check.ts:35-63, lib/db/schema-drift.ts:17-28, scripts/job-search.ts:49-52 -->

## How the pieces fit in daily use

| Situation | Command | What protects you |
|---|---|---|
| New clone, no database | `db:create {file}`, then `db:seed` | `db:create` takes an explicit target and refuses the real one |
| You edited `schema.prisma` | `db:migrate {name}`, then `npx prisma generate` if the client is stale | A dated backup is written first |
| Added a collector or parser | `db:seed` in the same change | The seed appends the new name to the bottom of the priority list |
| A command says the database does not match | `db:migrate` | The schema check stopped the command before any write |
| Need a scratch database for a test | `db:create {temp-file}` | The test sets `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL` to the scratch file, so the real file is never touched ([lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts:58-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/trace-proof.test.ts#L58-L70)) |

# Scoring

## Overview

A job search can collect, clean and sort jobs with plain code. It cannot decide whether a job is a good fit, or whether an employer is a good place to work. That takes judgment and live web research, which an agent does.

A pipeline run cannot stop and wait for an agent to think. So scoring is split into two commands with the agent between them. The first command, `score:gather`, writes out everything that needs a score. The agent works it out. The second command, `score:save`, writes the answers back. This is stated in the orchestrator's own header comment ([lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts:1-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L1-L8)).

The `score-backlog` skill runs the whole loop. The `job-search` skill calls it straight after the pipeline finishes, handing over the run identifier so scoring records join the same run ([.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L48)). See [The Job Search Run](../architecture/job-search-run.md) for the deterministic half.

### At a glance

| Component | Responsibility | Key file | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runScoringGather` | Cleans stale scores, lists who still needs a score, leaves a trace row for each | `lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts` | [scoring.ts:47-184](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L47-L184) |
| `runScoringSave` | Writes the agent's answers, marks jobs as judged, promotes companies | `lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts` | [scoring.ts:228-450](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L228-L450) |
| `score:gather` command | Opens the database, runs the gather, writes a JSON work file | `scripts/score-gather.ts` | [score-gather.ts:25-117](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-gather.ts#L25-L117) |
| `score:save` command | Reads the agent's answer file, runs the save, optionally prints the run summary | `scripts/score-save.ts` | [score-save.ts:43-137](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-save.ts#L43-L137) |
| `promoteCompanies` | Moves a well-scored company onto a polling list | `lib/handlers/company-promotion.ts` | [company-promotion.ts:103-163](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/company-promotion.ts#L103-L163) |
| `isJobJudged` | Decides whether scoring has judged a job | `lib/utils/job-judged.ts` | [job-judged.ts:15-22](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-judged.ts#L15-L22) |
| `score-backlog` skill | Tells the agent what to do in four phases | `.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md` | [SKILL.md:17-126](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L17-L126) |

## The two-command shape

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["npm run score:gather"] --> B["Work file<br>runId, jobs, companies,<br>warnings, failure"]
    B --> C["Agent reads rubrics<br>and sends helpers"]
    C --> D["Answer file<br>runId, jobs, companies"]
    D --> E["npm run score:save"]
    E --> F[("pipeline.db")]
    A --> F
    style A fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style B fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style C fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style D fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style E fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style F fill:#161b22,stroke:#30363d,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts:1-8, scripts/score-gather.ts:83-91, scripts/score-save.ts:59-65 -->

The work file and the answer file are plain JSON. The gather command writes `runId`, `jobs`, `companies`, `warnings` and `failure` ([scripts/score-gather.ts:84-91](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-gather.ts#L84-L91)). The save command reads `runId`, `jobs` and `companies` back. It treats the file as untrusted and casts it once, in one place ([scripts/score-save.ts:24-31](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-save.ts#L24-L31), [scripts/score-save.ts:61-65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-save.ts#L61-L65)).

Both commands refuse to run if the database does not match the schema the code expects. They call `schemaHasDrifted` first and set a failing exit code ([scripts/score-gather.ts:48-51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-gather.ts#L48-L51), [scripts/score-save.ts:71-74](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-save.ts#L71-L74)).

## Gather: cleaning first, then listing

The gather does cleanup before it asks who needs a score. The order matters. If a company's old score were cleared after the list was read, that company would be missing from its own re-score. The code comments say this directly ([lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts:113-116](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L113-L116)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant CLI as score-gather.ts
    participant O as runScoringGather
    participant H as backlog-cleanup handlers
    participant S as Services
    participant T as Trace
    CLI->>O: settings, companies, jobs, trace, runId
    O->>S: read expiry settings
    O->>S: findBacklog
    O->>H: cleanBacklogJobs
    O->>S: saveJobs (expired jobs land on disk)
    O->>S: companies.findScored
    O->>H: cleanBacklogCompanies
    O->>S: saveCompanies
    O->>S: findNeedingScores (jobs)
    O->>S: findNeedingScores (companies)
    O->>T: job_entered per job, company_entered per company
    O-->>CLI: jobs, companies, warnings, failure
```

<!-- Sources: lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts:68-175 -->

### Who counts as needing a score

| Kind | Rule | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job | Status is `backlog`, no alignment score yet, and the link is followed, the posting is read and the job is classified | [job-service.ts:469-486](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L469-L486) |
| Company | Has at least one backlog job, and at least one of its four category scores is empty | [company-service.ts:272-288](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L272-L288) |

The four categories are employee satisfaction, customer satisfaction, work/life balance and political alignment. They live in one list, `SCORE_CATEGORIES`, so a fifth category joins every check by being added there ([lib/services/company-service.ts:16-21](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L16-L21)).

### Scores that go stale

Backlog cleanup empties old company scores so employers get researched again. The two ages come from settings. The seed values are 90 days for a full score and 30 days for a guessed category ([scripts/db-seed.ts:58-65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L58-L65)).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Company has a scored_at date?"] -->|no| K["Kept"]
    A -->|yes| B["Age past score expiry?"]
    B -->|yes| C["All four scores cleared<br>scored_at reset"]
    B -->|no| D["Any guessed categories<br>and age past guess expiry?"]
    D -->|yes| E["Only guessed categories cleared<br>scored_at stays"]
    D -->|no| K
    style A fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style B fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style C fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style D fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style E fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style K fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts:203-246 -->

Full expiry is checked first. A company old enough to lose everything should not keep its researched scores while losing only its guesses ([backlog-cleanup.ts:221-229](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L221-L229)). A guess is a placeholder, so it goes stale sooner ([backlog-cleanup.ts:231-243](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup.ts#L231-L243)). The age test is inclusive: a score exactly at the limit counts as expired ([lib/utils/job-age.ts:61-63](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-age.ts#L61-L63)).

## The agent's work: four phases

The `score-backlog` skill is the procedure the agent follows ([SKILL.md](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md)).

| Phase | What happens | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Gather | Run `score:gather`, read the work file, stop on a failure or when both lists are empty | [SKILL.md:17-37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L17-L37) |
| 2. Companies | One helper per company, because a company means live web research | [SKILL.md:39-61](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L39-L61) |
| 3. Jobs | Jobs with a posting description go to helpers 10 at a time. A job with no description gets its own helper, which must open the posting first | [SKILL.md:63-97](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L63-L97) |
| 4. Save | Write the answer file and run `score:save` after each batch. Add `--summary` on the last batch | [SKILL.md:99-126](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L99-L126) |

Saving each batch as it returns is deliberate. A run that stops halfway keeps the research it already paid for ([SKILL.md:111](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L111), [scripts/score-save.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/score-save.ts#L1-L5)).

### The two rubrics

| Rubric | What it scores | Scale | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Job rubric | How well a job fits the candidate. 4-5 for senior or lead design roles with real ownership in complex domains. 2-3 for visual-heavy, large-process or research-heavy roles. 1 for management or pure marketing design | 1 to 5 | [job-rubric.md:6-28](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/job-rubric.md#L6-L28) |
| Company rubric | Four categories, each backed by a web search: Glassdoor or Blind, Trustpilot or BBB, work/life signals, and political alignment | 1 to 5 | [company-rubric.md:3-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/company-rubric.md#L3-L25) |

The job rubric is paired with a candidate profile. The real profile is private and untracked. A made-up example shows the shape: who the candidate is, the target role, core strengths and a skills inventory ([.alignment-info.example.md:1-30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/.alignment-info.example.md#L1-L30)). Splitting public rules from the private profile means the scoring rules can be shared while the person stays private.

### Guessed categories

When a company has no public information for a category, the rubric tells the helper to award a 3 and mark it guessed ([company-rubric.md:27-29](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/company-rubric.md#L27-L29)). The helper returns `guessed: true` for that category ([SKILL.md:55-57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L55-L57)).

Why track it? A guess is not research. Marking it lets cleanup expire it after 30 days instead of 90. It also keeps a company from being promoted on guesses alone: a flat 3 everywhere averages 3, below the 3.5 promotion bar ([scripts/db-seed.ts:55-60](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L55-L60)).

## Save: one entry at a time

The save is built so one bad entry costs only itself. Each job write and each company write sits in its own `try`. A failure records a trace row with reason `db_write_failed` and a warning, then the loop continues ([lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts:303-318](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L303-L318), [lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts:368-382](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L368-L382)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant CLI as score-save.ts
    participant O as runScoringSave
    participant J as JobService
    participant C as CompanyService
    participant P as promoteCompanies
    participant T as Trace
    CLI->>O: jobScores, companyScores, runId, scoredAt
    loop each job answer
        alt has a numeric alignment_score
            O->>J: update score and rationale
            O->>T: job_scored
        else no score
            O->>T: scoring_failed with the helper's reason
        end
    end
    loop each company answer
        alt has scores
            O->>C: saveScores (merge only asked categories)
            O->>T: company_scored or company_partially_scored
        else no scores
            O->>T: company_scoring_failed
        end
    end
    O->>J: mark is_judged where isJobJudged is true
    O->>P: companies saved in this batch
    P->>T: company_promoted or company_promotion_skipped
    O-->>CLI: warnings, failure, traceFailures
```

<!-- Sources: lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts:272-441, lib/handlers/company-promotion.ts:103-163 -->

| Detail | What the code does | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Job's collector | Looked up from the job row, not from the answer | An answer carries only an id | [scoring.ts:263-270](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L263-L270) |
| Failure reasons | Jobs: `no_posting_url`, `posting_unreadable`, `scoring_agent_failed`. Companies: `no_company_name`, `scoring_agent_failed` | A closed list of words | [scoring.ts:186-187](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L186-L187) |
| Partial company writes | `saveScores` writes only the categories it was given and rebuilds the guessed list | A company is re-picked when any category is empty, so a write must not blank the other three | [company-service.ts:366-397](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L366-L397) |
| Guessed marker in the trace | Any guessed category makes the trace event `company_partially_scored` with reason `insufficient_research` | The run summary can tell full research from partial | [scoring.ts:338-358](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L338-L358) |
| Judged pass | Runs after the company half | An employer scored in the same batch counts | [scoring.ts:386-419](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L386-L419) |

### What "judged" means

`isJobJudged` returns true when the job has a fit score. It also returns true when the employer holds any category score, even if the job's own score failed. The reason is that the agent sometimes cannot open a posting, and the job has still been looked at through its employer ([lib/utils/job-judged.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-judged.ts#L1-L5), [lib/utils/job-judged.ts:15-22](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-judged.ts#L15-L22)). The marker is not traced. It only changes how the dashboard shows a job ([scoring.ts:386-391](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L386-L391)). See [Judging Steps](../pipeline/judging-steps.md).

## Promotion onto a polling list

A company that scores well is worth watching directly. Promotion does not change the company. It changes the board rows in the ATS slug table by filling in the collector that polls that board from now on ([company-promotion.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/company-promotion.ts#L1-L6)). After that, the company's postings arrive first-hand instead of through an aggregator. See [Collection](../pipeline/collection.md).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Company saved in this batch"] --> B["All four scores present?"]
    B -->|no| S1["skipped: not_fully_scored"]
    B -->|yes| C["Average greater than threshold?"]
    C -->|no| S2["skipped: below_promotion_threshold"]
    C -->|yes| D["Any board with a pollable parser?"]
    D -->|no| S3["skipped: no_pollable_board"]
    D -->|yes| E["Any of those boards with no collector yet?"]
    E -->|no| S4["skipped: already_polled"]
    E -->|yes| P["addCollector on each<br>company_promoted"]
    style A fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style B fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style C fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style D fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style E fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style S1 fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style S2 fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style S3 fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style S4 fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style P fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/company-promotion.ts:57-101 -->

Key rules, all read from the handler:

- The bar is strict. An average exactly equal to the threshold does not qualify ([company-promotion.ts:81-84](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/company-promotion.ts#L81-L84)). The seed value is 3.5 ([scripts/db-seed.ts:60](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L60)).
- A parser maps to a collector through one table, `POLLABLE_COLLECTORS_BY_PARSER`. Ten sources are listed. A parser missing from it can be read but not polled, which is why a Dribbble company is never promoted ([company-promotion.ts:27-42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/company-promotion.ts#L27-L42)).
- A failed board lookup costs only that company. It becomes a warning, and the company is judged again next run ([company-promotion.ts:126-143](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/company-promotion.ts#L126-L143)).
- Trace rows are written only when the caller passes a trace, a run id and a step name. That lets the function run outside a job search ([company-promotion.ts:111-122](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/company-promotion.ts#L111-L122)).
- Promotion runs only when the batch saved at least one company, so a jobs-only batch does not read the setting ([scoring.ts:421-441](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L421-L441)).

## Failure reporting

Both orchestrators use a shared failure tracker. `at("name", fn)` runs a step, records its name and reason if it throws, and lets one outer `catch` end the run. The result then reports `failure.at` and `failure.reason` ([scoring.ts:60-66](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L60-L66), [scoring.ts:442-449](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/scoring.ts#L442-L449)). The commands print `Run stopped at ...` and set a failing exit code, so the skill checks status rather than guessing from text ([SKILL.md:130](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L130)). See [Tracing and the Run Summary](../architecture/tracing-and-run-summary.md).
