# Status Changes and the Work Log

## Overview

Everything else in this app runs inside a job search. A status change does not. It happens because the user says a job moved: they applied, had a phone screen, or had an interview. This is the first command that no job search starts ([scripts/change-status.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L1-L4)).

Three of those statuses matter in law. Each one files a **work log entry**, which is a record for the Texas Workforce Commission (TWC). The record cannot be rebuilt once its week has passed ([lib/handlers/status-change.ts:6-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/status-change.ts#L6-L8)). So the code is built around one rule: write the filing exactly once, or fail loudly enough that the user can act.

This page covers two commands and one skill. `find-jobs` finds the job the user means. `change-status` writes the status and the entry. The `change-status` skill drives both.

### At a glance

| Component | Responsibility | Key file | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `find-jobs` | Read-only lookup of jobs by link, else by employer name | `scripts/find-jobs.ts` | [find-jobs.ts:65-82](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L65-L82) |
| `change-status` | Validates a submission file, then runs the orchestrator | `scripts/change-status.ts` | [change-status.ts:37-160](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L37-L160) |
| `runStatusChange` | Calls the two handlers in a fixed order | `lib/orchestrators/status-change.ts` | [status-change.ts:43-93](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/status-change.ts#L43-L93) |
| `changeStatuses` | Writes each status and its work log entry | `lib/handlers/status-change.ts` | [status-change.ts:65-188](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/status-change.ts#L65-L188) |
| `enrichCompanies` | Searches for each employer's address, phone and website | `lib/handlers/enrichment.ts` | [enrichment.ts:54-186](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/enrichment.ts#L54-L186) |
| `activityFromStatus` | Maps a status to the TWC wording | `lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts` | [work-log-activity.ts:18-30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L18-L30) |
| Work log service | The only writer of the work log table | `lib/services/work-log-service.ts` | [work-log-service.ts:34-58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.ts#L34-L58) |
| Company search tool | One paid web search about an employer | `lib/tools/company-search.ts` | [company-search.ts:69-105](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L69-L105) |

## The whole flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U["User names a job<br>and a new status"] --> SK["change-status skill"]
    SK --> FJ["find-jobs<br>read only"]
    FJ --> SK
    SK --> CS["change-status<br>submission file"]
    CS --> H1["Handler 1<br>status + work log entry"]
    H1 --> H2["Handler 2<br>employer contact search"]
    H2 --> R["Report lines"]
    R --> SK
    style U fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style SK fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style FJ fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style CS fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style H1 fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style H2 fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style R fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: .claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md:22-84, lib/orchestrators/status-change.ts:57-86 -->

## Finding the job: `find-jobs`

The user has no job id. A person names a job by pasting its link or by saying who is hiring ([scripts/find-jobs.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L1-L6)). So this command turns those words into ids. It only reads. A search that matches nothing is a normal answer, not a failure ([find-jobs.ts:8-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L8-L9)).

| Step | What happens | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Clean the link | The link is reduced to a match key the same way stored links were, so share-button tracking values do not block a match | [find-jobs.ts:110-116](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L110-L116) |
| 2. Try the link | A link can point at one exact job, so it goes first. A match answers with `found_by: "link"` | [find-jobs.ts:71-77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L71-L77) |
| 3. Fall back to the employer | If the link matched nothing, the employer name part searches that employer's jobs. Answer: `found_by: "employer"` | [find-jobs.ts:79-81](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L79-L81) |
| 4. Report the link problem | `link_problem` is `no_match`, `not_a_link` or `null` | [find-jobs.ts:18-19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L18-L19) |

The role is never searched in code. The agent reads the employer's jobs and picks the one the user's role words describe ([find-jobs.ts:4-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L4-L6)). The skill says why: the user writes shorthand that no stored title contains ([SKILL.md:17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L17)).

The `--statuses` flag narrows the search. The skill picks it from the status being set. For example, moving a job to `screening` searches only jobs already applied for ([SKILL.md:33-39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L33-L39)). A trailing comma in the flag is dropped, and an empty flag means no narrowing ([find-jobs.ts:30-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs.ts#L30-L41)).

## Which statuses file an entry

The app accepts twelve statuses ([lib/utils/job-status.ts:24-41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L24-L41)). Only three write a work log entry. They are listed once, in `WORK_LOG_STATUSES` ([job-status.ts:49-53](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L49-L53)). The statuses `test` and `offer` are active job states but are not filing activities ([job-status.ts:46-48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L46-L48)).

| Status the user sets | Wording filed with the TWC | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app. sent` | `Applied for job` | [work-log-activity.ts:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L19) |
| `screening` | `Had phone screen` | [work-log-activity.ts:20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L20) |
| `interview` | `Had interview` | [work-log-activity.ts:21](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L21) |
| Any other status | No entry | [work-log-activity.ts:27-30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L27-L30) |

The three phrases are fixed values. The TWC rejects a filing whose wording the form does not recognize ([work-log-activity.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L1-L4)). The map is typed against the status list, so adding a status without wording fails to compile instead of silently writing nothing ([work-log-activity.ts:15-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L15-L17)).

The trigger is the status that arrives, not the path the job service took. A job going from backlog to `app. sent` takes a different service path than a job already active. Hooking the entry to a path would skip the first entry of nearly every job ([lib/handlers/status-change.ts:10-15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/status-change.ts#L10-L15)).

## Why legal writes happen before searches

The orchestrator calls two handlers in a fixed order. Every status and every entry in the batch is written before the first search starts. The comment states the reason. Searches are slow and a time limit can cut them short. A command cut short should lose searches and never lose a filing ([lib/orchestrators/status-change.ts:4-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/status-change.ts#L4-L13)). Two handlers called in order make this structural rather than a comment someone can move.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant S as change-status.ts
    participant O as runStatusChange
    participant H as changeStatuses
    participant W as WorkLogService
    participant E as enrichCompanies
    participant X as CompanySearch
    S->>O: changes, services, now
    O->>H: changes
    loop each change
        H->>H: find job, settle employer
        H->>H: write status
        H->>W: write entry if status calls for one
    end
    H-->>O: changed jobs and warnings
    O->>O: keep jobs with entry_written, one per employer
    O->>E: targets
    loop each employer
        E->>X: one search
        X-->>E: titles and text
        E->>E: save contact details and doubts
    end
    O-->>S: changes, companies, warnings
```

<!-- Sources: lib/orchestrators/status-change.ts:57-92, lib/handlers/status-change.ts:65-188, lib/handlers/enrichment.ts:54-186 -->

### Per job: the order inside `applyChange`

| Order | Step | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Read the job first | The job service would create a row for an unknown id and fail with a message about a missing column, which names the wrong fault. Reading first returns `no_such_job` | [status-change.ts:68-75](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/status-change.ts#L68-L75) |
| 2 | Settle the employer | A supplied name finds or creates that employer and links the job. The link is written first because an active job is frozen to everything but its status | [status-change.ts:85-106](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/status-change.ts#L85-L106) |
| 3 | Stop if the filing has no employer name | An entry naming a blank employer is the one thing the asking exists to prevent. The job keeps its old status | [status-change.ts:108-110](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/status-change.ts#L108-L110) |
| 4 | Write the status | Written before the entry | [status-change.ts:114-128](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/status-change.ts#L114-L128) |
| 5 | Write the entry | Employer name, job title and wording are copied onto the row | [status-change.ts:138-153](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/status-change.ts#L138-L153) |

No database transaction exists anywhere in this codebase, so nothing can undo either write. The protection is the order plus a failure the user can see ([status-change.ts:114-116](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/status-change.ts#L114-L116)).

The name check asks whether a usable name exists, not whether an employer is attached. Every hiring board the app polls creates an employer row with a slug and no name, so the obvious check would pass while the name is still blank ([status-change.ts:54-63](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/status-change.ts#L54-L63)).

### The work log service writes loudly

The work log service has no `try` block, on purpose. The trace service swallows a failed write and counts it, because losing a trace row costs less than losing a run. A work log row is a filing, so a failure must reach the caller ([work-log-service.ts:46-52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.ts#L46-L52)). The entry stores the employer name and job title as plain copies, and the job id has no relation. A filing already made survives the job or employer changing or going away ([work-log-service.ts:4-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.ts#L4-L8)). Nothing revises an entry, so the service has no update ([work-log-service.ts:10-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/work-log-service.ts#L10-L13)). See [Services](../data/services.md).

### Outcomes

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> ReadJob
    ReadJob --> no_such_job: no row holds the id
    ReadJob --> needs_company_name: status files an entry, employer has no name
    ReadJob --> WriteStatus
    WriteStatus --> entry_failed: status write threw
    WriteStatus --> changed_no_entry: status files no entry
    WriteStatus --> no_title: no title to file under
    WriteStatus --> WriteEntry
    WriteEntry --> changed_entry: entry written
    WriteEntry --> entry_failed: entry write threw
    no_such_job --> [*]
    needs_company_name --> [*]
    changed_no_entry --> [*]
    no_title --> [*]
    changed_entry --> [*]
    entry_failed --> [*]
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/status-change.ts:72-153, lib/types/changed-job.ts:8-13 -->

The outcome set is closed. A skill reads it to decide whether to come back and ask for an employer name ([lib/types/changed-job.ts:1-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/types/changed-job.ts#L1-L7)). The report builder fails to compile if an outcome has no printed line ([status-change-report.ts:39-44](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/status-change-report.ts#L39-L44)). The two wordings "needs an employer name" and "no job holds that id" are fixed, because the skill must tell them apart ([status-change-report.ts:9-12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/status-change-report.ts#L9-L12)).

## Checking the submission before touching anything

`change-status` reads a JSON array from `--in`. A bad status anywhere refuses the whole submission before the database is opened. Half a batch landing is worse than none, because the user would have to work out which half ([change-status.ts:5-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L5-L9), [change-status.ts:100-108](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L100-L108)). Each refusal names the entry's position so a skill-written file can be fixed without counting ([change-status.ts:62-63](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L62-L63)). The schema drift check then runs before any write ([change-status.ts:115-118](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L115-L118)).

## The employer contact search

A TWC filing asks for an address, a phone number and a website. After the entries are safe, the second handler searches for them ([lib/handlers/enrichment.ts:1-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/enrichment.ts#L1-L7)).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Target employer"] --> B{"Row exists?"}
    B -->|no| F1["failed + warning"]
    B -->|yes| C{"Already enriched?"}
    C -->|yes| F2["already_filled"]
    C -->|no| D{"Has a name?"}
    D -->|no| F3["no_name"]
    D -->|yes| E["Mark search started<br>build query with place"]
    E --> G{"Search ran?"}
    G -->|no credential| F4["no_credential + warning"]
    G -->|error| F5["failed + warning"]
    G -->|yes| H["Find first result whose title matches the name"]
    H --> I["Read contact only from that result"]
    I --> J["Work out doubts<br>save"]
    J --> K{"Any field filled?"}
    K -->|yes| F6["filled"]
    K -->|no| F7["found_nothing"]
    style A fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style B fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style C fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style D fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style E fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style G fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style H fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3

    style J fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3

    style F1 fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3

    style F7 fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/enrichment.ts:54-167 -->

| Rule | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Only jobs whose entry was written send their employer to the search | A job with no filing has no contact details to appear on | [orchestrator status-change.ts:65-69](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/status-change.ts#L65-L69) |
| One search per employer per batch | A search that found nothing leaves the employer open, so ten jobs at one unfindable employer would pay for ten searches | [orchestrator status-change.ts:72-84](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/status-change.ts#L72-L84) |
| Skip employers already filled in | The service is paid per search | [enrichment.ts:9-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/enrichment.ts#L9-L10), [enrichment.ts:73-82](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/enrichment.ts#L73-L82) |
| Never search a blank name | A query from a blank name matches every result and returns a stranger's address | [enrichment.ts:11-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/enrichment.ts#L11-L13) |
| Add the job's matched place to the query | A common employer name finds the wrong business on its own | [lib/utils/enrichment-query.ts:4-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/enrichment-query.ts#L4-L6) |
| Match the name first, read values only from that result | Scanning every result for a value while checking the name on only the first could take an unrelated organization's address | [enrichment.ts:136-142](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/enrichment.ts#L136-L142) |
| A name matches when either string contains the other, and a blank never matches | An empty string is contained by every string | [lib/utils/enrichment-name-match.ts:19-26](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/enrichment-name-match.ts#L19-L26) |
| A search that found nothing leaves the employer open | There is no permanently failed employer. It is asked about again next time | [company-service.ts:419-445](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/company-service.ts#L419-L445) |

### Doubts

After a search fills details in, the code raises **doubts**. A doubt is a detail worth checking before the user files. There are three ([lib/utils/enrichment-doubts.ts:19-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/enrichment-doubts.ts#L19-L23)).

| Doubt | Raised when | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `missing_address` | No address was found. The address is the field the form needs most | [enrichment-doubts.ts:41-42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/enrichment-doubts.ts#L41-L42) |
| `address_outside_us` | An address exists but has no state and ZIP pattern and no "United States" | [enrichment-doubts.ts:14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/enrichment-doubts.ts#L14), [enrichment-doubts.ts:43-45](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/enrichment-doubts.ts#L43-L45) |
| `missing_phone` | No phone was found | [enrichment-doubts.ts:47-49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/enrichment-doubts.ts#L47-L49) |

A missing website raises nothing, because the form does not ask for one ([enrichment-doubts.ts:51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/enrichment-doubts.ts#L51)). A missing address and an outside-US address are one decision, since an absent address cannot also be foreign. The file notes that two of six measured employers returned no contact details at all, so doubts are an ordinary result ([enrichment-doubts.ts:5-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/enrichment-doubts.ts#L5-L7)).

### The search tool

The tool wraps a paid Apify actor and returns only a title and a text snippet per result ([company-search.ts:42-58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L42-L58), [company-search.ts:99-102](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L99-L102)). The token is read at call time from `APIFY_API_TOKEN`, and a missing one throws a dedicated `MissingSearchCredentialError` ([company-search.ts:72-77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L72-L77)). A separate error type lets the run say different things about a never-set credential and a failing service ([company-search.ts:32-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L32-L34)). The call has a 60 second limit, handed to the service so it stops the paid run and not only our wait ([company-search.ts:27-30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L27-L30)). The actual call is injected, which keeps the tool testable without paying for a real search ([company-search.ts:19-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L19-L25)). See [Testing](../quality/testing.md).

The search is awaited in full. The earlier code started it and never waited, and Node kills work still in flight at exit, so the lookup ran only some of the time ([change-status.ts:129-131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L129-L131)).

## The skill's four phases

| Phase | What the agent does | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Read the request | Split into one item per job. Match each status to one of the twelve. Stop if one matches none | [SKILL.md:22-29](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L22-L29) |
| 2. Find each job | Run `find-jobs`. Ask only if the result is empty or ambiguous. Never widen a search without asking | [SKILL.md:31-56](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L31-L56) |
| 3. Change the statuses | Write a scratch file and run `change-status` | [SKILL.md:58-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L58-L70) |
| 4. Finish held-back jobs | Ask the user for the employer name of any job that needed one, then run again naming only those jobs | [SKILL.md:72-84](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/change-status/SKILL.md#L72-L84) |

There is no dashboard page that announces a filing in this phase. The printed report is where the user learns a legal record exists ([change-status.ts:11-12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/change-status.ts#L11-L12)). The dashboard does have a work log view, covered in [The Read-Only Dashboard](../dashboard/dashboard.md).

No trace rows are written anywhere in this flow. A hand-made change is not a job passing through a pipeline step, and counting it would put work in the funnel that the pipeline never did ([lib/handlers/status-change.ts:17-19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/status-change.ts#L17-L19)). That is why the report is built from handler results rather than from the shared run summary ([status-change-report.ts:5-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/status-change-report.ts#L5-L7)). See [Tracing and the Run Summary](../architecture/tracing-and-run-summary.md).

# External Jobs and Resumes

## Overview

A job search only finds jobs its collectors know how to pull. The user also finds jobs on their own: a link from a friend, a post on a social site, a company page. This page covers how those jobs get into the same database and the same scoring, and how the user then makes a resume for one of them.

There are three agent skills and two commands here.

| Skill or command | Purpose | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add-external-jobs` skill | Reads each pasted link, runs the add command, then scores the backlog and reports | [SKILL.md:11-94](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md#L11-L94) |
| `npm run add-external-jobs` | Runs only the user's links through the job search's steps | [scripts/add-external-jobs.ts:24-88](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/add-external-jobs.ts#L24-L88) |
| `generate-resume` skill | Finds a saved job, reads the live posting, picks resume items, renders a PDF | [SKILL.md:22-199](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L22-L199) |
| `npm run fetch-rendered-page` | Prints a page's finished HTML after its scripts have run | [scripts/fetch-rendered-page.ts:13-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/fetch-rendered-page.ts#L13-L34) |

### At a glance

| Component | Responsibility | Key file | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runAddExternalJobs` | Runs the pipeline handlers for only the ids it saved this run | `lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts` | [add-external-jobs.ts:85-327](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L85-L327) |
| `letJobsThrough` | Keeps a job in the backlog when the pipeline cannot judge it, and records why | `lib/handlers/let-through.ts` | [let-through.ts:68-103](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L68-L103) |
| `addedJobsReport` | Turns outcomes, warnings and failure into printed lines | `lib/utils/added-jobs-report.ts` | [added-jobs-report.ts:18-56](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/added-jobs-report.ts#L18-L56) |
| `createRenderedPageFetcher` | One page, one headless browser, closed afterward | `lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts` | [rendered-page-fetcher.ts:112-131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L112-L131) |
| `createRenderedPageBrowser` | One browser, many pages, used by the add run's parsing step | `lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts` | [rendered-page-fetcher.ts:145-164](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L145-L164) |

## Adding external jobs

### Why a separate runner

The job search reads whole tables: every job waiting at each step, whenever it was collected. If the add command did the same, it would also push the user's older waiting jobs through the steps. So this runner reads back only the ids it has saved during this run. A job that was already waiting before the run is never touched ([lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L1-L5)). It collects from no job source.

It reuses the same handlers as the job search. It does not copy their logic. This follows the rule that each job in the pipeline has one implementation, and that no part assumes it is inside a job search ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md)). See [The Job Search Run](../architecture/job-search-run.md).

### The submission

Each submission has a `link` and optionally a `title`, `employer` and `description` ([add-external-jobs.ts:37-42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L37-L42)). The skill reads each posting first and fills these fields in, because the agent can read a page that a collector cannot ([SKILL.md:23-32](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md#L23-L32)). A link whose page will not open is set aside, and the user is asked for a title and employer. If the user does not know them, the link is kept with neither. The agent must not guess ([SKILL.md:16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md#L16)).

Every added job is filed under the collector name `user` ([add-external-jobs.ts:34-35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L34-L35)). A link that is not a web address is refused with a warning and never becomes a job ([add-external-jobs.ts:121-124](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L121-L124)).

### The steps, in order

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Submissions"] --> B["Refuse non web addresses<br>build first list"]
    B --> C["normalize, associate, dedupe, save"]
    C --> D["Reset rechecked verdicts<br>back to backlog"]
    D --> E["Resolution<br>only if links need following"]
    E --> F["dedupe, save"]
    F --> G["Parsing<br>rendered page browser"]
    G --> H["normalize, associate, dedupe"]
    H --> I["let through after parsing"]
    I --> J["save"]
    J --> K["Classification<br>needs home location"]
    K --> L["let through after classification"]
    L --> M["save"]
    M --> N["Look up outcome per link"]
    style A fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style B fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style C fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style D fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style E fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style F fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style G fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style H fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style I fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style J fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style K fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style L fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style M fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style N fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts:119-248, 266-323 -->

Each stretch ends at the database, and the next stretch asks the database for the tracked ids at the right marker. The lookups use `findBacklogByIds` with a step name: `"resolution"`, `"parsing"` and `"classification"` ([add-external-jobs.ts:161](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L161), [add-external-jobs.ts:189](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L189), [add-external-jobs.ts:238](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L238)). The `tracked` set grows with every id a save hands back. A job merged into an existing row continues under that row's id ([add-external-jobs.ts:95-100](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L95-L100)). See [Dedupe and Save](../pipeline/dedupe-and-save.md), [Resolution](../pipeline/resolution.md) and [Parsing](../pipeline/parsing.md).

Details that differ from a job search:

| Detail | What the code does | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rechecked verdicts reset | A link matching a saved job with status `expired`, `too far`, `unresolvable` or `unparseable` is sent back to `backlog` with the resolved, parsed and classified markers cleared | Adding a link again means "look at this again". Other statuses, such as `app. sent`, stay as they are | [add-external-jobs.ts:150-159](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L150-L159), [job-status.ts:79-94](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L79-L94) |
| Browser only if needed | The resolution browser is opened only when `unresolved.length > 0` | A headed browser holds the machine while it runs | [add-external-jobs.ts:162-168](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L162-L168) |
| Parsing reads even unresolved jobs | The parsing lookup does not ask whether the link was followed | A job whose link was refused is still read and marked unparseable, which lets it be let through | [add-external-jobs.ts:187-189](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L187-L189) |
| Parsing browser starts lazily | The rendered page browser is created on the first page read and closed in `finally` | Many postings, one browser start-up | [add-external-jobs.ts:190-204](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L190-L204) |
| Home location read late | The location setting is read just before classification | A missing location stops the run after the first three stretches have finished | [add-external-jobs.ts:224-235](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L224-L235) |
| No scoring here | The runner never scores. The skill calls `score-backlog` afterward | Scoring needs an agent, see [Scoring](scoring.md) | [SKILL.md:68-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md#L68-L72) |

### The let-through protection

The user picked these jobs by hand, so a job the pipeline cannot read should not be dropped. In a normal job search, a job with no usable place ends up as `unparseable` or never gets classified. A hand-added job often has no listing page to resolve and no location text to check. Rather than leaving it stuck unjudged, `letJobsThrough` lets it through to scoring and records why ([lib/handlers/let-through.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L1-L5)).

It runs at two positions, chosen by the `after` option.

| Position | Condition | Result | Trace reason | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `after: "parsing"` | Job status is `unparseable` | Status back to `backlog`, with resolved, parsed and classified all set true | `no_location` | [let-through.ts:38-47](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L38-L47) |
| `after: "classification"` | Job is still in the backlog (or has no status) and was never marked classified | Marked classified, stays in the backlog | `location_unusable` | [let-through.ts:51-61](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L51-L61) |

The second case means the map could not find a place for the job. Marking it classified keeps it from being picked up again ([let-through.ts:51-54](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L51-L54)).

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> backlog: saved from submission
    backlog --> unparseable: parser finds no real place
    unparseable --> backlog: let through after parsing, reason no_location
    backlog --> backlog: let through after classification, reason location_unusable
    backlog --> scoring: all markers set
    scoring --> [*]
```

<!-- Sources: lib/handlers/let-through.ts:38-61, lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts:217-246 -->

The handler follows the usual handler rules. It copies each job, raises no warnings, and writes a trace row of event `job_let_through` for each job it lets through. It writes a row only when it has a trace service, a run id and a step name. A job with no id or collector is let through silently ([let-through.ts:75-99](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L75-L99)). Because the closed set of reasons is a TypeScript type, a word the step has no right to write fails to compile ([let-through.ts:23-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/handlers/let-through.ts#L23-L25)).

A let-through job is not scored with certainty. The report flags it as "could not be judged for certain" and prints each reason ([lib/utils/added-jobs-report.ts:35-37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/added-jobs-report.ts#L35-L37)).

### Reporting where each link landed

After the steps finish or stop, the runner builds one outcome per submission. Each starts as "not saved" or "not a web address". A lookup then finds the job by the same link key that duplicate checking uses, so two links to one posting land on one job ([add-external-jobs.ts:254-281](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L254-L281)). The outcome takes the job's status, and the last reason from this run's trace rows. For a job at `backlog` the reason is null, because nothing needs explaining. The let-through reasons come from `resolution_failed` and `job_let_through` rows ([add-external-jobs.ts:297-317](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L297-L317)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant U as User
    participant K as add-external-jobs skill
    participant C as add command
    participant R as runAddExternalJobs
    participant S as score-backlog skill
    U->>K: pastes links
    K->>K: open each link, read title, employer, description
    K->>U: ask for details of unreadable links
    K->>C: submission file
    C->>R: submissions, services, runId
    R-->>C: outcomes, warnings, failure
    C-->>K: Run line, one line per link, warnings
    alt run stopped
        K->>U: report failure and which links to add again
    else run finished
        K->>S: hand over run id
        S-->>K: warnings, or nothing to score
        K->>U: added, scored, not added, warnings
    end
```

<!-- Sources: .claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md:23-94, scripts/add-external-jobs.ts:56-84 -->

The command prints `Run: {run-id}` first so the scoring skill can file its trace rows under the same run ([scripts/add-external-jobs.ts:56-59](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/add-external-jobs.ts#L56-L59)). The skill does not score after a stopped run, and it leaves out the run summary ([SKILL.md:19-20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md#L19-L20)).

A schema check runs first, before the browser, for a specific reason. The trace service swallows writes it cannot make, so on a mismatched database the run would work for minutes and end with no record of having done so ([scripts/add-external-jobs.ts:40-48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/add-external-jobs.ts#L40-L48)). Failures are tracked the same way as in other orchestrators, with `createFailureTracker` ([add-external-jobs.ts:86-93](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L86-L93)). `FinishedHandler` is imported from the job search runner so a stopped run can list the steps that finished ([add-external-jobs.ts:32](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs.ts#L32), [added-jobs-report.ts:47-53](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/added-jobs-report.ts#L47-L53)).

## Resumes

### Why `fetch-rendered-page` exists

Many job postings build their text in the browser with scripts. A plain HTTP fetch hands back an empty shell. The resume skill needs the finished page, so it calls `npm run fetch-rendered-page` ([scripts/fetch-rendered-page.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/fetch-rendered-page.ts#L1-L4)). The script is a thin wrapper. Its core function takes the fetcher and the output functions as arguments, so tests can drive it without a browser. It returns exit code 0 and prints the HTML, or returns 1 with a "Failed to fetch rendered page" message ([fetch-rendered-page.ts:13-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/fetch-rendered-page.ts#L13-L34)). The `main` call is guarded so that importing the module runs nothing ([fetch-rendered-page.ts:46-49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/fetch-rendered-page.ts#L46-L49)).

The tool is separate from `fetch-page.ts`, which reads raw script-free text with no browser ([rendered-page-fetcher.ts:1-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L1-L8)).

| Setting | Value | Reason | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Load wait | `load` event, 30 seconds | Job pages that keep polling never go network-idle, so waiting for quiet would never finish | [rendered-page-fetcher.ts:79-88](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L79-L88), [rendered-page-fetcher.ts:34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L34) |
| Job data wait | Up to 5 seconds for a `script[type="application/ld+json"]` element to attach | Search-engine job data appeared within 1.4 seconds on the pages measured | [rendered-page-fetcher.ts:36-42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L36-L42) |
| If job data never shows | The page is returned as it stands | Only a page that never finishes loading is a failure | [rendered-page-fetcher.ts:99-109](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L99-L109) |
| Browser mode | Headless | Refusals seen so far came from aggregator redirect links, which this tool rarely fetches | [rendered-page-fetcher.ts:72-77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L72-L77) |
| Launcher | Passed in as an argument | A caller can hand in a fake browser | [rendered-page-fetcher.ts:67-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L67-L70) |

The tool offers two builders, as the tools rule allows. One opens and closes a browser per page. The other keeps one browser open for many pages and is what the add run's parsing step uses ([rendered-page-fetcher.ts:9-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L9-L13), [.claude/rules/tools.md](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/tools.md)).

### The `generate-resume` skill

The skill builds a tailored PDF resume for one saved job. It is **pick-only**. It never writes, rewords or invents resume text. It only chooses which existing items are shown ([SKILL.md:3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L3), [SKILL.md:26](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L26)). The resume content and the PDF renderer live in a separate portfolio project outside this repository. This page describes the procedure only, not any resume content.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    P1["Phase 1<br>find-jobs by link or employer"] --> P2["Phase 2<br>fetch-rendered-page"]
    P2 -->|tool failure| T1["Report error<br>retry or paste page"]
    P2 -->|reads as dead| T2["Ask user to confirm<br>stop if dead"]
    P2 -->|loads| P3["Phase 3<br>read resume inventory"]
    P3 --> P4["Phase 4<br>match items to posting"]
    P4 --> P5["Phase 5<br>show all picks, propose filename<br>user approves"]
    P5 --> P6["Phase 6<br>write selections file<br>render PDF into resumes folder"]
    style P1 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style P2 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style P3 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style P4 fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style P5 fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style P6 fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
    style T1 fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
    style T2 fill:#4a2e2e,stroke:#d45b5b,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: .claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md:32-199 -->

| Phase | What the agent does | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Find the job | Splits the request into link, employer and role words. Runs `find-jobs` with the link and employer but never the role. If the employer has several jobs, it picks the one the role words describe, or asks | [SKILL.md:32-64](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L32-L64) |
| 2. Fetch the posting | Fetches `resolved_url` if present, else `original_url`. A fetch failure is a fact about the tool, never about the job. A dead-looking page is confirmed with the user, and the job status is left untouched | [SKILL.md:66-98](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L66-L98) |
| 3. Read the inventory | Runs the portfolio project's inventory command and reads titles, summary parts, skills, tools and experience bullets, each with an `id` | [SKILL.md:100-124](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L100-L124) |
| 4. Match | Chooses items that answer the posting. Strengths are ranked, because the summary names them in order. No word may appear in every chosen strength. Work lines and skills must fit their limits | [SKILL.md:126-146](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L126-L146) |
| 5. Approval | Shows every item, chosen and rejected, with a reason for each chosen one. Proposes a filename. Nothing is generated until the user approves both | [SKILL.md:148-157](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L148-L157) |
| 6. Generate | Writes a selections file, runs the renderer, reads its errors, corrects and retries, then saves the PDF into the project's `resumes` folder | [SKILL.md:159-198](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L159-L198) |

Design choices worth knowing:

- The skill is pick-only because a resume is a statement about a real person. Selection can be checked. Generated text cannot ([SKILL.md:26](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L26)).
- The summary is built from fixed words with slots for an opener, three strengths and an achievement. The script prints each chosen item's summary text exactly, so the "no shared word" check swaps a strength instead of rewording it ([SKILL.md:110-113](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L110-L113), [SKILL.md:129-130](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L129-L130)).
- Allowed tools are listed in the skill's front matter, which limits the commands the agent can run to `find-jobs`, `fetch-rendered-page`, the renderer and a few file operations ([SKILL.md:11-19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L11-L19)).
- Generated PDFs go to `resumes/`, which is an untracked folder in this repository.

The skill relies on `find-jobs`, which is described in [Status Changes and the Work Log](status-change-and-work-log.md).

<doc title="The Read-Only Dashboard" path="./deep-dive/dashboard/dashboard.md">
# The Read-Only Dashboard

## Overview

The pipeline decides things about jobs. The dashboard shows what it decided. It is a small web page with four tabs: Backlog, Active Jobs, Disqualified and Work Log. It changes nothing. Every write to the database happens in a command, never on this page.

Because the page only reads, the command that starts it owns almost nothing. It gathers four lists and hands the web server a way to read them ([scripts/serve.ts:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L1-L3)). Three design choices shape everything else:

- **One page, one request.** All four lists are built at once. The page is small and read-only, so one address that shows where every job stands beats a round trip per tab ([lib/views/page.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/page.ts#L1-L4)).
- **Refuse to start on a bad database.** A page that starts and shows an empty table looks exactly like an empty backlog. So the server checks the schema first and will not listen if it does not match ([lib/tools/web-server.ts:114-120](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L114-L120)).
- **Views are the only place HTML is built.** A view takes values and returns HTML. It reaches no database ([.claude/rules/views.md:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/views.md#L7)).

### At a glance

| Component | Responsibility | Key file | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readPageContents` | Reads the three job lists and the work log from services | `scripts/serve.ts` | [serve.ts:25-51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L25-L51) |
| `createWebServer` | Answers requests, checks the schema, listens on a port | `lib/tools/web-server.ts` | [web-server.ts:63-146](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L63-L146) |
| `pageView` | Builds the whole document: tabs, four panels, script tag | `lib/views/page.ts` | [page.ts:17-80](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/page.ts#L17-L80) |
| `jobTableView` | One table used for all three job lists | `lib/views/job-table.ts` | [job-table.ts:236-267](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L236-L267) |
| `workLogView` | A sidebar of benefit weeks and the entries filed in each | `lib/views/work-log.ts` | [work-log.ts:71-127](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/work-log.ts#L71-L127) |
| `scoreTotal` | Works out a job's total on every page build | `lib/utils/score-total.ts` | [score-total.ts:83-97](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L83-L97) |
| Week helpers | Group entries by Sunday-to-Saturday week | `lib/utils/work-log-weeks.ts` | [work-log-weeks.ts:10-61](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-weeks.ts#L10-L61) |
| Browser script | Tab switching, week switching, the hide-unjudged switch | `public/scripts/dashboard.js` | [dashboard.js:5-90](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/public/scripts/dashboard.js#L5-L90) |

## Starting the server

`npm run serve` runs `scripts/serve.ts` ([package.json:6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L6)). The schema check lives inside the server instead of the command, unlike every other command. A dashboard has to refuse to listen, not just exit ([serve.ts:5-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L5-L7)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant U as User
    participant M as serve.ts main
    participant W as WebServer
    participant D as schemaHasDrifted
    participant B as Browser
    U->>M: npm run serve
    M->>W: createWebServer readContents, probes, publicDir
    M->>W: start port
    W->>D: probes
    alt database does not match the code
        D-->>W: drifted, reason printed
        W-->>M: false
        M->>M: exit code 1, disconnect
    else database matches
        W->>W: listen on port
        W-->>M: true
        B->>W: GET /
        W->>M: readContents
        M-->>W: PageContents
        W-->>B: HTML from pageView
        B->>W: GET /styles/styles.css, /scripts/dashboard.js
        W-->>B: static files
    end
```

<!-- Sources: scripts/serve.ts:60-80, lib/tools/web-server.ts:85-136 -->

| Detail | What the code does | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Port | `PORT` environment variable if it is a positive whole number, else 3001 | An unset, empty or unreadable value must not become port 0, which would be a port nobody was told about | [serve.ts:19-20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L19-L20), [serve.ts:53-58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L53-L58) |
| Database left open | `main` never disconnects on success | This command never finishes a task. It answers requests until stopped by hand | [serve.ts:77-79](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L77-L79) |
| Import guard | `main` runs only when the file is the entry point | Importing the module for a test must not bind a real port | [serve.ts:82-88](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L82-L88) |
| Same drift check as commands | `start` calls `schemaHasDrifted` | One database fault is explained one way, whichever command reached it | [web-server.ts:118-120](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L118-L120) |

### Why it is a tool

`createWebServer` lives in `lib/tools/`, not `lib/services/`. It wraps the port it listens on and the request library behind it, both outside the app ([web-server.ts:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L1-L3)). It splits answering a request (`respondTo`) from listening (`start`). Every real request goes through `respondTo`, so a made-up request in a test proves the same behavior a browser gets, with no port opened ([web-server.ts:5-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L5-L6), [web-server.ts:123-124](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L123-L124)). See [Testing](../quality/testing.md).

### What the server will answer

| Request path | Answer | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contains `..` | 404, before anything is opened | [web-server.ts:86-88](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L86-L88) |
| `/` | 200 with the page. If the read throws, 500 with a plain page that names the database problem | [web-server.ts:90-105](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L90-L105) |
| `/styles/...` or `/scripts/...` | The file from `public/`, only if it ends in `.css` or `.js` | [web-server.ts:43-48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L43-L48), [web-server.ts:107-109](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L107-L109) |
| Anything else | 404 | [web-server.ts:111](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L111) |

The 500 page exists because a blank tab says nothing about what went wrong ([web-server.ts:50-61](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L50-L61)). A missing static file is ordinary and prints nothing. Any other read fault, such as a refused permission, is logged, so the reader does not hunt for a typo that is not there ([web-server.ts:74-81](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L74-L81)).

## The four lists

`readPageContents` reads the lists with one query per status group, all at once ([serve.ts:29-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L29-L34)).

| Tab | Statuses | Source of the list | Sorted by | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Backlog | `backlog` | `findByStatuses(["backlog"])` | Highest score total first | [serve.ts:30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L30), [job-table.ts:220-226](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L220-L226) |
| Active Jobs | `app. sent`, `screening`, `interview`, `test`, `offer` | `ACTIVE_STATUSES` | Last changed first | [job-status.ts:8-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L8-L14), [job-table.ts:227](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L227) |
| Disqualified | `expired`, `too far`, `won't apply`, `unresolvable`, `unparseable`, `rejected` | `RULED_OUT_STATUSES` | Last changed first | [job-status.ts:63-75](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L63-L75) |
| Work Log | Every work log entry | `workLog.findAll()` | Grouped by week | [serve.ts:33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L33) |

The status lists come from the one file that declares them. The page and the pipeline cannot disagree about what a list covers ([serve.ts:22-24](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L22-L24)). The service reads each job together with its employer, because four of the five ratings behind a job's total sit on the employer ([job-service.ts:535-541](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.ts#L535-L541)). The work log entry stores the employer name when filed, but not contact details, which a search finds later. So the page reads the employer through the job the entry names, once for all entries. A job that has been deleted shows the details as not found rather than as an error ([serve.ts:36-48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L36-L48)). See [Services](../data/services.md).

The tab bar shows counts for the three job lists. The work log has no count on purpose. It is filed a week at a time, so a total across every week says nothing the user can act on ([page.ts:20-27](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/page.ts#L20-L27)).

## The job table

One table builds all three job lists. A single list of column definitions builds both the headings and every row, so a column cannot be added to one and forgotten in the other ([job-table.ts:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L1-L3)). The `Column` interface holds the heading and the cell builder together for the same reason ([job-table.ts:22-27](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L22-L27)).

| Column | Shows | Notes | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Score (backlog) or Status (other lists) | The total, or the status badge | The total leads the backlog because the question there is whether to apply. Once a job is applied for or ruled out, the status leads | [job-table.ts:109-132](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L109-L132) |
| Role | Employer and linked title | The link is the followed source posting, with the found address as a fallback | [job-table.ts:134-142](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L134-L142) |
| Type | An icon for remote, hybrid or in-office | Uses the matched mode, else the collected list | [job-table.ts:62-68](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L62-L68), [job-table.ts:144-152](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L144-L152) |
| Location | Matched place, else normalized, else raw | Ruled-out jobs often never reached classification, so they fall back to what was collected | [job-table.ts:47-57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L47-L57) |
| Posted | Relative date, plus an `RP` pill for a repost | Classification only marks a repost when both dates exist | [job-table.ts:159-172](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L159-L172) |
| Salary | Range and period, or `?` | A period the pipeline cannot read prints `?` instead of a guessed figure | [job-table.ts:70-85](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L70-L85) |
| Five ratings | Job alignment, employee, customer, work/life, political | A missing rating prints `?` | [job-table.ts:87-97](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L87-L97), [job-table.ts:205-209](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L205-L209) |
| Avg | Mean of the ratings given | Shown on narrow screens in place of the five. Its tooltip carries the five numbers | [job-table.ts:179-195](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L179-L195) |

Every value that came from outside is passed through `escapeHtml` before it goes into a tag ([job-table.ts:5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L5), [job-table.ts:131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L131)). Each list has its own empty message, and none reads like a failure ([job-table.ts:14-20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L14-L20)).

### Unjudged jobs

A job the pipeline never finished judging must not look like one that passed every check. In the backlog, an unjudged job shows a warning icon where its total would be. The tooltip names each unfinished step: link not followed, posting not read, location not checked. If all three finished, it reads "Not scored" ([job-table.ts:99-107](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L99-L107), [job-table.ts:116-120](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L116-L120)). The marker comes from `is_judged`, set during scoring. See [Scoring](../agent-workflows/scoring.md#what-judged-means).

The page tags unjudged backlog rows with `data-unjudged`. The browser script only hides and shows them, so it works nothing out on its own ([job-table.ts:230-234](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L230-L234)). The toggle counts hidden jobs too, so the user sees how much of the backlog is unchecked either way ([page.ts:37-44](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/page.ts#L37-L44)).

## The score total

The total is worked out as the page is built, not read from a stored column. An employer rescored after its jobs were saved moves all of its jobs at once, which a stored number could not do ([score-total.ts:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L1-L3)).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["Five ratings<br>each 1 to 5, missing counts as 3"] --> S["Weighted sum<br>scaled by weights"]
    S --> M["Multiply"]
    A["Age part<br>0.5 to 1.2"] --> M
    P["Pay part<br>steps from a target salary"] --> M
    M --> T["Round to whole number"]
    style R fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style S fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style A fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style P fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    style M fill:#5a4a2e,stroke:#d4a84b,color:#e6edf3
    style T fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#4aba8a,color:#e6edf3
```

<!-- Sources: lib/utils/score-total.ts:8-97 -->

`total = round(weightedSum x agePart x payPart)`, from [score-total.ts:96](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L96).

| Category | Weight at 5 of 5 | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job alignment | 40 | [score-total.ts:16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L16) |
| Employee satisfaction | 25 | [score-total.ts:12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L12) |
| Work/life balance | 25 | [score-total.ts:14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L14) |
| Political alignment | 25 | [score-total.ts:15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L15) |
| Customer satisfaction | 10 | [score-total.ts:13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L13) |

The weights add up to 125, the sum before the age and pay parts multiply it ([score-total.ts:8-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L8-L10)). Each rating is divided by 5 and multiplied by its weight ([score-total.ts:86-94](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L86-L94)).

**Missing ratings count as 3.** A freshly collected job has no scores, because scoring runs after the pipeline. Counting a missing score as zero would bury every new job under the ones an agent has already reached. Three is neither for nor against ([score-total.ts:21-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L21-L25)).

**Age part.** It is read from the first posting date, never the updated date, because an update says the posting changed, not that the role went live then ([score-total.ts:35-48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L35-L48)).

| Age of posting | Multiplier | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No date | 1 | [score-total.ts:43](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L43) |
| Under 1 day | 1.2 | [score-total.ts:45](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L45) |
| 1 to 3 days | 1 | [score-total.ts:46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L46) |
| Over 3 days | 1 minus 0.05 per extra day, never below 0.5 | [score-total.ts:47](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L47) |

An old posting that is still open is still a real opening, so it never falls past half ([score-total.ts:35-38](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L35-L38)).

**Pay part.** Figures are turned into a yearly amount with a period table. A period outside the known five returns 1, because the figures are probably not yearly and reading them as a yearly salary would wrongly halve the total ([score-total.ts:59-63](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L59-L63)). A range that contains the target salary scores 1. A range below it loses 0.1 for each 25,000 step below the top of the range. A range above it gains 0.1 for each step above the bottom of the range ([score-total.ts:27-29](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L27-L29), [score-total.ts:50-52](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L50-L52), [score-total.ts:68-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L68-L72)). A single figure is read as a plain number, because it carries no evidence of which end of a band it was ([score-total.ts:74-80](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L74-L80)).

Score colors come from `scoreBand`: 90 and above is good, 70 and above is ok, below that is bad. Single ratings use the same names at 4 and above, 3 and above, and below 3. A missing value gets its own band so it never reads as a bad score ([lib/utils/score-display.ts:8-28](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-display.ts#L8-L28)). The tooltip on a total shows only the job's own reasoning. The employer's four categories ran to about 2,848 characters, more than a browser tooltip can show ([lib/utils/score-reasoning.ts:1-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-reasoning.ts#L1-L9)).

## The work log tab

This tab is what the user copies from when filling in the Texas Workforce Commission form on that site ([work-log.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/work-log.ts#L1-L4)). The filing side is covered in [Status Changes and the Work Log](../agent-workflows/status-change-and-work-log.md).

| Behavior | What the code does | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Weeks run Sunday to Saturday | `weekStart` finds the Sunday at midnight, in local time | A benefit week is a run of local days, not a fixed number of hours | [work-log-weeks.ts:1-15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-weeks.ts#L1-L15) |
| Every week is listed | `weekList` lists each week from the first filing to today, newest first | A week with no filings still owes activities, so it is the one most worth seeing | [work-log-weeks.ts:17-32](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-weeks.ts#L17-L32), [work-log.ts:78-85](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/work-log.ts#L78-L85) |
| Week from the written date | `groupByWeek` keys on the entry's own `created_at` | That is the week the form is filed for | [work-log-weeks.ts:34-48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-weeks.ts#L34-L48) |
| Week label | Span of days, with the year on the closing day | A week that crosses new year still reads correctly | [work-log-weeks.ts:50-61](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-weeks.ts#L50-L61) |
| Fields from the entry | Date, employer name and job title read off the entry, never the job | A filing records what was true when it was made, so a later rename must not change it | [work-log.ts:13-22](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/work-log.ts#L13-L22) |
| Missing contact details | Shows "Company info not found" | The job may have been deleted or never linked to an employer. The user has to find the details, not assume a blank | [work-log.ts:24-31](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/work-log.ts#L24-L31) |
| Result field | Always `Application filed` | The only wording the form accepts in this field | [work-log.ts:9-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/work-log.ts#L9-L11) |
| Empty week | "No activities this week." | Says so, rather than leaving a blank | [work-log.ts:102-105](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/work-log.ts#L102-L105) |

## The browser script

`public/scripts/dashboard.js` is plain JavaScript with no dependencies. It does three things.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> BacklogTab
    BacklogTab --> OtherTab: click a tab button
    OtherTab --> BacklogTab: click Backlog
    state BacklogTab {
        [*] --> ShowAll
        ShowAll --> HideUnjudged: switch on
        HideUnjudged --> ShowAll: switch off
        HideUnjudged --> NothingLeft: every row hidden
        NothingLeft --> HideUnjudged: switch off
    }
```

<!-- Sources: public/scripts/dashboard.js:5-89 -->

| Behavior | How | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tab switching | Click toggles `is-hidden` on panels. Elements marked `data-shows-on`, such as the hide switch, appear only on their tab | [dashboard.js:6-29](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/public/scripts/dashboard.js#L6-L29) |
| Week switching | Same pattern for the work log sidebar and week sections | [dashboard.js:31-48](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/public/scripts/dashboard.js#L31-L48) |
| Hide unjudged | Toggles `is-hidden` on tagged rows. If no row is left, swaps the table for a message "No Judged Backlog Jobs" | [dashboard.js:50-71](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/public/scripts/dashboard.js#L50-L71), [job-table.ts:248-253](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L248-L253) |
| Remember the switch | Stored in `localStorage`, inside `try` blocks. Nothing stored means off. Blocked storage still lets the switch work for the visit | [dashboard.js:73-89](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/public/scripts/dashboard.js#L73-L89) |

The server always draws the switch off. The script restores the saved choice ([page.ts:37-39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/page.ts#L37-L39)). The page links an icon stylesheet from `unpkg.com` (Phosphor icons) and its own `/styles/styles.css`, so the icons need network access in the browser ([page.ts:52-54](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/page.ts#L52-L54)). The stylesheet has these responsive rules ([public/styles/styles.css:488-530](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/public/styles/styles.css#L488-L530)).

| Screen width | What changes | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Under 1440 pixels | The Location column is hidden | [styles.css:501-505](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/public/styles/styles.css#L501-L505) |
| 1024 pixels and under | The five individual rating columns are hidden and the Avg column is shown | [styles.css:508-517](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/public/styles/styles.css#L508-L517) |
| 767 pixels and under | The Salary column is hidden and the work log sidebar stacks above the entries | [styles.css:519-530](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/public/styles/styles.css#L519-L530) |

## Why views are the only place HTML is built

| Rule | Where it is stated | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A view takes values and returns HTML and reaches no database | [views.md:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/views.md#L7) | A page can be proved from made-up values |
| Files are `lib/views/{subject}.ts` with a `{subject}View` function | [views.md:9-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/views.md#L9-L10) | A reader knows where a screen is built |
| A util answers one small question. A view owns a whole screen, or a part of one | [views.md:11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/views.md#L11) | `scoreTotal` is a util. `jobTableView` is a view |

The web server tool imports `pageView` directly, but it hands the data in through `readContents` and never queries a table itself ([web-server.ts:14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L14), [web-server.ts:95](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L95)). The line between data and presentation therefore runs through `readPageContents` in the command and `PageContents` in `page.ts`.

# Testing

## Overview

This app talks to job sites, a browser, a map service, a paid search service and a database. A test suite that touched any of them would be slow, would cost money, and would break when a website changed. So the suite is built on one idea: **every outside thing has a stand-in**, and the real services run against a throwaway database.

There are 235 test files tracked in git, of which 33 are flow tests, and 13 shared stand-ins (counted with `git ls-files`). The kinds of file and their names are fixed by the naming rule ([.claude/rules/naming.md:25-33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L25-L33)).

### At a glance

| Kind of file | Name | What it proves | Example | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unit test | `{name}.test.ts`, beside the file it tests | One file does what it says | `lib/handlers/association.test.ts` | [naming.md:27](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L27) |
| Trace-row test | `{name}-events.test.ts` | A handler records what happened to each job | `lib/handlers/backlog-cleanup-events.test.ts` | [naming.md:28](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L28) |
| Flow test | `{scenario}.flow.test.ts`, beside the runner it drives | A whole job search or command works from start to finish | `lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts` | [naming.md:29](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L29) |
| Stand-in | `{name}.fake.ts` | Replaces a service or tool used by more than one test file | `lib/services/job-service.fake.ts` | [naming.md:31-33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L31-L33) |
| Stand-in test | `{name}.fake.test.ts` | The stand-in itself behaves like the real thing | `lib/tools/geocoder.fake.test.ts` | [naming.md:30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L30) |
