`npm run lint` runs ESLint and then the type check, `tsc --noEmit` ([package.json:19-20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L19-L20)).

## Stand-ins

A stand-in (the code also calls it a fake) implements the same interface as the real thing and answers from a table the test fills in. The rule is: a stand-in used by more than one test file lives in `{name}.fake.ts`. One used by only a single test file may stay inside that file ([naming.md:31-33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L31-L33)). The builder is named `fake{Subject}...`, for example `fakeJobService` ([services.md:10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/services.md#L10), [tools.md:13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/tools.md#L13)).

| Stand-in | Replaces | What it does | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fakeJobService` | The job service and its database | Remembers what happened between calls. It mirrors the real create, update and delete rules against an array, so a job created by one call is found by the next | [job-service.fake.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.fake.ts#L1-L5), [job-service.fake.ts:65-72](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/job-service.fake.ts#L65-L72) |
| `fakeResolutionBrowser` | The browser that follows job links | Answers `goto` from a table of pages, follows redirect chains up to 10 hops, can simulate a page that hangs | [resolution-browser.fake.ts:15-16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/resolution-browser.fake.ts#L15-L16), [resolution-browser.fake.ts:29-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/resolution-browser.fake.ts#L29-L70) |
| `fakeCompanySearch` | The paid employer search | Answers from a query-to-result table and records every query asked, so a test can prove the service was not asked twice | [company-search.fake.ts:1-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.fake.ts#L1-L6) |
| `fakePageFetcher` | Every job website | One local web server holding a page for each host and path. It swaps in for global `fetch`, records every visit, and can launch a real headless browser pointed at the local server | [page-fetcher.fake.ts:1-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/page-fetcher.fake.ts#L1-L9), [page-fetcher.fake.ts:33-51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/page-fetcher.fake.ts#L33-L51) |
| `fakeWebServer` | The dashboard server | Answers `/` with a fixed page and `start` with true, with no port or database | [web-server.fake.ts:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.fake.ts#L1-L3), [web-server.fake.ts:14-26](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.fake.ts#L14-L26) |
| `fakeRenderedPageFetcher` | The rendered-page fetcher | Returns HTML from a table of pages | [rendered-page-fetcher.fake.ts:6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.fake.ts#L6) |
| `fakeSettingsService` | The settings service | Takes overrides for the values a test cares about | [settings-service.fake.ts:13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/services/settings-service.fake.ts#L13) |

The full list of tracked stand-ins is in `lib/services/` (ats-slug, company, job, place, settings, work-log) and `lib/tools/` (company-search, geocoder, page-fetcher, rendered-page-fetcher, resolution-browser, resolution-page, web-server). There is no stand-in for the trace service, because flow tests use the real one against the scratch database.

Stand-ins have tests of their own (`*.fake.test.ts`), so a stand-in cannot quietly drift away from the interface it copies. The company search fake carries a sentinel, `NEVER_ANSWERS`, because the real tool has a 60 second limit and testing that needs a search that never answers ([company-search.fake.ts:11-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.fake.ts#L11-L14)). The real tool is built to take its outside call as an argument for exactly this reason ([lib/tools/company-search.ts:19-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L19-L25)). See [Status Changes and the Work Log](../agent-workflows/status-change-and-work-log.md).

The fake browser parses pages with `linkedom`, the library that turns an HTML string into a queryable document in plain Node. That is why page-reading code can run in a test with no browser ([resolution-browser.fake.ts:4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/resolution-browser.fake.ts#L4), [resolution-browser.fake.ts:94-109](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/resolution-browser.fake.ts#L94-L109)).

### Fixtures: replaying a saved page

Browser-based collectors save the HTML of their results container after a real run. An offline test then replays that saved file. If a site quietly changes its markup, the replay fails ([lib/collectors/fixture.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/fixture.ts#L1-L5)). Two fixtures are tracked: `dribbble.html` and `uiuxjobsboard.html`. They are read by the `-cards.test.ts` files for each collector ([lib/collectors/dribbble-cards.test.ts:1-5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/dribbble-cards.test.ts#L1-L5)).

The baseline is protected from bad writes:

| Guard | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A run whose own self-check failed never overwrites the fixture | It would write the run's own breakage into the baseline the test exists to compare against | [fixture.ts:54-56](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/fixture.ts#L54-L56) |
| Empty HTML is refused | A blank container is what a broken selector produces | [fixture.ts:58-62](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/fixture.ts#L58-L62) |
| `writeFixture` never throws | Every refusal comes back as a warning, so a collection that worked is never reported as a collector that failed | [fixture.ts:47-49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/fixture.ts#L47-L49) |
| The best container wins, not the last | Cleanliness beats size. Equal card counts keep the incumbent. Keeping the last once left a fixture with one card, which proves little | [fixture.ts:89-111](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/fixture.ts#L89-L111) |
| The directory is read per call from `COLLECTOR_FIXTURE_DIR` | A test can point it at a scratch folder for one test | [fixture.ts:27-31](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/fixture.ts#L27-L31) |

See [Collection](../pipeline/collection.md) for the collectors themselves.

## Flow tests

A unit test proves one file. A flow test proves that the files work together. It runs a whole job search or command, with real services, against a real but throwaway database. The only thing standing in is the outside world.

The example the page uses is `hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts`. Its header states the scenario in plain words: five hiring systems each have a full board and a quiet board, one system has more jobs than a single reply returns, and a Dover board must never be sent a request ([hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:1-28](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L1-L28)). The `Covers:` line lists what it proves ([hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:26-28](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L26-L28)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant T as Flow test beforeAll
    participant S as npx tsx scripts
    participant D as Scratch SQLite file
    participant F as Stand-in fetch
    participant R as runJobSearch
    T->>T: mkdtemp in the OS temp folder
    T->>S: db-create.ts with file URL
    S->>D: build schema
    T->>S: db-seed.ts
    S->>D: fill settings
    T->>D: connect, add boards and search terms
    T->>F: replace globalThis.fetch
    T->>R: every collector, fake browser, fake places, fake geocoder
    R->>F: board list requests
    F-->>R: made-up replies
    R->>D: save jobs and trace rows
    T->>D: read back titles and boards
    T->>T: afterAll restores fetch, disconnects, deletes folder
```

<!-- Sources: lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:293-311, 336-392 -->

| Technique | How the test does it | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scratch database | Creates a temp folder and a file URL for `pipeline.db` inside it | [hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:337-338](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L337-L338) |
| Real schema and seed | Spawns the real `db-create.ts` and `db-seed.ts` scripts with `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL` pointing at the scratch file | [hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:293-300](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L293-L300) |
| Safe by design | `db:create` refuses to rebuild the database named in `.env`, so these tests cannot damage the real one | [CLAUDE.md, Commands](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) |
| Connection | `connect` sets the environment variable only for the moment the client is built, then restores it | [hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:302-311](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L302-L311) |
| Sites replaced | `globalThis.fetch` is swapped for a stand-in that answers each system's board address in the shape measured live, and restored in `afterAll` | [hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:20-24](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L20-L24), [hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:361](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L361), [hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:388-392](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L388-L392) |
| Browser and maps replaced | A browser that stays put, a fake place service that always answers, and a fake geocoder | [hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:264-291](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L264-L291), [hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:313-325](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L313-L325) |
| Registry used for real | Passes `COLLECTORS` so no collector is left out of the "does any reach Dover" question | [hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:363-370](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L363-L370) |
| Time limit | A 120 second setup ceiling, because two scripts are spawned and a job search runs after them | [hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:55-57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L55-L57) |
| Assertions | Matching titles collected, non-matching not collected, an empty board still on its polling list, the last page read, no request to Dover | [hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts:394-419](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/hiring-systems-paging.flow.test.ts#L394-L419) |

Why a real database instead of `fakeJobService` here? A flow test exists to catch a fault that only appears when real pieces meet. If the services were also fakes, a mistake in how a handler uses a real service could never show up. Unit tests use fakes for speed. Flow tests use real services for truth.

Flow tests are named for the scenario they prove and sit beside the runner they drive. There are 28 in `lib/orchestrators/` and 5 in `scripts/`, which cover commands such as `find-jobs` ([scripts/find-jobs-by-link.flow.test.ts](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/find-jobs-by-link.flow.test.ts)). The add-external-jobs runner alone has eight ([lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs-failed-save.flow.test.ts](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/add-external-jobs-failed-save.flow.test.ts)). See [External Jobs and Resumes](../agent-workflows/external-jobs-and-resumes.md).

## How no test touches a real site or browser

| Outside thing | What a test uses instead | Does anything real run? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job websites over `fetch` | Swapped `globalThis.fetch`, or `fakePageFetcher` | A local web server on this machine only |
| Link-following browser | `fakeResolutionBrowser` or a hand-written browser that stays put | No browser |
| Rendered-page browser | `fakeRenderedPageFetcher`, or an injected launcher | No browser |
| Parsing browser in a page-reading flow test | `fakePageFetcher.launchBrowser()` | A real headless browser, but it is launched to find every host name on this machine, so it only reaches the local server |
| Paid employer search | `fakeCompanySearch`, or an injected actor runner | No |
| Map and geocoding service | `fakeGeocoder`, `fakePlaceService` | No |
| The real database | A scratch SQLite file in the OS temp folder | A real file, deleted afterward |

Sources for the table: [page-fetcher.fake.ts:1-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/page-fetcher.fake.ts#L1-L9), [page-fetcher.fake.ts:33-51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/page-fetcher.fake.ts#L33-L51), [resolution-browser.fake.ts:130-140](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/resolution-browser.fake.ts#L130-L140), [rendered-page-fetcher.ts:67-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L67-L70), [company-search.ts:25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L25).

The reason a launcher or runner is passed in as an argument, rather than called inside the tool, is the testing seam. The rendered page tool says so: a caller can supply its own launcher, the same reason the resolution browser takes one ([rendered-page-fetcher.ts:67-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L67-L70)). The web server tool splits `respondTo` from `start` so a made-up request proves the page with no port opened ([lib/tools/web-server.ts:5-6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L5-L6)). And `serve.ts` guards its `main` so importing it for a test binds no port ([scripts/serve.ts:82-88](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L82-L88)). See [The Read-Only Dashboard](../dashboard/dashboard.md).

| Test | What it guards | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `import-direction.test.ts` | No util imports from `handlers` or `orchestrators`, value or type-only | A plain function sits at the bottom of the app and must depend on nothing above it. A failure tells the reader to move the shared shape into `lib/types/` | [import-direction.test.ts:1-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts#L1-L8), [import-direction.test.ts:15-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts#L15-L34) |
| `prisma.config.test.ts`, AC1 | The Prisma config points at the current schema and migrations, and reads `PIPELINE_DATABASE_URL`, not `DATABASE_URL` | Stops a command pointing at the wrong database | [prisma.config.test.ts:35-60](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma.config.test.ts#L35-L60) |
| `prisma.config.test.ts`, AC2 | The database URL has no fallback. Unset means a clear error | A missing setting must fail loudly | [prisma.config.test.ts:62-89](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma.config.test.ts#L62-L89) |
| `prisma.config.test.ts`, AC3 | `pipeline.db` is git-ignored and untracked | Keeps the real database out of the repository | [prisma.config.test.ts:91-103](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma.config.test.ts#L91-L103) |

The import-direction test applies the rule that a plain function never names a file in `handlers/` or `orchestrators/` ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md)). It is the rule turned into something that fails the build. The `prisma.config` test names its checks "AC1" to "AC3", short for acceptance criteria, which is the wording the project's feature specs use (inferred from the test names). See [Project Rules](project-rules.md).

Config tests that import `prisma.config.ts` get a 10 second ceiling because the first import is slow. It was measured at 318 ms alone, and slower when other workers compete for the processor ([prisma.config.test.ts:10-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma.config.test.ts#L10-L13)). They restore the environment and the module cache after each test, so one test cannot leak into the next ([prisma.config.test.ts:15-25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma.config.test.ts#L15-L25)).

# Project Rules

## Overview

This project keeps its design rules in writing, in two places. The first is `.claude/rules/`, thirteen short files that Claude Code loads when it edits matching files. The second is the "Working Agreements" section of `CLAUDE.md`, which holds four rules that apply everywhere. The rules exist because the code is written largely with an AI agent. An agent that cannot ask questions needs the answer to "where does this go, and what is it called?" written down.

Each rule file names the paths it applies to in a `paths:` line at the top. Claude Code loads the rule only when it touches a file that matches ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L1-L3)). Only one rule has automatic enforcement in a test. The rest depend on the agent and on review.

## At a glance

| Layer | What it is | Applies to | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rule files | 13 files, each answering one question | Paths named in each file | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:1-3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L1-L3) |
| Working agreements | 4 rules about how to build | All work | [CLAUDE.md:107-115](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L107-L115) |
| Linting | ESLint with the TypeScript plugin | Every `.ts` file outside `docs/` and `generated/` | [.eslintrc.json:1-8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.eslintrc.json#L1-L8) |
| Type check | Strict TypeScript, no output files | Every `.ts` file outside `docs/` and `generated/` | [tsconfig.json:6-20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/tsconfig.json#L6-L20) |
| Automatic check | A test that stops utils importing from handlers | `lib/utils/` | [lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts:16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts#L16) |

## Where does new code go?

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q{"What does the new code do?"}
    Q -->|Fits one job site| S["collectors or parsers"]
    Q -->|Runs at one pipeline position on a list| H["handlers"]
    Q -->|Calls handlers in order| O["orchestrators"]
    Q -->|Owns one table or row| V["services"]
    Q -->|Wraps something outside the app| T["tools"]
    Q -->|Follows a job link on a page it was handed| R["resolvers"]
    Q -->|Turns data into HTML| W["views"]
    Q -->|Takes values, returns values| U["utils"]
    Q -->|A shape used by more than one folder| Y["types"]
    classDef default fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```

<!-- Sources: .claude/rules/naming.md:7-25, .claude/rules/part-ownership.md:7-11, .claude/rules/tools.md:7, .claude/rules/resolvers.md:7 -->

The `lib/db/` folder holds the database connection and the schema check, and only that folder builds a connection ([.claude/rules/naming.md:25](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L25)).

## The four working agreements

| Agreement | In plain words | Why it exists | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Build broadly, not for the case in front of you** | A rule that exists only to make one seen example come out right is a defect. Fold it into a general step that already exists | One-off fixes pile up into code nobody can reason about | [CLAUDE.md:109](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L109) |
| **No guardrail for a failure nobody has seen** | A measured occurrence justifies building against a failure. Until then the risk is written down, not coded around | Guards for imagined failures add code that never runs and hides real design | [CLAUDE.md:111](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L111) |
| **An exception is a closed list, never a judgement** | Where a rule allows an exception, it names the exact files or cases | An exception left to judgement gets taken every time | [CLAUDE.md:113](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L113) |
| **Knowledge about a job site is data, never code** | A rule may read a list of websites. It may not contain one. Site-specific judgement lives in collectors and parsers only | New sites should mean a new entry, not a new branch in shared code | [CLAUDE.md:115](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L115) |

You can see all four in the code. The parser registry is keyed by the website each parser owns, and the lookup falls through to a general parser for any unowned link, so no shared code names a site ([lib/parsers/registry.ts:51-79](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/registry.ts#L51-L79)). The one exception rule in `sources.md` is a closed list of one: `general.ts` is the only parser that owns no website ([.claude/rules/sources.md:23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/sources.md#L23)). The recovery command asks the registry whether a parser claims a link and holds no knowledge of sites itself ([scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts:62-70](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/recover-unparseable-jobs.ts#L62-L70)).

## Rule by rule

### part-ownership

This rule decides which part of the pipeline may do what. It starts from one fact: collectors and parsers are the only code written for a particular site, and no part branches on which collector produced a job ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:7-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L7-L11)).

Seven jobs have exactly one implementation: removing duplicates, saving and updating, following a link, tidying names, matching a location, clearing the backlog, and recording what happened. A second copy is "a defect, not a variation" ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:13-17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L13-L17)). No part may assume it runs inside a job search, so the same save code serves a search, a hand status change, and scoring ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:19-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L19-L23)). Each stretch ends at the database and the next one asks the database for its work ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:25-27](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L25-L27)).

| Part | Owns | Never does | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Collector | Gathers raw jobs into `raw_` fields exactly as they arrived | Interpret anything | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L33) |
| Normalizer | Reshapes raw data already present | Go looking for missing data | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L34) |
| Resolver | Follows a link to the employer's own posting | Read anything off the page it lands on | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L35) |
| Parser | The final attempt at filling `raw_` fields | Format what it extracts | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:36](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L36) |
| Company association | Decides the employer; creates one if none | Invent a name from a slug, or a slug from a name | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L37) |
| Dedupe | Reduces the job list using identity tests | Merge when no test has the fields it needs | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:38](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L38) |
| Save | Creates, updates, deletes rows; owns the merge rule | Decide which employer a job belongs to | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:39](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L39) |
| Classification | Judgements such as location match and expiry | Reshape a value or look for a missing one | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:40](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L40) |
| Scoring | Alignment, employer scores, promoting an employer | Reach the database except through the services that own each table | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L41) |
| Backlog cleanup | Expires old backlog jobs, and empties stale employer scores | Delete a job or an employer | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L42) |

The rule gives a test that separates reshaping from going looking: reshaping changes a value that is there, and going looking produces one that is not ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:48-50](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L48-L50)). It also says which step may set which status ([.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:44-46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L44-L46)), shown in [Quick Reference](../../getting-started/quick-reference.md#job-statuses).

### naming

Files are kebab-case, one folder per kind of thing. Tests sit beside the code and are named by what they test ([.claude/rules/naming.md:27-38](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L27-L38)).

| Test file name | Meaning | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{name}.test.ts` | Tests one file | [.claude/rules/naming.md:31](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L31) |
| `{name}-events.test.ts` | A handler's trace-row tests | [.claude/rules/naming.md:32](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L32) |
| `{scenario}.flow.test.ts` | Runs a whole search or command from start to finish | [.claude/rules/naming.md:33](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L33) |
| `{name}.fake.test.ts` | Tests a stand-in | [.claude/rules/naming.md:34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L34) |

Value names follow one pattern ([.claude/rules/naming.md:46-51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L46-L51)): a fixed written-out value is `SCREAMING_SNAKE` (`ACTIVE_STATUSES`), an object carrying functions is `camelCase` (`adzunaCollector`), a type is `PascalCase` (`JobListEntry`), and everything else is `camelCase`. The code follows this: `ACTIVE_STATUSES` and `VALID_STATUSES` are in `lib/utils/job-status.ts` ([lib/utils/job-status.ts:8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L8)). A shape used by more than one folder goes in `lib/types/`; a shape one folder uses stays there ([.claude/rules/naming.md:40-44](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/naming.md#L40-L44)).

### handler-contract

A handler takes a list, acts on every entry, and returns that list under the name of what is in it (`jobs` or `companies`, never both) ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:9-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L9-L11)). The orchestrator makes this concrete: its `HandlerResult` type forbids a result that carries both, so the entry count cannot pick one arbitrarily ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:58-67](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L58-L67)).

The rule separates two kinds of record ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:31-35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L31-L35)):

| Record | Purpose | Who sees it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Trace row** | Analytics. Written as the handler runs. Changes nothing | Nobody is told |
| **Warning** | Validation. Something is wrong the user needs to know | Returned up to the agent, which presents it |

An event can produce both. A salary that could not be read writes a trace row and returns a warning ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L35)). A handler reads no database beyond the trace service ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L17)), and it is handed the step name because one handler runs at more than one position ([.claude/rules/handler-contract.md:37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/handler-contract.md#L37)). The orchestrator shows this: `dedupeJobs` runs at three positions with a different `step` each time ([lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:334-343](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L334-L343), [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:408-417](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L408-L417), [lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts:528-538](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/orchestrators/job-search.ts#L528-L538)).

### orchestrators, services, tools, resolvers, views, types, utils

These seven rules are short. They set a name pattern and one sentence about what the part may touch.

| Rule | Pattern | Boundary it sets | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orchestrators` | `lib/orchestrators/{subject}.ts`, function `run{Subject}` | Calls handlers in order and hands each what it needs as arguments | [.claude/rules/orchestrators.md:7-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/orchestrators.md#L7-L13) |
| `services` | `{subject}-service.ts`, `create{Subject}Service(db)`, `{Subject}Record` | Owns exactly one table or row, reaches the database only through its client | [.claude/rules/services.md:7-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/services.md#L7-L13) |
| `tools` | `{subject}.ts`, builder starts with `create`, stand-in `fake{Subject}()` | Wraps one outside thing, owns no table, takes no job list | [.claude/rules/tools.md:7-13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/tools.md#L7-L13) |
| `resolvers` | `resolve-job-url.ts`, `resolveJobUrl` | Drives a page it was handed and never opens one | [.claude/rules/resolvers.md:7-10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/resolvers.md#L7-L10) |
| `views` | `{subject}.ts`, `{subject}View` | Takes values, returns HTML, reaches no database | [.claude/rules/views.md:7-11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/views.md#L7-L11) |
| `types` | `{subject}.ts` | Declares a shape; holds no logic and calls nothing | [.claude/rules/types.md:7-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/types.md#L7-L9) |
| `utils` | `{subject}.ts`, named for a noun it returns or a yes-or-no question | Takes values, returns values, reaches no database | [.claude/rules/utils.md:7-12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/utils.md#L7-L12) |

The utils boundary is the only one with a test. `lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts` reads every non-test util file and fails if one imports from `handlers` or `orchestrators`, including type-only imports ([lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts:16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts#L16), [lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts:27-35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts#L27-L35)). The test explains why: a folder meant to depend on nothing must not depend on the pipeline ([lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/import-direction.test.ts#L1-L4)). The rule that states this direction is a line in the `utils` rule ([.claude/rules/utils.md:12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/utils.md#L12)).

### sources and source-registry

Collector and parser file names must match their `name` field, and a source joins the pipeline only by being listed in its registry ([.claude/rules/sources.md:11-14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/sources.md#L11-L14), [.claude/rules/sources.md:20-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/sources.md#L20-L23)). The paired rule explains the cost of forgetting the next step: a registry change must run `npm run db:seed` in the same change, because a source missing from the priority list loses every contested field ([.claude/rules/source-registry.md:7-9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/source-registry.md#L7-L9)). The seed does the appending ([scripts/db-seed.ts:204-218](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L204-L218)). See [Parsing](../pipeline/parsing.md) and [Collection](../pipeline/collection.md).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Dev as Developer
    participant R as registry.ts
    participant Rule as source-registry rule
    participant Seed as db:seed
    participant S as Setting row
    Dev->>R: Add collector or parser to the list
    Rule-->>Dev: Run db:seed in the same change
    Dev->>Seed: npm run db:seed
    Seed->>R: Read every registry name
    Seed->>S: Append names missing from source_priority_list
    S-->>Dev: New source ranks last, owner reorders by hand
```

<!-- Sources: .claude/rules/source-registry.md:7-9, scripts/db-seed.ts:88-95, scripts/db-seed.ts:189-219, lib/collectors/registry.ts:19-34 -->

### run-summary

Every step prints, even with no work, because "a missing block reads as a step that never ran" ([.claude/rules/run-summary.md:9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L9)). The heading carries how many jobs entered, and each job leaves by exactly one line, so the lines sum to the heading ([.claude/rules/run-summary.md:15-23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L15-L23)). A reason clause uses the value written to `Trace.reason`, so the summary and a database query use one name ([.claude/rules/run-summary.md:32-34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L32-L34)). A note is something true about the jobs that is not a path out of the step, and never counts toward the heading ([.claude/rules/run-summary.md:43-45](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L43-L45)). Every count is read back from trace rows, never from what a handler returned ([.claude/rules/run-summary.md:88-90](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/run-summary.md#L88-L90)). The command does exactly that ([scripts/job-search.ts:117-130](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/job-search.ts#L117-L130)). A stopped step is marked in its heading ([lib/utils/run-summary.ts:119](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/run-summary.ts#L119)). See [Tracing and Run Summary](../architecture/tracing-and-run-summary.md).

## Lint, types, and hooks

| Tool | Setting | Why it matters | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ESLint | `eslint:recommended` plus the TypeScript recommended set | Baseline correctness checks | [.eslintrc.json:4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.eslintrc.json#L4) |
| Unused variables | A warning, not an error; names starting with `_` are exempt for arguments | Lets a function keep a parameter it does not use | [.eslintrc.json:6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.eslintrc.json#L6) |
| Lint scope | Ignores `node_modules`, `generated`, and `docs` | `docs/` holds research spikes, not app code | [.eslintignore:1-4](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.eslintignore#L1-L4) |
| TypeScript | `strict: true`, `noEmit: true`, module `esnext` | Type errors fail `npm run lint` since it runs the type check second | [tsconfig.json:6-7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/tsconfig.json#L6-L7), [package.json:19-20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L19-L20) |
| Type scope | Includes `**/*.ts`; excludes `node_modules`, `generated`, `docs` | Same boundary as lint | [tsconfig.json:19-20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/tsconfig.json#L19-L20) |
| Vitest | Time zone fixed to UTC; `docs/` excluded | Tests that read dates cannot depend on the machine | [vitest.config.ts:14-18](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/vitest.config.ts#L14-L18) |
| Claude Code hooks | After every edit, write, or shell command: `code-review-graph update --skip-flows`; at session start: `code-review-graph status` | Keeps the code graph that agents query in step with the files | [.claude/settings.json:3-27](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/settings.json#L3-L27) |

The lint rules are not strict about the architecture. ESLint here checks style and correctness only, and the architectural rules live in the written rule files plus the one import test (inferred from reading `.eslintrc.json`, which has no custom rule).

## Optional


<doc title="Executive Guide" path="./onboarding/executive-guide.md">
# Executive Guide

This guide is for someone who has to decide what to do with this tool. That might be its builder, deciding where the next weekend of work goes. It might be a friend who wants to run their own copy. It might be a person judging whether the tool is worth extending.

It is a personal tool. One person built it to run their own job search. There is no team, no on-call rotation, no customers and no service level. The guide keeps the usual executive sections, but each one is answered honestly for a team of one.

The guide uses no code. Where a claim needs proof, it links to the source file on GitHub.

## 1. System Overview

The tool finds job postings, ranks them, tracks applications, and files the weekly unemployment work log for the Texas Workforce Commission. It runs on one laptop. Claude Code skills drive it: the person types a short command, and an AI agent runs the steps and does the judging.

| Question | Answer | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who uses it? | One person: the builder. | [CLAUDE.md:3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L3) |
| What problem does it solve? | Checking many job sites by hand is slow and repetitive, and no single site surfaces the right roles well. | [docs/APP.md:9](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/APP.md#L9) |
| What is the business value? | Time saved, better job choices, and a legal record of search activity that is filed without manual bookkeeping. | [docs/APP.md:13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/APP.md#L13) |
| Where does it run? | On the person's own computer. Nothing is hosted. | [lib/tools/web-server.ts:131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L131) |
| Who pays for it? | The person. The paid parts are small and are listed in the cost section. | [.env.example:13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.env.example#L13) |

The stated goal is that the job search becomes "a short daily task, not a full-time job" ([docs/APP.md:13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/APP.md#L13)). Real job searches already run on the current version of the tool ([CLAUDE.md:20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L20)).

### The one decision this guide supports

The question is not "does it work?" It works. The question is "what is the next hour of effort best spent on?" The honest options are:

| Option | What it means | When it is right |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keep using it as is | Run searches, score, apply. Fix only what breaks. | The search is active and the tool already finds good jobs. |
| Invest further | Add job sources, harden the weak spots, add backups. | Too few good jobs surface, or the single points of failure worry you. |
| Hand it to someone else | Let another person run their own copy. | A friend is job hunting. Expect a half day of setup and some edits to personal files. |
| Retire it | Stop when the search ends. | The person is employed. The code and the history stay on disk. |

The recommendations section at the end picks among these.

## 2. Capability Map

The table shows what the tool can and cannot do today. "Built" means the step is coded, tested, and used on real searches. The statuses come from the code and the changelog, not from the README.

| Capability | Status | Maturity | Depends on | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Collect jobs from 14 sources in one run | Built | High. 14 sources are registered. | Two paid or keyed job APIs, plus public job boards | [lib/collectors/registry.ts:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/registry.ts#L19) |
| Follow a job link back to the employer's own posting | Built | Medium. Some sites refuse automated visits. | A visible browser window | [lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts:23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts#L23) |
| Read a posting for description, place, pay and dates | Built | High for 11 named hiring sites, medium for the general reader | None outside the posting page | [lib/parsers/registry.ts:37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/registry.ts#L37) |
| Remove duplicate jobs across sources | Built | High | None | [docs/CHANGELOG.md:77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md#L77) |
| Decide whether a job is close enough, by real geography | Built | High | A map lookup service | [lib/tools/geocoder.ts:13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L13) |
| Score each job and each employer with an AI agent | Built | Medium. The quality is the agent's judgement. | Claude Code, plus web access for employer research | [.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:1](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L1) |
| Rank jobs by a weighted total | Built | High | Scores from the step above | [lib/utils/score-total.ts:83](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/score-total.ts#L83) |
| Watch good employers directly on later searches | Built | Medium | Employer scores, three supported hiring-site boards | [docs/CHANGELOG.md:73](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md#L73) |
| Track a job through twelve statuses | Built | High | None | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:24](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L24) |
| File Texas work log entries | Built | High, with one paid lookup for contact details | A paid search service | [lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L19) |
| Show everything in a local read-only dashboard | Built | Medium. Read-only by design. | None | [docs/architecture.md:65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L65) |
| Add a job found by hand from its link | Built | Medium | Claude Code reads the page | [.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md:23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-external-jobs/SKILL.md#L23) |
| Write a tailored PDF resume for a job | Built | Medium. Depends on a second project on the same machine. | A separate portfolio project | [.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md:102](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L102) |
| Run automatically on a schedule | Not built | Not applicable. Every run is started by the person. | Not applicable | [docs/architecture.md:110](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L110) |
| Edit data from the dashboard | Not built, by design | Not applicable | Not applicable | [docs/architecture.md:65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L65) |
| Serve more than one user | Not built | Not applicable. Personal files and one database file. | Not applicable | [.gitignore:12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.gitignore#L12) |

## 3. Architecture at a Glance

The tool is a set of small programs on one computer. Each step reads its work from one database file and writes its result back. Because every step ends in a write, a run that stops partway keeps everything finished so far ([docs/CHANGELOG.md:67](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md#L67)).

    end
    subgraph Local["The person's computer"]

    CC --> CMD
    CMD --> DB

### How a job search flows, in business terms

| Stage | What happens | Why it exists | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clean up | Old jobs are marked expired. | An old posting wastes attention. | [docs/architecture.md:23](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L23) |
| Collect | Jobs are pulled from 14 sources. | One list instead of many tabs. | [lib/collectors/registry.ts:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/registry.ts#L19) |
| Merge | Duplicates become one job. | The same job often appears on several sites. | [docs/CHANGELOG.md:77](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md#L77) |
| Follow | The tool finds the employer's own posting. | Aggregator copies are often incomplete. | [docs/architecture.md:15](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L15) |
| Read | The posting's details are extracted. | Pay, place and description drive the ranking. | [lib/parsers/registry.ts:37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/parsers/registry.ts#L37) |
| Judge distance | Each job is tested against the person's location. | Jobs that are too far away are noise. | [docs/architecture.md:29](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L29) |
| Score | An AI agent rates the job and the employer. | Ranking by fit, not by recency alone. | [.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:6](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L6) |
| Show | The dashboard lists the best matches first. | The person decides what to apply to. | [lib/views/job-table.ts:223](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/views/job-table.ts#L223) |

Scoring is the only step that is not a plain command. An agent has to think, and a command cannot pause while an agent thinks, so scoring is split into a "gather" command and a "save" command with the agent in between ([docs/architecture.md:37](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L37)).

## 4. Team Topology

There is one owner. The useful question for a team of one is "what happens if that person is unavailable?", so this section reports the bus factor honestly.

| Component | Owner | Criticality | Bus factor | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Collectors and parsers | Builder | High | 1 | Each is written to fit one site. The rules for adding one are written down in the project rules. |
| The database and its commands | Builder | Critical | 1 | One file holds all history. See the risk section. |
| Scoring rules and profile | Builder | High | 1 | The public rules are tracked. The personal profile is private and kept off the repository. |
| Work log and status changes | Builder | Critical | 1 | A legal record. |
| Dashboard | Builder | Low | 1 | Read-only. A failure here loses no data. |
| Resume generation | Builder | Medium | 1 | Needs a second project that is not in this repository. |

A bus factor of 1 is normal for a personal tool. It matters only if someone else is meant to run the tool. The mitigation is documentation, and the repository has an unusually large amount: a written architecture file, path-scoped rules for each kind of file, and 235 test files ([docs/architecture.md:1](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L1), [CLAUDE.md:51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L51)). The test file count comes from listing tracked files.

One more detail matters to a would-be adopter. Several planning folders are deliberately kept private and off the repository ([.gitignore:24](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.gitignore#L24)). A new owner would not inherit the builder's plans, backlog, or research.

## 5. Technology Investment Thesis

The thesis is: keep the code simple and deterministic, and use an AI agent only where judgement is needed. The names below are from the dependency list ([package.json:24](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L24)).

| Technology | Purpose | Alternatives considered | Risk level | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TypeScript run directly, no build step | Fast edits, one language everywhere | A compiled build | Low | [CLAUDE.md:7](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L7) |
| One SQLite database file | Zero setup, no server to run | A hosted database | Medium. One file, no replication. | [prisma/schema.prisma:8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L8) |
| Prisma with a libsql adapter | Typed access to the database | Raw queries | Low. A known quirk is documented. | [docs/APP.md:49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/APP.md#L49) |
| Playwright browser automation | Follow links that need a real browser | Plain web requests | Medium. A visible window is required. | [lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts#L19) |
| A page-reading library that needs no browser | Read saved pages quickly and test offline | Always use a browser | Low | [CLAUDE.md:10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L10) |
| Claude Code skills | Orchestrate steps and do judging | A scheduled script with a model API | Medium. Depends on one vendor's tool. | [.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:1](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L1) |
| Server-rendered HTML dashboard | A simple local screen | A web app framework | Low | [CLAUDE.md:11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L11) |
| Vitest | Fast tests, including offline replays of site pages | Other test runners | Low | [package.json:21](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/package.json#L21) |
| Apify client | Paid employer contact lookup | A different search API | Medium. Pay per use. | [lib/tools/company-search.ts:42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L42) |

### Why this thesis is sound for one person

| Principle | Effect | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Knowledge about a job site is data, never code | Site rules can change without touching shared logic. | [CLAUDE.md:115](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L115) |
| Only collectors and parsers are written for a particular site | A broken site breaks one file, not the whole tool. | [.claude/rules/part-ownership.md:3](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/rules/part-ownership.md#L3) |
| Every step ends in a database write | A crash loses little. A rerun resumes. | [docs/CHANGELOG.md:67](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md#L67) |
| No guard for a failure nobody has seen | Less code to maintain. Risks are written down instead. | [CLAUDE.md:111](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L111) |
| The source ranking decides which copy of a fact wins | Better data beats more data, and the person can reorder it. | [prisma/schema.prisma:309](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L309) |

The line numbers for the two working agreements in this table were read from the project instructions file. They are tied to the file at the time of writing and may shift.

### The investment so far

The changelog shows where effort went. Each entry is a version and a theme.

| Version | Theme | What it bought | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.1.0 | First dashboard and 7 sources | A usable list | [docs/CHANGELOG.md:125](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md#L125) |
| 0.2.0 | Honest posting dates | Old jobs stop looking new | [docs/CHANGELOG.md:107](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md#L107) |
| 0.3.0 | Tailored PDF resume | Faster applications | [docs/CHANGELOG.md:95](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md#L95) |

The pattern is clear. Early work added breadth. Later work removed jobs that were stuck unread. The latest work improves day-to-day use. That pattern suggests the tool is past its building phase and in its polishing phase.

## 6. Risk Assessment

Each risk is rated by the author of this guide. The ratings are judgement, not measurement. The evidence for each is cited. "Owner" is always the builder.

| # | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation in place | Gap | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Job sites block or change under the scraper | High | Medium | Two lanes with a pause for sites that refuse. A refusal is retried next run. A general reader is the fallback. | Fast lane has no pacing of its own. | Builder |
| R2 | One database file is lost or damaged | Low | Critical | A dated backup is written before each schema change. | No automatic backup of the live file. No copy off the machine. | Builder |
| R3 | A work log entry is wrong or missing | Low | High | Entries are written before the slow lookups. They copy employer and title so later changes cannot alter them. | The contact details come from a search and can be wrong. They are flagged for a check. | Builder |
| R4 | Paid or keyed services change terms or price | Medium | Low | Each service is wrapped in one file. Missing keys give a clear message. | No spending alert. | Builder |
| R5 | The map service stops or throttles | Medium | Medium | A place that cannot be looked up is retried next run. Looked-up places are stored. | Jobs stay unjudged until it returns. | Builder |
| R6 | The AI agent scores poorly or inconsistently | Medium | Medium | Written rubrics. Scores carry a written reason. A guessed score is marked as a guess and expires sooner. | No second opinion, no audit of agreement. | Builder |
| R7 | Dependence on Claude Code | Medium | High | Every step is also a plain command. | The judging steps need an agent. | Builder |
| R8 | Private data leaves the repository by accident | Low | High | A strict ignore list covers databases, resumes, secrets, and personal planning files. | The list is a manual control. | Builder |
| R9 | Automated page visits break a site's terms of use | Medium | Medium | A blocked-site list. A pause for refusing sites. | No written terms review. See below. | Builder |
| R10 | The tool is abandoned when the search ends | High | Low | Everything is local and keeps working. | None needed. | Builder |

### R1. Job sites blocking the scraper

This is the most likely risk, and the code is open about it. Plain requests are turned away by sites that screen for automated traffic, so every request says it is a browser ([lib/tools/page-fetcher.ts:8](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/page-fetcher.ts#L8)). The link-following step uses a visible browser window, because headless requests were refused and headed ones were not in the builder's measurements ([lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts#L19)).

The cost of that choice is that the screen is held while a search runs. The settings explain it: a headed browser holds focus, so the machine is unusable for as long as it runs ([prisma/schema.prisma:322](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L322)).

The tool also learned from a bad day. Before refusals were told apart from dead pages, one bad afternoon at one source took 100 of 334 jobs out of play for good ([docs/architecture.md:17](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L17)). Now a refusal leaves the job alone so the next run tries again.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Job link to follow"] --> B{"Did the site<br>answer normally?"}
    B -- "Yes" --> C["Use the page"]
    B -- "Page is gone" --> D["Mark job unresolvable<br>for the person to repair"]
    B -- "Site refused for now" --> E["Move host to the slow lane<br>pause between jobs"]
    E --> F["Leave job status unchanged<br>retry next run"]
    classDef box fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class A,B,C,D,E,F box
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```

<!-- Sources: docs/architecture.md:17-19, prisma/schema.prisma:316-339, prisma/schema.prisma:531-535 -->

The slow-lane pause is set from a measurement. About 25 page visits per five minutes passed against one aggregator, and about 30 were refused, so the pause is twelve seconds ([prisma/schema.prisma:331](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L331), [scripts/db-seed.ts:54](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/db-seed.ts#L54)). The architecture file is plain about the limit: the two lanes cut the cost of a block but do not prevent one, because the fast lane has no pacing of its own ([docs/architecture.md:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L19)).

A related control is a list of fourteen web addresses that a job is never worth following to. It holds paywalled aggregators and spam destinations ([lib/utils/blacklist.ts:5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/blacklist.ts#L5)). Note that the project's own principle says knowledge about a job site is data, not code ([CLAUDE.md:115](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L115)). A list of sites written in a source file sits uneasily with that principle. This is an observation, and it is a small cleanup item rather than a risk.

### R2. A single SQLite file

All history lives in one file: jobs, employer scores, the trace of every job's path, and the work log. The ignore list keeps database files and their backups out of the repository on purpose, because they hold the real job search ([.gitignore:12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.gitignore#L12)).

What protects it today:

| Control | Effect | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A schema change writes a dated backup first | A bad migration can be undone | [CLAUDE.md:34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L34) |
| One command is the only way to change the schema | No hand edits | [CLAUDE.md:41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L41) |
| The rebuild command refuses to touch the real database | Protects against a typo | [CLAUDE.md:41](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L41) |
| Every command checks the database matches the code | Catches a drifted schema before work is lost | [docs/architecture.md:11](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L11) |
| Work log entries stand free of the jobs they describe | A deleted job cannot erase a filing | [prisma/schema.prisma:652](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L652) |

What is missing, as far as the code and docs show: a scheduled backup of the live file, and any copy kept off the machine. This is an inference from the absence of such a step in the commands list ([CLAUDE.md:22](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L22)). If the laptop's disk fails, the work log history goes with it. Because the work log is a legal record, this is the single most important gap.

### R3. The legal work log

The Texas Workforce Commission counts three activities: applied, phone screen, and interview ([lib/utils/job-status.ts:49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L49)). Moving a job to one of those statuses writes an entry with the Commission's own wording ([lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts:19](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/work-log-activity.ts#L19)). The code comments call it "a legal filing that cannot be regenerated once the week it belongs to has passed" ([lib/utils/job-status.ts:55](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L55)).

Design choices that protect it:

| Choice | Why it matters | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The entry copies the employer name and job title | A later change to the job cannot alter what was filed. | [prisma/schema.prisma:665](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L665) |
| No update path exists for an entry | An entry cannot be rewritten by accident. | [prisma/schema.prisma:656](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L656) |
| Statuses and entries are written before any lookup | A run cut short loses a lookup, never a filing. | [docs/architecture.md:147](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L147) |
| The lists of statuses live in one file | A typo cannot silently stop entries being written. | [lib/utils/job-status.ts:44](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/job-status.ts#L44) |
| A job with no employer name stops and asks | A filing with a blank employer is worthless. | [docs/architecture.md:49](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L49) |
| Doubtful contact details are flagged | The person checks them before filing. | [prisma/schema.prisma:200](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L200) |

The remaining exposure is that the person is responsible for what is filed. The tool prepares entries. It does not submit anything to the state, as far as the code shows. Contact details come from a search and are best-effort. Anyone adopting this for their own claim should treat the work log as a draft record, and should check the rules of their own state, because the wording and the three activity types are specific to Texas.

### R4 to R10 in brief

| Risk | Evidence | Reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keyed service changes | Missing keys return a plain message and the run continues. [lib/collectors/jsearch.ts:116](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/jsearch.ts#L116) | A lost key costs one source, not the run. |
| Map service throttling | A refusal stores nothing and is never retried in the same run. [lib/tools/geocoder.ts:5](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L5) | Jobs wait for the next run. |
| Agent quality | A guessed score is awarded a 3 by rule and marked as a guess. [prisma/schema.prisma:177](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L177) | The guess is visible and expires sooner. |
| Claude Code dependence | The skill files say the pipeline command "runs the whole pipeline" on its own. [.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:13](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L13) | Collection works without an agent. Scoring does not. |
| Data leak | The ignore list names databases, secrets, resumes, and planning files. [.gitignore:2](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.gitignore#L2) | Strong, but manual. |
| Site terms | Requests identify as a browser. [lib/tools/page-fetcher.ts:10](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/page-fetcher.ts#L10) | The author has not found a terms review in the repository. For personal use at low volume the exposure is small, but it is not zero. |
| Abandonment | Everything runs locally. | No cost when idle. |

### Risk heat map

```mermaid
quadrantChart
    title Risk likelihood and impact
    x-axis Low likelihood --> High likelihood
    y-axis Low impact --> High impact
    quadrant-1 Act now
    quadrant-2 Prepare
    quadrant-3 Accept
    quadrant-4 Watch
    Site blocking: [0.85, 0.50]
    Lost database file: [0.20, 0.95]
    Work log error: [0.25, 0.80]
    Service price change: [0.50, 0.20]
    Map service outage: [0.50, 0.45]
    Weak agent scores: [0.50, 0.50]
    Claude Code dependence: [0.50, 0.75]
    Data leak: [0.20, 0.80]
    Terms of use: [0.50, 0.50]
```

<!-- Sources: .gitignore:12-22, lib/tools/page-fetcher.ts:8-11, lib/tools/resolution-browser.ts:19-23, lib/tools/geocoder.ts:5-9, docs/architecture.md:17-19 -->

## 7. Cost and Scaling Model

Costs are small and mostly pay-per-use. Exact prices are not in the repository, so this section gives the shape of each cost and says where the number would have to come from. Where a limit comes from code, it is cited. Where it comes from the outside vendor, the guide says so.

### Services and who pays

| Service | Used for | How it is paid | Limit visible in code | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Adzuna job API | Collecting jobs | Free key from the vendor. Terms are the vendor's. | Up to 50 results per search, one page, with a warning when more matched. | [lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:152](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/adzuna.ts#L152) |
| JSearch via RapidAPI | Collecting jobs | A RapidAPI subscription. Plan size is the vendor's. | Always two searches per run, three pages each, jobs from the past week. | [lib/collectors/jsearch.ts:131](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/jsearch.ts#L131) |
| Geocode.maps.co | Turning place names into coordinates | A free tier, one request per second, per the template note. | One lookup every 1.1 seconds, held by the tool itself. | [lib/tools/geocoder.ts:16](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L16) |
| Apify search actor | Finding an employer's address, phone and website | Pay per use on the person's Apify account. | One search per employer, 60 second limit, one employer is never searched twice once filled in. | [lib/tools/company-search.ts:30](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/company-search.ts#L30) |
| Public job boards and hiring sites | Collecting and reading postings | Free. Subject to each site's terms. | A 15 second timeout per request. | [lib/utils/fetch-utils.ts:1](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/utils/fetch-utils.ts#L1) |
| Claude Code | Running skills, scoring jobs, researching employers, resumes | The person's Claude subscription or usage | One helper per employer. Ten jobs per helper. | [.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:42](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L42) |

### What drives cost

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Search terms<br>and location"] --> B["Number of searches<br>per job API"]
    C["Watched employers<br>grow with good scores"] --> D["More board polls<br>no vendor fee"]
    E["New jobs per search"] --> F["Link visits<br>time, not money"]
    E --> G["Map lookups<br>only for new places"]
    E --> H["Agent scoring<br>Claude usage"]
    I["Jobs moved to<br>applied or screening"] --> J["One paid contact<br>search per new employer"]
    classDef box fill:#2d333b,stroke:#6d5dfc,color:#e6edf3
    class A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,I,J box
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e
```

<!-- Sources: lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:141-180, lib/collectors/jsearch.ts:131-153, lib/tools/geocoder.ts:16, docs/architecture.md:35, docs/architecture.md:51, .claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:42-71 -->

### Cost drivers in plain terms

| Driver | Behaviour | Scales with | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Adzuna calls | Two searches for each search term: one nationwide for remote work, one near the person. | Number of search terms times two | [lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:141](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/adzuna.ts#L141) |
| JSearch calls | All search terms are joined into one query, so the count stays at two searches. | Fixed per run | [lib/collectors/jsearch.ts:127](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/jsearch.ts#L127) |
| Map lookups | A place is looked up once and stored. In the builder's data, 3,975 lookups resolved to 789 distinct places. | New places only | [docs/architecture.md:35](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L35) |
| Contact searches | Run when a job reaches a status that files a log entry, and never repeated for a completed employer. | New employers the person engages with | [docs/architecture.md:51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L51) |
| Agent work | One helper per employer, plus one helper per ten jobs that carry a description. Jobs with no description get a helper each. | Unscored backlog size | [.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md:69](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/score-backlog/SKILL.md#L69) |
| Employer scores age out | A researched score expires after a number of days. A guessed one expires sooner. | Time, so research repeats | [prisma/schema.prisma:349](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L349) |

The Adzuna count of calls per search term is read directly from the loop in the collector. The guide does not state a dollar figure because no price is in the repository.

Two cost controls are worth naming. First, a minimum pay floor is asked of Adzuna in the request, so its one page is not spent on jobs that would be dropped ([lib/collectors/adzuna.ts:12](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/adzuna.ts#L12)). Second, an expired job stops before any paid map request is spent on it ([docs/architecture.md:29](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L29)).

### Scaling limits and when to invest

| Dimension | Today | First limit | Trigger for investment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Users | One | The personal profile, personal settings, and one database file are all single-person. | A second person wants to use it. |
| Jobs stored | Hundreds to low thousands, inferred from the trace counts in the docs | SQLite handles far more. | Not near a limit. |
| Sources | 14 | Each new site adds one collector, one reader, and a registry entry plus a seed run. | A source is missing that matters. |
| Run time | Minutes. The browser holds the screen. | Link visits are paced per site. | Searches start to feel too slow. |
| Job API depth | One page from Adzuna, three pages from JSearch | Postings beyond the page are not seen. | The warning about unseen postings becomes common. |
| Machine | A laptop | A visible browser needs a screen. | Wanting unattended runs. |

The last row matters most for the future. A scheduled, unattended run is blocked by two facts: the browser must be visible, and scoring needs an agent in the loop. Both are design choices rather than defects, but together they set the ceiling on automation.

| Hiring site boards | Public website | A site that sends a broken reply is skipped and named in warnings. | Other boards and aggregators | [docs/CHANGELOG.md:43](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md#L43) |
| Design job boards | Public website | Fewer design-specific jobs. | Aggregators | [lib/collectors/dribbble.ts:18](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/collectors/dribbble.ts#L18) |
| Geocode.maps.co | Service | Jobs cannot be judged on distance. They stay in the backlog, marked unjudged. | Retry next run | [lib/tools/geocoder.ts:127](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/geocoder.ts#L127) |
| Apify search actor | Service | Contact details are not filled in. The work log entry itself is still written. | The person fills them in by hand | [docs/architecture.md:51](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L51) |
| Claude Code | Platform | No scoring, no skills. Plain commands still collect and show jobs. | None for scoring | [.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:46](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L46) |
| Browser engine | Library | Link following stops. | Pages that need no browser still read | [lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts:14](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/rendered-page-fetcher.ts#L14) |
| Portfolio project | Separate project on the same machine | Tailored resumes cannot be made. | Write the resume by hand | [.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md:102](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/generate-resume/SKILL.md#L102) |
| SQLite file | Local file | Everything is lost without a copy. | A dated backup before schema changes | [CLAUDE.md:34](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L34) |

The resume dependency deserves a flag for anyone adopting the tool. The resume skill reads a separate project at a fixed place under the user's projects folder. A new owner would need that project too, or would have to rewrite the resume step.

## 9. Key Metrics and Observability

The tool does not have dashboards for operations or alerts. It has something more useful for a personal tool: a record of every job's path through the pipeline, which can answer questions after the fact.

| Metric or signal | What it answers | Where it comes from | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Run summary | How many jobs each step handled, per source and per reason | Read back from the trace rows after each run | [docs/architecture.md:57](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L57) |
| Errors and warnings list | Which source failed or degraded | Printed first in every run's output | [.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:29](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L29) |
| Job trace | What happened to every job, and why it was dropped | One row per event | [prisma/schema.prisma:618](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/prisma/schema.prisma#L618) |
| Unjudged marker | Which jobs could not be fully checked | Shown in the dashboard | [docs/CHANGELOG.md:59](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md#L59) |
| Source yield | Which sources produce jobs the person applies to | Answerable from the trace | [docs/CHANGELOG.md:71](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md#L71) |
| Exit status | Whether a run stopped early | Non-zero exit | [.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md:58](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/.claude/skills/job-search/SKILL.md#L58) |

There are no target values, because no service level is defined. The table below proposes what would be useful targets. These are suggestions from the author of this guide, not existing commitments.

| Proposed target | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Zero work log entries lost | It is a legal record. |
| A copy of the database less than a week old, off the machine | Closes the biggest gap. |
| Fewer than a set share of jobs left unjudged after a run | Shows source health. |
| Share of applications that came from each source | Tells where to invest in collectors. |

The dashboard is deliberately read-only and records nothing about being viewed, so glances at the backlog never distort the counts ([docs/architecture.md:65](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L65)). It listens only on the local machine at a default port ([scripts/serve.ts:20](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/scripts/serve.ts#L20), [lib/tools/web-server.ts:132](https://github.com/mablahblah/job-assistant/blob/main/lib/tools/web-server.ts#L132)). The address printed is a localhost address. Whether the server is reachable from other machines on a network depends on how the port is bound, which this guide did not verify.
